projects.features: ["added machines you can combine freely in the browser builder", "the builder checks that the chosen mods fit together", "added machines: SOLID, CHIPS, MAXSAW (seven saws), TERRA (wave terrain), VOSIM (formant pulses)", "CHORD+: the CHORD machine plays your own wavetables, and chords of a key with one finger on the TRIG keys", "Track FX controllable by MIDI CC 74/71/75/76", "SAMPLE: hear a +Drive sample from the browser on the pad or TRIG keys before loading it", "Perform Kit: keep the track sounds, levels and effects across pattern changes"]
projects.notes: Repo was offline 2026-11-07 to 11-09 (check_updates 2026-11-08); public again on 2026-11-09 (altstrument and SPOKES change reports; README read 2026-11-10). Beta fork of Modded Cycles 1.55 with a short mod list in the browser picker. Licence: MIT; distribution: browser-installer. Listed by altstrument. 2026-11-02: a web Manager keeps one Model:Cycles project per firmware: it backs up the current project, flashes the other firmware over USB and restores that firmware's project (notes/77). 2026-11-15 (README, notes/81): Perform Kit (SETTINGS + PATTERN) keeps the six track sounds, levels and delay/reverb values across pattern changes, after the Digitakt II's PERFORM KIT mode; nothing is kept unless the pattern is saved. The README no longer offers the web Manager: it advises one project per set of machine cards, since a project belongs to the firmware it was made on (on the official OS a project that names an added machine can freeze the MACHINES page). 2026-11-16 (README 0.68, notes/83, notes/60): CHIPS is model27's own fixed-point rewrite of Plaits' chiptune oscillators (MIT); Plaits' trigger arpeggio is replaced by an arpeggio inside each note. A CHIPS square costs about a third of TONE's instructions a block. One-Shot is pinned at v0.18. A note and its immediate note-off in one batch left previews held with GATE on (I113). 2026-11-17 (README 0.69, notes/84, REGISTRY, PROVENANCE): MAXSAW is model27's own code (MIT) built from the numbers and formulas in Adam Szabo's KTH 2010 thesis, no code taken; the Syntakt's SY SWARM uses the same detune curve. MAXSAW costs about half of TONE's instructions a block (Sub off). The web Manager is linked from the site again. SAMPLE stays at One-Shot 0.18. 2026-11-18 (README 0.72, notes/85, notes/57 section 7, BUILD.md, REGISTRY, PROVENANCE): TERRA is model27's fixed-point rewrite of Plaits' wave terrain engine (MIT); Plaits' wavetable data (about 50 KB) are copied unchanged. To fit them the builder learnt "far tables": large read-only tables placed in the variables' room above the code window. Six TERRA tracks showed CPU 67 %, peak 80 % on a unit; TERRA 0.2 stops clicks at trigs through the stock VCA (I144). The flasher now asks which device you own; the Samples OS tab and flasher/?samples are gone. The flasher refuses an OS file with more than 16,270 SysEx packets. 2026-11-19 (README, CHANGELOG, MAKING-MODS, notes/86, 63, 57, 37): release 0.75 adds VOSIM (Braids' integer steps kept, MIT) with SWEEP formant tracking and a CONTOUR window; the dispatcher tables now hold eight machines, so all six added machines and CHORD Tables can be ticked together, and a full build ran on a unit. The normal return from the Cycles OS to the Samples OS worked on a real Model:Samples (2026-11-18). A tester's Model:Samples stalled at 0-1 % on the first USB send with every flasher of this protocol, the second always worked; 0.73 resends once (I156). Packaging rules moved to MAKING-MODS.md; CHANGELOG.md is new. 2026-11-20 (notes/87, CHANGELOG, README 0.76, BUILD.md, REGISTRY, PROVENANCE): release 0.76 renames CHORD Tables to CHORD+ and adds Chord Joy, model27's own code (the idea from Chord Keys, none of its code): MACHINES + PUNCH turns it on per sound; TRIG 1-7 play the degrees of a major key, each with its chord on SHAPE, TRIG 8 the root an octave up; TRIG 9-16 with a degree held change the chord's colour until released; with REC + PLAY the chords are recorded with a SHAPE lock. It sits in CHORD Tables' package because two packages that extend the same stock machine cannot be composed. The first unit test heard each new chord start on the old one and slide over; the cause was the OS's per-block parameter smoothing, and the fixed build passed on a Model:Cycles the same day.

projects.notes: Modular Octatrack OS 1.40C "remixer": bus and track effects, FM synth machine, 255 kits, USB audio/MIDI, stock bug fixes. Base of Modwerk. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument; README, CHANGELOG and contributing docs read 2026-11-10. 2026-11-03: new midi-follow module (docs/site/usage/midi-follow.md, a test remix); not read further. 2026-11-10: WAVE (wavecf) is a 4-voice wavetable machine on the ColdFire, reduced from CHOMPI WAVE, heard on an MKII in builds W1-W6 (I58); XF CURVE offers 13 crossfader curves, run on a contributor's MKII on 2026-11-06; KEYBUS publishes each track's block peak for side-chain keys (make check only); a demand-loader soak with STEM REC froze an MKII (I57, open). 2026-11-12/13: new FRAME GUARD module holds a late frame interrupt out of a window in which the DSP's frame exchange stalls at START or a program change (I82); with it 32 first STARTs and 192 program changes ran clean on an MKII with a 20-channel USB capture. MIDI SCENES: CLEAR, COPY and PASTE SCENE act on the MIDI and audio locks together in either track mode, and a scene held across the MIDI key shows its locks as a fresh press does. 2026-11-15 (FAILURE_MODES, TRAPS, CHIP, MODULES): a program change to a demand effect that was not loaded stopped the audio in about two runs of three on an MKII while panel and USB still answered (I108); moving the loader's copy from the head to the end of DSP core B's frame cured it in 12 of 12 runs. A new gate lets a DSP instruction form ship only with a stock site, a register row or a module proven on a unit; a tool lists modules changed since their unit proof. 2026-11-16 (unreleased, 2026-11-14/16): REMOTE, an event ring a host reads over USB with PEEK and four commands; SCOPE and TUNER share the TEMPO key in the octabam remix; DRUMMER's KIT BALANCE takes step and scene locks; a LIM stereo peak limiter after MIX on RESONATOR and SHATTER; MIDI SCENES sends the Part's value when no scene locks a CC; SCALES keeps one audio scale per bank and Part; a ColdFire instruction-form check reports forms but refuses none yet. 2026-11-17 (CONTRIBUTING, remixes, TESTING): contributors' own remixes now live in remixes/community/<name>/ and may not use the octabam name; cxosc-core moved there. One module per pull request. CI runs one unit per gate job and skips units whose gates already passed for the same image. 2026-11-18 (CHANGELOG, TRAPS, firmware docs, module READMEs): PATTERN MUTE's per-pattern layer had been stored in byte 40 of each audio track record, which is the low byte of the one-shot trig mask; on an MKI a one-shot on step 1 or 2 read as a mute and an unmute deleted it (I146). The layer now lives in its own pmute.work side file and a 48-byte battery copy, and the double-FUNC switch ignores FUNC chords. DIRECT_JUMP_KYOTI V7.3 is pinned. New stock reading: SAVE PROJECT's job path, the PART window and its edit menu, the key-layer list per window, and the stock WAV header's RIFF size 8 bytes over the specification. 2026-11-19 (README, modules lazy-chop, src3-key, zoom-keep, CYCLE_SCAN, COSTS, CHIP, TRAPS): three audio-editor modules by a contributor, all on main and unreleased: LAZY CHOP slices a playing sample by tapping TRIG 1-16 (four pages, up to 64 slices, STUDIO and LIVE CHOP, ZERO SNAP, undo), SRC3 KEY starts and stops an SRC3-only recording with [MIDI] in the audio editor (MKI only), ZOOM KEEP keeps the editor's zoom per page; all three ran on the contributor's MKI (2026-11-10..14) with no issues found, ZOOM KEEP's across-tracks part in the emulator only. A new tool prices every module and stock effect from the DSP56300 manual's cycle table; against the unit's LOAD METER it reads about 3 % high on average (38 settings, 22 effects). 2026-11-20 (README, five new module READMEs and usage pages, FAILURE_MODES, HARDWARE_TESTING, TRAPS, DSP module READMEs): five new contributed modules, unreleased. From Hteah's ot-mods (entry ot-mods-hteah), ported by a contributor: PAGE LOOP (GRID REC: PAGE + trig 1-4 loops that page of the current track, in time), TRIG MUTE (hold a step + FUNC; the mute is kept as the trig's condition + 65, so stock plays such a trig and shows ERR) and TRACK TRIG MODE (CHROMATIC / SLOTS / SLICES per audio track, saved as a comment line stock skips); the readmes report each on an MKI in the author's ACCLOOP images since 2026-10-25/28, the octabam table grades them emulator only. By the LAZY CHOP contributor: LOCK EDIT ([TRIG] + [BANK] in grid recording opens the audio editor on the step's sample and slice; on an MKI 2026-11-14) and LAZY CHOP TEMPO (a BPM popup from the chop spacing; a personal build on an MKI read a 73.5 BPM take within 1 %, 78 % of 27 known-tempo takes within about 1 BPM offline; the final build not yet on a unit). Ten DSP effects got bit-identical speed passes (modelled, not measured on a unit; STUTTR no longer writes an M register inside its sample loop). New unit reports on an MKII (BUILD 05): the remote-commanded REMIX SWITCH boot hang is now seen three times (I110); a project reload after a demand-loader phase left the DSP frame count stopped three times; DARK REV picked on all eight tracks while MODULATION was loaded stopped the DSP in 6 of 9 replays. A host tool now loads projects and switches images over USB. 2026-11-22 (README, DSP_AUDIT (new), CYCLE_SCAN, FAILURE_MODES, TRAPS, module READMEs, remixes): no new release. A DSP audit register lists 34 techniques that make effect code shorter or cheaper with bit-identical output, applied to most DSP effects (MINIVERB's modelled cost 13.4 to 11.2 % of a frame, VERBERATION's 10.1 to 8.7 %); modelled only, not measured on a unit. The DARK REV stall (I170) was narrowed on an MKII: it needs MODULATION loaded when DARK REV starts on many tracks; a stock-effects image without the demand loader did not stall in 60 starts. Two diagnostic builds had placed SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR's stubs inside the window DARK REV writes (I188), so their results were discarded and the build now refuses such placements. Commanded REMIX SWITCH boots (I110) failed mostly while the DSP was stalled. New author reports on units: BATCH_BUGFIXES lights [BANK] for banks with trigless locks and ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS works on MIDI tracks (MKI, KYOTI release candidate), CX OSC's INDX changes the saw and triangle carriers, VOID's NBR follows the KEYBUS level (MKII). 2026-11-23 (CHANGELOG, tag v0.5, README, modules/README, fet76, vca160, keybus and morph READMEs, GLOSSARY, remix pages, FAILURE_MODES): v0.5 is the web builder's version, with three remixes. Its release check on the author's MKII left 3 of 32 program changes unapplied on octabam (INEW1); it ships with the DARK REV stall as a known fault, which octabam-verbs (no stock DARK REV) and octabam-bus (no demand loader) avoid by design but were not run against. A contributor's FET76 and VCA160 arrived after the tag; VCA160's KEY now reads a mean-square word that KEYBUS publishes for every track, so it no longer needs a hook of its own. MORPH v1.2 adds a way back (RET, CURV, END), simulator only. Most of the diff moves or shortens docs. 2026-11-24 (CHANGELOG, module READMEs, untagged): TEMPO BUS takes scene locks on the bus delay and reverb knobs; SCENES P2 also locks from scene B; COPY PROJECT makes stock SAVE TO NEW carry the sidecar files except .strd (I202); KITS now needs BATCH_BUGFIXES; WAVE ends every note on STOP; SHATTER gets DRV and FOLD gain compensation; THIRD_PARTY.md credits PAGE LOOP, TRACK TRIG MODE and TRIG MUTE as MIT code from Hteah/ot-mods. TRIG MUTE's docs now say stock turns a muted trig into an unmuted 8:8 trig on project load.

Digitakt-style with ringing tails", "direct pattern jump, locked to the clock, trig conditions kept", "CLYPS: launch any pattern's track sequence onto one track, alone or with its sound, Ableton-style", "reload a track, its sound or a pattern from the project on the card", "BLACKPYRAMIDS_303: a TB-303 voice as a track machine on the DSP, one per core", "sidechain compressor with key listen; varispeed and repitch", "three stock bug fixes in every image"]
projects.notes: Feature and fix builds keeping the stock feel: mute modes, pattern jump, sidechain compressor, varispeed, repitch. Tested on an MKI. Licence: MIT; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument. 2026-11-02: MUTE_MODES KEYHOLD fixes octabam#934: with SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR a muted track that had been the KEY played again once KEY moved away; held tracks now keep the post-FX cut until unmuted. Confirmed on an Octatrack MKI. 2026-11-09: RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT reloads one track's slice of the Part from the card ([BANK] + [TRACK n]) or a whole pattern ([PTN] + [BANK] + trig), landing on the next step while playing; a click from a copy with interrupts masked was fixed on the unit (I60); the REC_TRIG_MUTE fix was confirmed on hardware. 2026-11-10: octabam's HOOKS chain lets RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT and FREE LOOP share their UI-tick site in one image (emulator-checked, not flashed). 2026-11-13 (NOTES.md): BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 is being rebuilt as one packaged DSP engine for the Modwerk base (not flashed); its host check is bit-exact against the emulator twin. 2026-11-14 (README, NOTES, module README): RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT takes over the landing rules of the author's Clyps work: a reloaded track lands one tick before the step boundary, so it is never a step late; a FULL reload's sound settings change only with the first trig that sounds, never on a ringing sample; trig conditions (1:2, PRE, FILL, also after STOP and PLAY) carry on as if the saved sequence had always played. A twelfth hook at the stock trig-condition reset does this. The standalone image passed every walk-through item on the author's MKI the same day; not yet run in an octabam-built image. 2026-11-17 (README, NOTES, FLASHING, Clyps manual and scope): new CLYPS, a clip launcher after Ableton's Session view: [PTN] + [BANK] shows the active track's sequence in all 16 patterns of a bank; a trig loads one onto the track (with its sound when [FUNC] is held) while the others play on; originals, per-track temp saves and card reloads put things back. It keeps ~10 MB of sample memory and always ships with DIRECT JUMP, never beside RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT. KYOTI V1.8 (RELOAD + DIRECT JUMP) and V1.8C (CLYPS) replace V1.7; every image now carries the three bug fixes. DIRECT JUMP V7.2.2 releases tracks that SILENCE TRACKS mutes just before a jump, curing a pop on the unit (an earlier fix inferred in the emulator did not); V7.3 counts a jump's position and trig conditions from the last normal pattern change, confirmed by ear in V1.8C on 2026-11-16. 2026-11-17 (Clyps manual): a card reload of another pattern ([PTN] + [BANK] + trig) is cued by stock's CHAIN AFTER setting, or lands legato when DIRECT JUMP is on; Clyps' "x" marks only an edited sequence, never an edited Part. 2026-11-20 (README, NOTES, FLASHING, START_HERE, BUILD_KYOTI, blackpyramids-303 module README, BC handoff): new combined image KYOTI V1.8BC = V1.8C + BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 (the TB-303 voice); it gives up PLATE REV as well as SPRING REV (a project saved with either loads that FX2 as NONE) and keeps about 10 MB of sample memory. BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 now allows one voice per DSP core on every path: the machine list, TRACK PASTE, an SRC page paste and (in V1.8BC) Clyps loads refuse a second one with ONE 303 PER CORE!, and a UI-task check repairs any other way (a project saved with two keeps the lower track). Its SRC page now copies and pastes as a BLKPYRAMD; a muted BLKPYRAMD track starts no note in MUTE MODE DT-T. On a pattern or Part change the voice now carries over until the track's own first trig, ties hold across a pattern boundary, and the first note after a load gets its full GATE; before, the last step was lost, a pop could sound and the first note was a blip (found on the author's MKI in octabam test images, fixed). VARISPEED_EMUS VEM11 prices a Part switch as the overlap of old and new sounds: over the DSP budget it drops held notes to OT, then steps the new Part's engines down, and a held VARI note keeps its speed until its own next trig (it changed about 145 ms early before). Open: once, after pasting a BLKPYRAMD track into another Part's pattern, the sequencer did not advance on PLAY (not reproduced); loading a project with two voices on a core not tried on the unit. 2026-11-21 (NOTES, FLASHING, README, START_HERE, BUILD_KYOTI, octabam module READMEs): release candidates RC1-RC3 bundle three changes. VARISPEED now enters VARI at QUAN 1/1 unless the track left VARI with another QUAN, remembers that across a save and keeps a held VARI note's speed through a Part switch; its state moved out of the NEIGHBOR bytes it had shared with BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 into four Part bytes stock never edits, and older projects migrate on load. EMPTY_PATTERN_LED_FIX also lights [BANK] for trigless locks that carry a locked value (318 B, +0.3-0.5 % CPU with [BANK] held). ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS now covers MIDI tracks (I173). Two BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 bugs found on the MKI: a 303 chosen on a FLEX track was silent (I172, fixed in RC2) and a track leaving the 303 played a burst of its FLEX sample (I174, fixed in RC3, not flashed). On 2026-11-20 VARISPEED, VARISPEED_EMUS, ERASE, BATCH_BUGFIXES and the other feature images were promoted FINAL; KYOTI V1.8 / V1.8C / V1.8BC, BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 and CLYPS wait for RC3, and their builders refuse without the WIP opt-in until then. Pin pull requests for octabam's three modules are open (octabam#1200-1202).

projects.notes: Mod system for the Syntakt bringing Digitakt mk1 sample machines (ONE SHOT, WERP, REPITCH, SLICE), a per-project sample pool with long samples in slots 65-128 and a basic sample manager. Experimental. MIT. 18 stars at first sight. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-02; README start read. 2026-11-02: the GitHub repo no longer answers (deleted, renamed or private); details here are from the earlier read. 2026-11-03: the Lapin list links it as an external web app, https://synfact.app (builds custom Syntakt firmware from the user's stock OS file). 2026-11-03: the project moved to GSM1980/synfact-dev and was rebuilt on elekloader (GPL-2.0; the old release repo was MIT): a core (mods/core-st) with hook bus, UI and SETTINGS events, SMZ4 banks of machines and modules that can change without reinstalling, long-sample storage (HZFS) and a project sample pool. Mods: SP sample machines, SY FM DTONE, audio recorder, third LFO, arpeggiator, POLY, system info, sample manager. Builds change MAIN and a bounded part of AUDIO only; a recovery core that never loads the bank can replace a bank that stops the unit from starting. Also builds in the browser (synfact.app). A snapshot of the old release repo survives as nrdsrfr/synfact-release (2026-10-17). 2026-11-06: project lifecycle audit after a user report of slow project load and save; arp-st leaves default carriers absent (81 % fewer emulated instructions); RANDOMIZE pages documented. 2026-11-09: new docs SETUP, MACHINES (writing a machine), MACHINE-REFERENCE and SAFE-BOOT- SMZ4-07-16; a safe-boot trial crashed every boot until core 1.7.1 (I62); a companion window broke BASE/WDTH until 1.7.2 (I63). 2026-11-14: a MAIN-CPU optimisation release across core and optional mods (full bank 86 % -> 83 % MAIN on a stock pattern); a withdrawn development core of the same number crashed every boot because a routine sat in boot storage that startup wipes (I104); LFO3 1.3 fully suspends an engine with neutral depth or no valid destination, which can change active RANDOM sequences; samplers' stereo code borrows the Chorus SRAM windows when Chorus is absent. 2026-11-17: new playhead-st 1.0 (per-track step order, saved in a free tail of each kit slot that stock never reads); Chorus 1.2 (assembly, bit-identical buses); core 1.8.2 fixes a stock deferred view cleanup that drops a close raised during UI composition, which left ARP blank after mute on the owner's unit (ARP 1.9.1-1.10.4 reports); core 1.9.0 (host API 15) lets Recorder 1.4 run MAIN reduced (mixer, FX and modulation skipped) while a finished take is edited, and speeds MAIN LR stereo capture (owner's unit: 92 % MAIN in PLAY, 99 % recording before); new docs RECORDER-AUDIO-PAUSE and RECORDER-CAPTURE-CPU are in Spanish. 2026-11-18 (docs/OS142-PORT.md, STOCK-SAMPLE-CORE-OVERLAP.md, mod CHANGELOGs): source builds now target Syntakt OS 1.42 (core 2.0.0; all 108 resident patch sites re-audited; no single code offset between 1.41 and 1.42). Core 2.0 requires SMZ4 feature 16 and contract 0x53594605 and refuses older and untagged banks, so every bank must be rebuilt. Core 2.0.1 fixes a boot crash with many stock samples: stock's sample blob in MAIN grew over Synfact's resident core at 0x46000000 (I145); the core now streams stock samples to the voice CPU page by page and draws waveforms only when a page asks. The web builder and SMZ catalogue are not yet on 1.42. 2026-11-18, later (docs/INTEGRATING.md, SYNFACT-WEB.md, js/README.md): the documented web core route now takes Syntakt OS 1.42; the normal build has ten optional groups (Playhead added; ARP needs LFO3) plus the always-on modulation skip, 768 selections the matrix checks against the reference build. 2026-11-19 (MACHINE-REFERENCE, FORMAT, TESTS, ADAPTING, mod READMEs and CHANGELOGs): core 2.0.3 (chorus-st now needs it), arp-st 1.10.7, playhead-st 1.1-1.2.1 with four new modes and a modal selector drawn through the native Bitmap API; playhead now builds before the other UI modules so its modal takes keys first. The OS 1.42 suite checks 218 stock preimages. Synfact names firmware routines by their OS 1.41 address even in 1.42 modules; only the newly named 1.42 addresses are 1.42. All new work emulator only. 2026-11-20 (new docs AUDIO-MEMORY-MAP, LFO3-MODULE-ONLY-INVESTIGATION, PROJECT-OPERATIONS-CPU, STOCK-MAIN-CPU-PROFILE in Spanish; new mods icache-lock-st and mix-fast-st; high-memory probe; core-st README, SAMPLE-POOL, SMZ4, mod CHANGELOGs): core 2.1.0 stops the sequencer and runs MAIN's reduced audio path while a native project worker (new, save, load, rename, copy, paste, clear, delete) runs, without the recorder. 2.1.1 frees the bank file's AUDIO section from MAIN's heap after boot (it stayed until reboot: 108,640 bytes in the normal bank, 711,152 with the MD machine) and compiles cold core files at -Os, so the 64 KiB resident reserve goes from 176 to 11,616 bytes free. 2.1.2 fixes a module-only bank (LFO3, ARP, zero machines): the registry never became active, so LFO3's page showed ERR labels; confirmed on the owner's unit. 2.2.0 grows the bank's AUDIO section to 4 MiB and moves the sample pool above AUDIO's own page (63.62 MiB of long samples, 31.30 before); new contract 0x53594606, so every bank must be rebuilt. 2.3.0 checks that a whole sample batch fits before changing AUDIO (AUDIO FULL), and Sample Manager 1.3 shows sizes and a project memory meter. New always-in-bank modules: mix-fast-st (skips zero gain ramps in the stock mix kernels, exact) and icache-lock-st (locks hot stock audio code in half of MAIN's I-cache); both CPU savings are models, pending the unit. An emulator profile of stock 1.42 says about half of MAIN's cost is instruction-cache misses. A test-only probe machine (type 70) checks on the unit that nothing writes the new high AUDIO zone and measures the AUDIO stack depth; no result yet. 2026-11-21 (new comp-st README, FX-BUS-COMPRESSOR-FEASIBILITY in Spanish, REAL-SYSTEM-PROFILE; ADAPTING, FORMAT, MACHINE-REFERENCE, SMZ4, mod CHANGELOGs, commits of 2026-11-20): new comp-st 0.2.0, a compressor on the FX track bus only. Its DSP is SyntHack OS's master-comp (MIT, kept in upstream/); the controls come from the user's own Digitakt OS 1.54 file. Detector on the FX ADC pair, gain through the two FX VCAs, parallel MIX; settings in the kit slot tail [0x15d0, 0x15e0). Core 2.4.0 (host API 16) adds event 15 FX_CV and takes over the shared Kit sites from Chorus 1.2.2 and LFO3 1.3.2; older cores reject such a bank. The owner reports comp-st 0.2.0 working on the unit. An emulator profile of the full shipped bank found that the mods are not an I-cache miss source; the stock audio block is, so a better lock set cannot win much. 2026-11-23 (new COMP-SIDECHAIN-FILTER-FEASIBILITY in Spanish; comp-st, core-st and samplers-st READMEs, mod.json and CHANGELOGs; MACHINE-REFERENCE, ADAPTING, TESTS): comp-st 1.0.0 is COMP's first release: a high-pass on the detector only (SCF: off plus 127 cutoffs, 60 Hz to 1 kHz), ATK and REL in ms, THR 127 by default. On the unit MAIN rose with 0.2.0's COMP page open; the GR meter's repaints were the cause, now capped at 10 Hz (I196). Core 2.5.0 lets samplers-st 1.6.0 run a stereo track's right channel inside the stock chain; emulator only. 2026-11-24 (main 2026-11-23): core 2.6.1 raises the module limit to 32; two new machines, SY MnM (digimono-st 0.8.1, Monomachine-style types) and MD MACHINEDRUM (md-st 0.2, vendors soejrd/mdkit at 96157fe, CC0); a new offline tool tools/monomachine-reference compares the bank oscillators with the Monomachine's own DSP run through Monomodule on the user's OS 1.32B. FM+ table arrays taken from the Monomachine OS are committed at the owner's request (with a recipe and hashes); the DigiPRO tables are not. The web builder now takes several OS donors (Digitone 1.44, Digitakt 1.54, Monomachine 1.32B) and offers 13 optional groups. Unit CPU readings per machine and the AUDIO cost model are on the Syntakt page.

The 0.5.0 features are marked in testing on their pages. The voices clipped at the stock Rytm's track ceiling in 0.4.x and now play 9 dB lower. Do not combine with newer elekloader cores: they store their settings in the bytes Sidecar uses. 2026-11-18 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.1, docs): 0.5.1 updates only the Pi, from the web page (a .scu file, a trial boot, automatic return to 0.5.0 if it does not come back). MORPH, the looper, sidechain and a new WAVETABLE moved again, to 0.5.2. A catalog in the web page installs community user machines from a public registry (trigcondition/sidecar-machines): native code, no sandbox, not tested by Sidecar. A USB host that vanished mid-traffic on the Pi's USB-C port halted the Pi in 0.5.0; 0.5.1 recovers. 2026-11-22 (docs: troubleshooting, web UI, start here): the docs for the coming 0.5.2 add a Lag now button that writes a marker into the Sidecar's black box log when the Rytm feels slow while the Sidecar is attached, and a procedure for sending that log (about the last 1.5 to 3 hours, in two files under /.rytm). 0.5.1 is still the current release. 2026-11-23 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.1.1, INSTALL-PI, docs install-pi, patch-and-flash, start-here, upgrading, what-works-now): Sidecar 0.5.1.1 (2026-11-22) is a fixes release. The Pi update works alone, also with the Rytm on firmware 0.5.0; the optional Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1 (OS 1.74 only) stops stock Rytm samples playing under Sidecar machines (I195) and fixes the SMPL key. A 0.5.0 or 0.5.1 Pi cannot compare a four-part version, so the first update needs "Install it anyway". New: black box download with secrets masked, catalog audio previews, a Lag now marker. MORPH, the looper, sidechain and WAVETABLE stay in 0.5.2.

projects.name: C7
projects.author: sata1000000
projects.notes: Desktop app controlling the Machinedrum and Monomachine over SysEx/MIDI (kits, sounds, patterns, songs, samples) with a DAW bridge plug-in for automation. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: OctaLib
projects.author: snugsound
projects.notes: Librarian for Octatrack projects (bank swaps and more by rewriting the project files). Unlicense.

projects.name: ModuleDrum
projects.author: K-X420
projects.notes: Chip-level Machinedrum emulation as a DAW plug-in that runs the user's own OS and DSP programs, with the sequencer and a library. Fork of Monomodule and still builds the Monomodule plug-ins. AGPL-3.0.

projects.name: Machinemodule for MPC OS
projects.author: sd88me
projects.notes: The Machinedrum's own DSP code and machine/LFO/mixer maths as a VST2 for Akai MPC/Force standalone devices (all 16 tracks in one instance). The same author ports it to Ableton Move (Schwung) and ships Monomodule for MPC OS. User supplies the OS file. AGPL-3.0. 2026-11-18 (README): the installer is now the OpenMPC Plugin Manager; the Gen2 download needs the user's own Machinedrum OS 1.63 file added to the plugin folder after installing (the Gen 1 build-it-yourself zips put it in during the build).

projects.name: Monomodule for MPC OS
projects.author: sd88me
projects.notes: shnolk's Monomodule engine as VST2 plug-ins for Akai MPC and Force standalone devices: Monomodule One (15 synth machines) and Monomodule FX (7 effect machines). A static recompiler turns the DSP56300 code into ARM code so it runs in real time. Needs MPC OS 3.x for the touchscreen page. User supplies the Monomachine OS file; the Force build is built from it by the user.

projects.name: MachineModule (desktop)
projects.author: AcidReff
projects.notes: Windows/macOS standalone and VST3 port of sd88me's Machinedrum engine with a JUCE interface; 0.4.6 adds a native ARM JIT for voices and master effects. AGPL-3.0.

projects.name: Monomodule for Schwung
projects.author: legsmechanical
projects.notes: Port of Monomodule (chip-level Monomachine engine) to Ableton Move via Schwung, as one synth track plus the seven FX machines. GPL-3.0 per README (repo metadata says AGPL-3.0).

projects.name: mdkit
projects.author: soejrd
projects.notes: The Machinedrum's EFM, TRX and P-I voice families as standalone C99 for porting, with a web demo. Whether it was derived from the OS or modelled from recordings is not said in the README start. CC0 (LICENSE and NOTICE read 2026-11-11; the NOTICE adds that CC0 covers what the contributors can dedicate, not third-party names or materials).

projects.name: OP-XY MNMD
projects.author: mmockett
projects.version: v1.3.6 (tag, 2026-11-13): MD KIT builds into one firmware with Hexagon's Moth; v1.3.5: the synths play at one loudness, MD KIT raises its quieter machines by up to 6 dB
projects.notes: Machinedrum and Monomachine engines written from scratch (not an emulation of the chips) for the Teenage Engineering OP-XY on the Open-XY SDK. MIT. v1.3.2 (README 2026-11-12) gives each MD KIT key its own pan, level, filter, sample-rate reduction and FX sends with step locks (needs OP-XY SDK 1.10). v1.3.3/v1.3.4 (README 2026-11-13) adds a second kit, MD E12, plays the Machinedrum's sixteen E12 machines from samples the user captures from their own ROM (silent without them); both kits target SDK 1.15 for their Shift mixer.

projects.name: BSP Machinedrum
projects.author: ABarracu87
projects.notes: Uses an Arturia BeatStep Pro as a front panel for the Gearmulator Machinedrum/Monomachine plug-ins, talking to the plug-ins through their MCP servers. MIT.

projects.name: Analog Rytm MK1 OS 1.74 mods
projects.author: hugz202
projects.tested_note: README: the full image flashed and played on a Rytm MK1, OS 1.73; the 1.74 build not flashed yet (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["seven Machinedrum TX-8 and TX-9 ports as new machines", "a chorus as a third send effect", "DUCK: sidechain-style pumping from one track", "CPU probe build with live load readouts"]
projects.notes: Sister project of the A4 MK1 mods (same registry/verify method). Adds Machinedrum TX-8/TX-9 ports as new machines, a chorus as a third send, a sidechain-style duck at the voices' analog VCAs, and a CPU-load probe build. Has hazards and flashing docs. MIT.

projects.name: rytm-mods boot report
projects.author: Iced-Cream
projects.notes: Evidence for Modwerk's add-a-machine steps on the Rytm MKII - the stock file rebuilt byte for byte, a modified OS booted on a unit and recovered with stock, and elekloader's core-ar2 with every shared event observed on a unit. Hashes, addresses and photos only. GPL-2.0.

projects.name: TrackPatterns
projects.author: pgstath
projects.features: ["each of the 16 tracks plays its own pattern of the playing bank", "a track changes pattern at its own loop end (clip-style)"]
projects.notes: Each of the 16 tracks can play its own pattern of the playing bank and switch at its own loop end (a clip-style workflow). Checked in the ColdFire emulator and on the contributor's MKII; also submitted to octabam (PR 846). MIT.

projects.name: OType
projects.author: nordseele
projects.tested_note: README: developed on an Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C; not tested on the MKII (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["scripting language: scripts on the card run on the machine", "reach trigs, locks, pages, parts, scenes, tempo, patterns and banks", "load and free machines and sample slots", "save the current take as a WAV and load audio files", "live scripts on clock, note, CC and trig events"]
projects.notes: A line-oriented scripting language for the Octatrack - scripts on the card reach (almost) every editable parameter and audio files and are called on the machine. Command reference in a separate docs repo. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: octalab
projects.author: nordseele
projects.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (text, docs, images; versions before 2026-09-27 MIT)
projects.features: ["randomisation in one gesture (sample pool, LFOs, effects, scenes, locks)", "GROOVE with a groove pool; Euclidean and Grids generators", "CAPTURE: an instant sampler on the trig keys", "TAPE: record the master straight to the CF card while playing"]
projects.notes: An Octatrack firmware workshop built on octabam, tested on an MKI. The README documents what was tried in September 2026: one-gesture randomisation, GROOVE and a groove pool, generators (Euclidean, Grids), CAPTURE (an instant sampler on the trig keys) and TAPE / Direct to CF (recording to the card while the machine plays). Publishes no firmware, builds or source code. The work continues in OType and ot1; some features may come as octabam modules.

projects.name: OctaDraw
projects.author: nordseele
projects.notes: Browser pixel editor for the Octatrack's 128x64 screen that exports ColdFire assembly drawing the same pixels, plus PNG previews and a JSON description for wiring into a firmware module. A developer tool for UI mods. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: octa-bt-pt
projects.author: bryantysinger
projects.tested_note: README: nothing is exposed as a labelled control unless its behaviour was checked against a real unit (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["web tool that writes parameter values into your own OS 1.40C file", "effect defaults and FX1/FX2 default assignment", "AMF multiply fix", "each patch checked against the stock file's hash"]
projects.notes: Web UI that patches parameter values (effect defaults, FX1/FX2 default assignment, an AMF multiply fix) into the user's own 1.40C file - values, not code, listed in a registry. macOS build tooling. MIT.

projects.name: aCiDtRacK modules
projects.author: braikomarko-hub
projects.tested_note: README: tested on one Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, hours of playing (Oct 2026) (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["octa303: a circuit-modelled TB-303 voice per track", "devilish: Devil Fish mods for the 303 voice", "distorx: distortion insert", "db666: compressor insert with side-chain"]
projects.notes: octabam modules - a circuit-modelled TB-303 voice per track on the ColdFire (calibrated against recordings), Devil Fish mods, an SD-1/RAT-style distortion and a dbx-160-style compressor. The README marks what is proven. MIT.

projects.name: Machinedrum USR machines (RASP, KOOK, SMSH...)
projects.author: SamplesAndSnacks
projects.features: ["three USR machines: RASP (blown trill), KOOK (kookaburra), SMSH (smashed piano)", "no sample banks needed"]
projects.notes: Custom USR machines, each a single SysEx file sent to MDX's machine manager. MIT.

projects.name: Monomachine Lab
projects.author: Jick238
projects.notes: AU/VST3 that runs one Monomachine DSP track's original DSP56300 code (15 synth and 7 FX machine dispatches, the per-track chain, kit SysEx import). Independent of Monomodule, which it points to for a fuller emulation.

projects.name: Maschine MD-MM
projects.author: sid366
projects.notes: Fork of gearmulator-md-mm with Native Instruments Maschine MK3 integration. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: MDDT (Machinedrum Data Tool)
projects.author: waftlord
projects.notes: Browser tool (WebMIDI) for Machinedrum MK1/MK2/UW data over SysEx. Apache-2.0.

projects.name: Tributary
projects.author: stampman3000-jpg
projects.version: v1.2.6 (tag, 2026-11-20: README donation link and developer name only, no functional change). v1.2.5 (tag, 2026-11-14): the chosen output switches and level survive a meter redraw and are stored with the MPC project. v1.2.4 (2026-11-13): the plugin holds about 11 ms of Digitone II audio (enough for the MPC's 256-sample block); Capture waits 470 samples after the bar
projects.notes: An Overwitch rework that plays Overbridge USB audio on Akai MPC standalone tracks; heard on a Digitone II, holding ~4 ms behind the newest USB sample. Shows Overbridge streaming works outside a desktop host. GPL-3.0. 2026-11-12 (CAPTURE.md) - a Capture tab records the machine's own 48 kHz samples for 1-16 bars, locked to the MPC's bar and shifted by the 162-sample monitoring delay, into a 24-bit wav; host tests only, not yet on an MPC. 2026-11-22 (README): a badge and a screenshot only; nothing new.

projects.name: TurboMIDI (C++)
projects.author: DatanoiseTV
projects.notes: Header-only C++ implementation of Elektron's TurboMIDI speed negotiation (up to 20x DIN MIDI speed). Since 2026-11-04 the repo no longer answers anonymously (git asks for credentials, so private or removed); still gone on 2026-11-11, so it is no longer polled.

projects.name: rytm-rs / rytm-sys
projects.author: alisomay
projects.notes: Rust abstractions over the Rytm's undocumented SysEx (bindings to a fork of bsp2's libanalogrytm). MIT.

projects.name: Analog Four sound SysEx cheatsheet
projects.author: kimasendorf
projects.notes: Tables of the A4 sound SysEx bytes, from reverse engineering.

projects.name: ot-tools-io
projects.author: jhw
projects.notes: Rust crate for reading and writing the Octatrack's binary project/bank/marker files; the same author's octapy does it in Python. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: Model:Cycles .mcpst format notes
projects.author: kg4zow
projects.notes: Reverse-engineered layout of the Model:Cycles preset files (.mcpst) with dump/compare scripts.

projects.name: Plock (Rytm pattern editor)
projects.author: plentyofnames
projects.notes: Browser pattern editor for the Analog Rytm over Web MIDI: pulls the current pattern and kit by SysEx, edits trigs, parameter locks, retrigs, micro-timing and sound locks in a step grid and sends the result back; opens and saves .syx dumps and exports MIDI. The README credits earlier community work on the format. MIT per README (no licence file in the repo).

projects.name: Digitakt Pattern Editor (JUCE)
projects.author: mk3stn3r
projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI; offline sample playback over USB audio needs OS 1.20 or later
projects.notes: Native desktop app (C++/JUCE, built for Linux, CMake also for macOS/Windows): downloads a pattern or a whole project over USB MIDI, edits the step grid and sample locks, imports MIDI files, uploads samples to the +Drive and plays patterns offline through the computer. The README says the format layer is a C++ port of elk-herd rather than a wrapper, and that it writes lanes elk-herd only decodes. BSD-2-Clause (licence file carries elk-herd's copyright). Was in ignore.yml as an empty repo; re-reviewed 2026-11-03 after altstrument listed it.

projects.name: digitakt-reorder
projects.author: daguilarc
projects.notes: Python library and job template that reorders, drops and de-duplicates the sample pool of a Digitakt project dump and remaps every kit and sample-lock reference. Works on a .syx file fetched and sent with elk-herd; no MIDI code. MIT.

projects.name: ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)
projects.author: luizvarela
projects.notes: Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

projects.name: ElekPrep Transfer
projects.author: unknown
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

projects.name: Digitone 2 Pattern Manager
projects.author: morukutsu
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app: requests Pattern+Kit dumps from a Digitone II slot over Web MIDI, keeps them in a local library and sends them back to a chosen slot; also imports project capture .syx files and replays a captured project stream. Proprietary. Shows that DN2 pattern/kit dump requests per slot work over SysEx (claim, not checked by us).

projects.name: MachineDrandom
projects.author: Kerem Ergener (per altstrument)
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app that randomises the loaded Machinedrum kit live over Web MIDI, engine by engine and parameter by parameter, and can generate rhythm patterns played as MIDI notes. Nothing is stored until the kit is saved on the unit. Proprietary.

projects.name: Say A! (MCL chromatic A tool)
projects.author: BartBral
projects.notes: Browser sample prep and transfer tool for the Machinedrum UW: shifts each sample so its root lands on an A for MegaCommand's chromatic mode, resamples, processes loops, and sends over MIDI Sample Dump or saves WAV and .syx. Licence not stated. Repo clone timed out (large); details from altstrument.

projects.name: SM (Machinedrum sample manager)
projects.author: Fyris
projects.notes: Closed-source browser sample manager for the Machinedrum UW using MIDI Sample Dump Standard over Web MIDI: 48 slots with waveform view, WAV and .syx import/export, reverse, invert, loop and name controls. Proprietary.

projects.name: Model:Cycles Web Editor
projects.author: tkawamu0622-cmd
projects.notes: Browser piano-roll editor and sequencer for the Model:Cycles over Web MIDI: parameters as CC, pattern select by program change, and recording a sequence into the unit one track at a time by playing it in over MIDI clock (no pattern SysEx). Licence not stated. Repo clone failed (transfer error); details from altstrument.

projects.name: BIAS (six-oscillator percussion machine)
projects.author: 100demons
projects.features: ["BIAS machine: six oscillators with their own envelopes", "wavefolder and a second envelope after it", "clock locked to the note"]
projects.notes: Source package for a percussion machine with six oscillators, each with its own envelope, summed, wavefolded and given a second envelope, on a clock locked to the note; written clean-room after Noise Engineering's published description of the Basimilus Iteritas Alia (no NE code or tables per its notices). Fixed-point C for the ColdFire, a table generator, a host build and an emulator test on the OS's own voice loop. A machine package for model27, with a fixed-slot tweak for Modded Cycles 2.0; also on the Cycles Engines flasher. Played on a Model:Cycles 2026-11-03 in slot 11 (README): heavy on the processor, and it does not combine with five model27 Track FX packages (15 overlap problems). Commits a compiled object (bias.o). Found via altstrument 2026-11-04.

projects.name: CTRL+ / USER CFG (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: DigiAlchemydsp
projects.tested_note: shop: tested on hardware, stable
projects.features: ["the Digitone Keys' User Mode pages in the regular Digitone's TRIG rotation", "USER CFG page to assign the eight encoders", "assignments saved with the project"]
projects.notes: Adds the Digitone Keys' User Mode page (stock page 24) to the regular Digitone's TRIG page rotation, plus a USER CFG page that assigns the eight encoders; the assignment is saved with the project through core-dn1 project data. Testing status not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: CHOKE GROUPS (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 3.1 or later
projects.features: ["two choke groups, set per track", "a note fades out the other tracks of its group", "CHK knob on the second TRIG page, p-lockable"]
projects.notes: Two choke groups set per track from the Mod Menu and saved with the project: a note on a track fades out the voices of the group's other tracks over one 32-sample block (0.7 ms). Names no firmware address (uses ev_voice_on, ev_render_voices, fw_voice_track). Checked only in digiemu (11 voices choked, output RMS measured); not heard, not on a unit.

projects.name: PROGRAM CHANGE -> SOUND (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.features: ["a MIDI program change loads that pool sound onto the track", "PRG knob on the second TRIG page, p-lockable per trig"]
projects.notes: A program change on a track's channel loads that number's sound from the project's pool onto the track, as the SOUND BROWSER's FUNC + YES does (program 1 = pool sound 001). Checked only in digiemu, not on a unit.

projects.name: MIDI LOOPBACK (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.features: ["MIDI loopback: a MIDI track's messages go back into the unit as if from DIN", "MIDI tracks can sequence and p-lock the synth tracks or the master effects", "LOOP knob on the MIDI TRIG page and a LOOPBACK tile in the Mod Menu"]
projects.notes: An internal MIDI cable: what the MIDI tracks send on one chosen channel goes back into the unit as if from DIN, so a MIDI track sequences and p-locks a synth track or (on the FX channel) the master effects. Names no firmware address. Checked only in digiemu with its DIN output captured; the CC path only through core_midi_receive.

projects.name: SOLO & MUTE GROUPS (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.features: ["solo a track with PAGE + track key", "four mute groups to store and recall"]
projects.notes: Track key + FUNC solos a track among its four; four mute groups. Checked only in digiemu (with LOOPBACK and PC SOUND in the same build), not on a unit.

projects.name: ARP MENU (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.features: ["a long FUNC + KEYBOARD press opens the ARP menu", "a quick press still toggles the arpeggiator"]
projects.notes: A long FUNC + KEYBOARD opens the ARP menu (stock: FUNC + SYN1 at the other end of the panel); a quick press still toggles the arp. Checked only in digiemu; not on a Digitone Keys or a unit.

projects.name: Mezclando (transition mode for Digitakt II)
projects.author: Lucioic (Oicul)
projects.features: ["DJ-style mix mode on the SONG key", "bring a reference pattern's tracks into the playing one, one by one", "per-track levels, mutes and one-step undo", "load the whole reference pattern with its kit"]
projects.notes: A DJ-style mix mode on the SONG key: pick a reference pattern and bring its tracks, with their sequences and sounds, into the playing pattern one by one, with per-track levels, mutes and a one-step undo; YES loads the whole reference pattern with its kit (stock copy + paste). Uses only the firmware's own functions and stores nothing of its own; stock SONG functions move to FUNC + SONG and TRK + SONG. Built locally in a browser patch page or from source (m68k-elf GCC, Node 24, a Modwerk checkout with core-dt2 1.0). English and Spanish README. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: Digitakt LED colours
projects.author: ceredmeat
projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI OS 1.54; elekloader core 4.0.1 or later and seq-events (since 0.6); djfilter 0.6+ optional
projects.tested_note: 0.9 tested by the author on a Digitakt MKI with OS 1.54 (themes, custom colours incl. editing RED with a coloured track, per-track colours, quick-mute colours, LED FX HEAT/RIPPLE/BREATH, HEAT following djfilter, settings across a power cycle); earlier versions in digiemu (mod README, read 2026-11-18); 1.0 and 1.1 (DigiARCADE game lights, BLOOM, only RIPPLE while recording) also tested on the unit (read 2026-11-24)
projects.features: ["LED theme editor: six themes plus CUSTOM, RGB 0-31 per colour family with trig-key previews", "per-track colours for all 16 tracks (hold TRK + LEFT/RIGHT); a track colour stands in for the theme's red", "LED FX: HEAT step heat map, RIPPLE on key presses, BREATH at rest", "HEAT follows the DJ filter when djfilter 0.6+ is in the build", "eleven idle light shows (COMET, RAINBOW, BREATHE, RAIN, SCANNER, SPARKLE, WAVE, HEARTBEAT, FIREWORKS, LITESHOW, BLOOM)", "trig keys follow DigiARCADE games and VISUALS screensavers; only RIPPLE while recording", "settings kept after restart, in one eMMC block"]
projects.notes: LED theme editor and standby light show: six themes plus CUSTOM, eleven colour families with RGB 0-31, trig-key previews, idle animations, settings restored at start-up. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06. 2026-11-17: 0.5 is tested on a unit; the licence changed from MIT to GPL-2.0-or-later (LICENSE file added). 0.3 added seven shows and core 4.0.1 support (it calls the firmware's redraw routine directly), 0.4 per-track colours, 0.5 one folding LED COLORS row in SETTINGS and a 2-second timeout for the TRK colour view, which could stay on. The repo no longer ships a ready-to-flash .syx, only the .elemod. 2026-11-18 (tag 0.9LEDCOLORS): 0.6 adds LED FX (HEAT, a cooling heat map of what plays on each of the 16 steps; RIPPLE; BREATH when stopped and untouched for 5 s) and needs seq-events; 0.7 shows the stock green/red mute colours during quick mute (TRK + FUNC); 0.8 pauses HEAT while recording and links it to djfilter 0.6+ through an optional (weak) symbol; 0.9 lets a CUSTOM red edit show while the active track has its own colour. The mod README is now a user manual with an FAQ. 2026-11-24 (tag 1.1LEDCOLORS): 1.0 lights the trig keys for DigiARCADE games and follows VISUALS 0.5's screensavers (optional weak links digiarcade_leds and visuals_leds); 1.1 adds BLOOM, a cellular-automaton standby show coloured by cell age, and shows only RIPPLE while recording.

projects.name: ZIBENS (drum-synth machine)
projects.author: ceredmeat
projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI OS 1.54; elekloader core 4.4 and machine-pages
projects.tested_note: README: tested on a Digitakt MKI, OS 1.54 (read 2026-11-24); no detail on what was tested
projects.features: ["four voices (KICK, LOW, SNARE, HATS), each with three algorithms and two parameters", "decay, drive and level per voice", "pitch envelope, a gritty bucket-brigade-style delay and a compressor on page 2", "pictures of the drum and of the envelopes (VIEW)"]
projects.notes: Elekloader machine mod (machine 34) laid out like a four-voice drum synth. Voices run at 24 kHz and are filled out to 48 kHz; a track costs nothing once sound and echoes have died. Page 2 uses sound slots 46-52, so FX Locks and Deja Vu RND destinations must not be used on a ZIBENS track. With DIGIWAVE and all flexmods loaded mod memory is at 251 of 256 KB. No .syx shared. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-17. 2026-11-18 (README, v0.6): each track's delay memory is now taken from the Digitakt's spare memory the first time the track plays ZIBENS, not from the mods' shared space, which frees 32 KB for other mods; if that memory runs out the track plays without its delay. DRIV, SEND, FDBK and COMP show numbers. 2026-11-24 (tag v0.7): the screen code is built smaller, which frees RAM for other mods; the sound is unchanged.

projects.name: DigiARCADE (games)
projects.author: ceredmeat
projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI OS 1.54 only; elekloader core 4.4 and seq-events; ledcolors 1.0+ optional for the trig lights
projects.features: ["21 games: rhythm game and two-player DRUM HERO, Simon, Breakout, Snake, Pong, Tetris, Space Invaders, Pinball, a raycaster maze shooter and more", "games that follow the playing pattern's steps and tempo", "ear trainer, beat match, pattern copy and sequencer puzzle", "trig-key lights for every game with ledcolors", "best scores saved on the unit"]
projects.notes: An elekloader mod with 21 games on one master page (FUNC + LFO, then the ARC page). Many play along with the pattern: notes fall on the steps, enemies march to the tempo, and games play the user's own track sounds (knob D picks the track). While a game is open the trig keys belong to it. Best scores and settings are kept in one 512-byte eMMC block (0x6004d). Snake and Pong moved here from flexmods' VISUALS. With LED COLORS in the build the trig keys light up for every game. Created 2026-11-18 empty (then a candidate); first content 2026-11-23. The README states no unit test.

projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI OS 1.54; elekloader core and machine-pages 1.5 or newer
projects.tested_note: README: on a unit with all other flexmods loaded, six DIGIWAVE tracks play smoothly, seven lag (read 2026-11-17)
projects.features: ["two wavetable oscillators and a square sub per track", "26 tables of 16 waves, PPG size and depth", "decay envelope sweeping the wave position; smooth or hard PPG steps", "bit crusher", "3D picture of the table"]
projects.notes: Elekloader machine mod (machine 33): two wavetable oscillators and a sub per track, 26 tables of 16 waves of 128 8-bit samples (22 made in the PPG manner, 4 from the Jomox Alphabase wave file, which the table generator needs and the repo does not include). projects.name: FX Locks (delay and reverb locks, Digitakt)
projects.author: ceredmeat
projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI OS 1.54; elekloader core and seq-events
projects.features: ["parameter locks on delay TIME, WID, FDBK and reverb DEC from the audio track", "TIME locks snap to the delay's note values", "a lock holds until the same track's next trig"]
projects.notes: Elekloader mod that stores delay and reverb locks in sound slots 48-51 of each step (unused by audio machines, but used by machine-pages machines with extra values) and applies the active lock about 1,500 times a second; the higher track wins when two lock the same knob. 0.1 stored locks that never played (it waited for a signal the OS does not give for these slots); 0.2 reads each step's locks as the trig fires. Ships the .elemod, no .syx. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-17.

projects.name: Modded Cycles Techno Edition
projects.author: mbreilly (m_reilly)
projects.version: v1.11 (tag, 2026-11-23): LFO 2, a second LFO on every track (press LFO twice; own speed, multiplier, wave, destination and depth, saved and p-lockable, CC 111-115, about 1.7 % CPU with all six tracks). v1.10.1 (tag): PUNCH works on SAMPLER, GRANULAR, WAVETABLE, UBSAW, GROWL, VACF, XMOD and DX; GRANULAR's Position follows the knob while a note plays. v1.10 (tag, 2026-11-22): the retrig becomes an arpeggiator on every track
projects.tested_note: v1.6 tested on a Model:Cycles before release; the Model:Samples build installed on a real Model:Samples through the startup menu over MIDI (2026-11-16 and 2026-11-18), Transfer not verified; the CHANGELOG marks v1.4.1, v1.6.1, v1.6.3, v1.6.4, v1.8, v1.9, v1.10, v1.10.1 and v1.11 as tested in emulation, not yet played on hardware (README, CHANGELOG, read 2026-11-20)
projects.features: ["28 machines: 909, 808 and 606 voices, 707 percussion, rumble kick, acid and growl basses, Braids, 6-op FM, a supersaw, sampler, granular and wavetable", "filter, insert effect and an attack fade-in on every track; Turing Machine LFO waves; an arpeggiator with chords, gate and latch", "sidechain and master DJ EQ", "6-channel USB audio", "companion plug-in that shows every knob", "load your own DX7 32-voice bank into the DX machine when building", "experimental Model:Samples build (turns it into a modded Model:Cycles)", "a second LFO (LFO 2) on every track"]
projects.notes: 25 machines (Elektron's six plus 19: 909/808/606 voices, rumble kick, modal metal, additive drum, acid and growl basses, Braids, VA, cross-mod, 6-op FM, pad, and a sampler / granular / wavetable engine), a filter and insert effect per track, sidechain, master DJ EQ, 6-channel USB audio, CPU monitor and budget; plus a VST3/AU/standalone plug-in that follows the Cycles and reads sounds back. Built locally from the official OS (Python only), checked byte for byte. README: every part tested in emulation, and played on real hardware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05. 2026-11-14: the repo moved from mbreilly/Modded_f-king_cycles to mbreilly/Modded_cycles_techno_edition (same history; the old URL redirects). 2026-11-16 (README, CHANGELOG, docs/MACHINES.md): 26 machines; the author takes bug reports but no feature requests and invites forks. The web builder uses a JavaScript port of drumkilla's mtlib. 2026-11-17 (README, CHANGELOG v1.2/v1.3): the builders take an optional DX7 bank for the DX machine (algorithm, feedback, operator ratios, levels, envelopes and velocity are used; keyboard scaling, pitch envelope, LFO and AM are not), and the built-in sounds ship as a DX7 bank for Dexed. v1.3 fixes four machine bugs, among them a RUMBL tail that could hum on and keep using CPU. The repo no longer holds any bytes of Elektron's firmware: each patch checks the original bytes by length and SHA-256. 2026-11-18 (CHANGELOG v1.4-v1.6, README, MACHINES.md): 27 machines with UBSAW (seven detuned saws on the curves of a published JP-8000 analysis, written from scratch); an Attack stage after the filter and insert effect on all 27 machines; the CPU budget's default raised to 80 % because a project made before flashing already counts about 74 % with the six stock machines (I140). The README now documents what happens to projects moved between this firmware, the official OS and other mods, and a clean switching procedure. 2026-11-19 (README, CHANGELOG v1.6.1-v1.6.2): the web builder and patch.py --machine samples take both official OS 1.13 files (Cycles and Samples) and pack this firmware inside the Samples OS, as Modded-Cycles does, so bootloader, startup menu and signature stay Elektron's; the result turns a Model:Samples into a modded Model:Cycles. Installed through the startup menu (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4) over MIDI IN; after that Transfer can no longer update it. Going back: the official Samples OS through the startup menu, after setting tracks on added machines back to stock machines. A Model:Cycles running the Samples OS would accept the file and then refuse Cycles firmware over USB until the Cycles OS is reinstalled over MIDI. 2026-11-20 (README, CHANGELOG v1.6.3-v1.9, MACHINES.md): 28 machines with 707 (machine 28, after UBSAW so project machine numbers stay; six synthesised parts at 24 kHz and 8 bits, cymbals 6 bits). Trig preview (hold a trig, press PAGE while stopped) taken from drumkilla's mod. Turing Machine LFO waves T3-T16 (a looping random sequence of 3 to 16 steps; a stock OS reads them as RND). UBSAW lost its own filter and Attack in v1.6.5, so its projects from v1.5-v1.6.4 sound different. v1.9: the Cycles' mute only holds back sequencer trigs, so ATMOS's trigless GATE drone kept sounding on a muted track; it now stops on mute (user report). 2026-11-23 (CHANGELOG v1.10, README): v1.10 turns the retrig into an arpeggiator on every track (FUNC + RETRIG: Arp, Oct, Chd with 12 chord types, Gat, Lat); a retrig on a trig arpeggiates that note and its chord at the retrig rate, or RETRIG held plays it live. The live arpeggiator comes from the original Modded Cycles; chords, sequencer use, gate and latch are new. Tested in emulation, not yet on hardware. 2026-11-24 (CHANGELOG v1.10.1, v1.11): LFO 2 on every track (FADE, Sph, MODE and Pol shared with LFO 1; both on one destination add up), an LFO 2 page in the plug-in; PUNCH now acts on the machines that use the Cycles' own amp envelope (projects saved with PUNCH on them sound punchier); the manual is at its eighteenth edition (56 pages). Tested in emulation, not yet on hardware.

projects.name: Whiplash (agent plays a Digitakt II)
projects.author: hejijunhao
projects.tested_note: two live sessions on a Digitakt II (2026-11-11, OS not stated) found MIDI Start also starting the unit's own pattern and basslines pitched far too low; both fixed in 0.4.0/0.5.0, but every release from 0.5.1 says it is not tested on a real unit
projects.notes: A Hermes Agent plugin that jams on a Digitakt II over USB MIDI: starts patterns by genre or mood, changes sounds live by CC/NRPN, mutes tracks (optionally the unit's own mute, CC 94); nothing is saved to the unit. Falls back to a virtual MIDI port without hardware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06. 0.3.0-0.8.0 (CHANGELOG, 2026-11-11): the timing runs in the plugin's own sequencer on MIDI clock; parameter ramps, bar-aligned pattern edits, sample slot select (CC 19), a clock-only mode, melodies, chords and song arrangement, a mix tool, listening to the unit's USB audio, play-along and undo; it never sends SysEx or program change and writes nothing to the unit; caps of 48 ramps and 1,000 CC per second. 2026-11-20 (README, CHANGELOG 0.9.0-0.9.5, reference.md, hardware checklists): 0.9.0-0.9.5 (all 2026-11-19) add a named "ontology" library: grooves with five energy levels, microtiming and ghost notes, 28 named progressions, bass/stab/lead phrases that follow the chords, darker/brighter/tension intents and key changes, song forms and moves ("build to the drop in 16 bars"), a taste review, and six more genres (classic, progressive, minimal and tropical house, melodic and minimal techno); one new tool, whiplash_list_library. No new MIDI message type or CC number. None of it is tested on a Digitakt II; a v0.9 hardware checklist waits for a session. The multi-device studio plan moved to 0.10.

projects.name: DBX-K2 (resonator kick for MDX)
projects.author: MonCalamari
projects.version: kick2-v0.9 (2026-11-06): HOLD replaces colour, pitch 38-160 Hz, saturation always on; v0.7 first release the same day
projects.features: ["DBX-K2: resonator kick USR machine with a falling pitch sweep", "knobs for pitch, sweep depth and time, decay, attack pulse, hold, saturation and tone"]
projects.notes: A DSP56300 user machine sent as SysEx into a USR slot: each trigger strikes a tuned resonator whose pitch falls from a higher start; knobs for base pitch, sweep depth and time, decay, attack pulse, hold, saturation and a low-pass tone. The release page lists cycle counts for the MKII and for the MKI with DRAM or SRAM and says it was tested on a MKII with the +Drive. Send the slot-1 .syx with about 300 ms between messages; it replaces USR slot 01. The author credits Claude with the DSP code and tooling. Per altstrument 2026-11-06 (the repo was empty on 2026-11-05).

projects.name: Machinedrum WebLoader (MDX user machines)
projects.author: gerdtanck
projects.tested_note: README: layouts checked in desktop Chrome at phone sizes; a real WebMIDI write test and a physical phone test are still outstanding; earlier hardware slot reads (MKI UW+, X.20 C) were made with a Python/RtMidi lab tool (read 2026-11-20)
projects.features: ["library of 131 MDX user machines with descriptions", "slot view showing what a load would replace", "load over WebMIDI from the browser, phone-friendly"]
projects.notes: Mobile-first web page (German UI) that loads MDS user machines onto a Machinedrum running MDX X.20 over WebMIDI: a library of 71 machines with PNG descriptions (dbx, murdenihcam, waftlord folders, unchanged originals), a slot view and a load queue, plus a dry run without a device. Ships no firmware or ROM files; protocol sources are pinned in toolchain.lock.json. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-17. 2026-11-20 (README, CREDITS.md, machines/jmamma/README.md): interface now in English; the library has 126 machines, adding 55 X.20-C user machines by jmamma (byte-identical SysEx, description images generated from the release's README and package data). Slots U01-U16 only (an earlier U17 read timed out); the X.20 C profile reads NAK 12 detail 0 as an empty slot, a heuristic for that profile only. "Loaded" means the final commit ACK came back; there is no readback compare. 2026-11-21 (README, CREDITS.md, machines/minimal/): 130 machines; four new development packages by minimal, all effects for an input on the preceding track (the Neighbor input): the CROSSFIELD stereo reverb pair RVB-XA + RVB-XB (r0001; uses UW RAM slots R1 and R2 and almost all of the DSP, reads across tracks outside the MDS specification, so not certified), the three-band OTT compressor NFX-OT (r0003) and the mono-to-stereo decorrelator NFX-DC (r0001). Checked in DSP fixtures (CROSSFIELD also in a firmware emulator), none on a unit. 2026-11-22 (README, CREDITS.md, machines/minimal/RVB-MR.md): 131 machines; new RVB-MR r0001 by minimal, a fully wet reverb after Mutable Instruments Rings (MIT) on the track after its source, mono or as a stereo pair on two tracks, borrowing UW RAM slots R1 (and R2); missing or occupied UW RAM gives silence. A quick-checked development build: 23 DSP checks, no firmware-emulator or unit run, and it misses its DSP target (about 15,700-17,100 cycles per 32-sample block measured in simulation on MKI and MKII).

projects.name: sample-shepherd
projects.author: julesyoungberg
projects.notes: Organises a sample library (through Fourier Samples), exports it per device profile and syncs it to a sampler without breaking the projects on it: backs up projects, works out which samples they use, plans uploads and deletions and carries them out resumably; never deletes a sample a project uses. Elektron devices through elektroid-cli; used only with a Digitakt II so far (about 30,000 samples over a USB link measured at about 77 KB/s). Licence not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07. 2026-11-10: the CLI reports sync progress as JSON events and stops a sync cleanly between files, for a planned desktop app. 2026-11-11: `plan-edit` turns rows of a sync plan off or on by id. 2026-11-12: `library index` writes a read-only SQLite index of a library (path, category, duration, format, hash) for the desktop app's browser. 2026-11-13: library index --ratings fills each file's rating (keep, drop, misfiled) from Fourier's review file, read only. 2026-11-17 (app/README.md, docs): the desktop app's first piece exists in app/: a SvelteKit front end with a style sheet page; the Tauri shell and the CLI sidecar come next. Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-18 (docs/cli): `library ls` lists the indexed samples (with --json, one row event per sample for the app). Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-19 (docs, app/README): the app's first Library screen (folder tree, sample table, filters) reads a recorded library ls run. Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-20 (app/README, docs): the Library screen adds a "terrain" (folders as bands sized by sample count); the CLI refuses a --db that is not a library index. Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-21 (app/README, docs/cli): `export check --json` reports every issue a render would hit on the device (too many files in a folder, folders too deep, wrong rate or bit depth, Elektron names over 32 characters) as rows, and the app gains an Export check screen (shown with a digitakt_2_50_3 profile run). Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-22 (app/README, CLAUDE.md, desktop plan): the desktop app now has its Tauri shell (a native window around the screens, still reading recorded runs; the CLI sidecar comes next). Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-23 (README, docs/fourier-patches): profiles digitakt_2_50_5 and generic_folder_5 sort up to five folder levels (a crowded group splits once more); not yet tried on a Digitakt. The project now carries 11 patches to the Fourier sorter. 2026-11-24 (app README, desktop plan): the desktop app gains a Sync plan screen (the plan's totals and two flows sized by bytes, export into the device and what's on the device to its fate; clicking a band filters the rows), fed by a recorded run until the sidecar exists.

projects.name: elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)
projects.author: Iced-Cream
projects.notes: One local MCP server per PC that gives AI agent sessions the same tools for testing Elektron units (Analog Rytm MKII, Analog Four MKII, Digitone; Digitakt untested on hardware) and their emulators: claim a unit, run a test plan, flash an OS, take screenshots, record and check USB audio, take or restore an Overbridge Total Recall image. It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same. 2026-11-11 (config example): an optional emulator headroom check waits for CPU, free RAM and a cap on running emulators before each emulator start. 2026-11-12: emulator timing (analog-emu unit or exact timing, the Sidecar's Overbridge stream on the Rytm) and a CPU gate that fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU. 2026-11-13: elklock marks a unit that stalled on its restart after a flash and refuses every device command on it until a watched power cycle (elkflash usb-cycle). 2026-11-14: DIN MIDI interfaces are configured per interface, not per unit; at a run's first DIN step elkbench probes each interface with the unit's working-kit dump request and uses the one that answers, so a cable can move between units without a config change; elklock locks each interface as its own device.

projects.name: sidecar-emu (Sidecar emulator)
projects.author: Iced-Cream
projects.notes: QEMU cut down to the Raspberry Pi 4B and the devices Sidecar's engine needs: boots the Sidecar engine image, answers over Ethernet, puts an Analog Rytm MKII stand-in on its USB-A side and gives its USB-C gadget a raw MIDI TCP port, so an OS upgrade or an elkbench run can go through the emulated Pi into analog-emu. A local experiment, not meant for QEMU upstream. 2026-11-19 (README): a usb-teensy device stands in for the Teensy 4.1 relay of the Sidecar firmware (its link protocol and the HalfKay bootloader, with fault options for flows that failed on the unit), behind an emulated high-speed USB hub, so a Teensy flash through the Pi can be rehearsed in the emulator. 2026-11-22 (README): an Analog Four MKII stand-in (usb-a4, USB id 1935:0b47, same link protocol as the Rytm stand-in: 256-byte blocks in for 8 channels, 200-byte blocks out for 6) makes a two-box Pi possible, with a gate script that boots, unplugs and replugs the Rytm and the A4 in both orders. The emulated Pi now has its SD card on EMMC2 as the real Pi 4. The Digitakt is not modelled. 2026-11-23 (README): several gate runs can share one host: stubs link over unix sockets in a private folder and forwarded ports fall back to free ones.

projects.author: sadnoise (femifleming)
projects.base_os: Octatrack MKII only; replaces the OS (Elektron's bootloader and Startup Menu stay untouched); the install file is built from the user's own copy of the official OS file, OS 1.40C
projects.version: v0.9.5-beta (tag, 2026-11-19): a repair release, no new features (headphones from a cold start, MKII headphone L/R order, level lamps, NO backs out, sequencer lock and MIDI timing, kits A to Z); simulator-tested only. v0.9.4 (not released separately): eight MIDI tracks, crossfader modes, Dutch, 8 patterns and song mode. v0.9.3-beta (2026-11-13): BBD removed, engine in DSP core 0's private memory
projects.tested_note: docs/CHANGELOG.md: the builds of 2026-11-13, 15 and 16 were tested and flashed on the unit (key sweeps of both faces, captures of all four outputs over a cable loop, DIN MIDI loopback); v0.9.5-beta (2026-11-19) is tested only in the project's new simulator (10 suites on the real image), not yet on the unit; the effect ports are verified in a DSP56300 emulator against the author's plugin models (aeria-fx test_results)
projects.features: ["replaces the Octatrack MKII's OS with its own", "weather-driven multi-effect chain of up to seven effects on the inputs", "8 audio tracks (sampler, synth and polyphonic MIDI machines) and 8 MIDI tracks on one clock", "ratchets, conditions, curved clock and a cellular automaton per track", "sequencer reverb bus and per-track routing to main, cue and headphones", "three LFOs, a Lorenz attractor and a flock of boids as modulators", "18-channel stems over USB"]
projects.notes: An operating system of its own for the Octatrack MKII, not a patch of Elektron's OS: a weather-driven multi-effect on inputs A-D (up to seven effects whose knobs the chosen weather moves) and an 8-track sequencer groovebox (sampler, sub, FM, noise, Karplus-Strong and polyphonic MIDI machines, p-locks, ratchets, per-track cellular automata), plus LFOs, a Lorenz attractor and boids as modulators. ColdFire part in C, effects in hand-written DSP56300 assembly. Installing it removes the stock OS until it is reinstalled from the card; both keep their saved data in the same battery-backed SRAM, so back up before switching. The build uses the Modwerk SDK's tools (not included); aeria-os/HARDWARE.md and AUDIO.md map the MKII for writing an OS from scratch, largely from octabam's and Modwerk's documents. Some effect folders (head, tap) are marked as someone else's work. Made with Claude Code (README). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-13. 2026-11-14: docs/CHANGELOG.md lists every release build and what was checked on the unit; docs/LOG.md is the request log of the 9-13 Nov build, with the hardware findings now on the Octatrack page and incidents I83-I86. 2026-11-20 (tag v0.9.5-beta, README, new docs/AERIA_PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md, CHANGELOG, LOG, aeria-fx test_results): the weather is trimmed to CLEAR, RAIN, FOG and AURORA (with a WX OFF switch); DIST, WIND, HAIL, TWISTER, BBD and the master EQ are gone. Builds of 2026-11-15/16 added eight MIDI tracks beside the audio tracks, a sequencer reverb bus, per-track routing to main, cue and headphones, crossfader modes, Dutch, 8 patterns and song mode, and were flashed on the unit. On 2026-11-15 a mis-encoded DSP multiply put garbage on the headphones; the build now refuses that form. After flashing the headphones were still silent (2026-11-17); v0.9.5 blames the cold-start order of the DSP clock and the output ring (a RAM boot cannot show it) and is not yet tested on the unit. New: aeria-os/sim runs the real image and both DSP programs on octabam's emulators with ten test suites; the specification lists the MKII facts used (output slot order, level lamp ids, battery RAM layout) and what only the unit can show. Cheaper effects since 2026-11-13: SMEAR with a 512 hop (1,165 -> 641 instructions a sample), VERB and AURORA at half rate (1,145 -> 736, 216 -> 165).

projects.notes: Unofficial custom OS for the Digitone II that adds TERRAIN, a wave-terrain synth machine (module "terreno"), plus quality-of-life mods. Built in the browser from the user's own OS 1.12 file: a patch list copies bytes from the user's sections 3 and 7 and inserts the project's own, then checks the result's SHA-256 against the tested build and reruns Elektron's integrity checks before the download. Built with a patched digikit (40 parameters per machine, voice adapter, OS 1.12 anchors) and dnfw's container code; several mods are ported from dn2_firmware_explore. Some page glyphs were captured from the stock pages (to be replaced by calls to the firmware's own drawing). Uninstall by sending the original OS 1.12. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14 (created that day, one commit); README read 2026-11-14. 2026-11-17: build v63e (2026-11-16) extends MOD GRAPHICS (gliding knob graphics) to the SYN pages of the stock machines by taking over the SYN page's draw method.
