projects.features: ["SMEAR: granular, phase-vocoded looper after the Qu-Bit Nebulae (in WERP's place)", "PLATEAU: plate-reverb FX machine fed by a BUS of chosen tracks; FLEX can record the BUS", "FASCIA: physical and spectral percussion and tuned-body engine (two exciters into two coupled modal bodies), 32 p-lockable controls", "ORGAN: pipe organ (stops, drawbar ranks, chiff, wind, tremulant, celeste) plus ATTACK and BREATH pages", "SILT: material synthesis (string, grains, skin, fluid) played by ten gestures, alone or as an ensemble", "Digitakt II sample machines from the DN2 mk2 mod (ONESHOT, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE)", "FLEX live-buffer machine with MUTE SRC and buffer locks", "+Drive sample library, recorder, Direct Jump and parameter slides kept from the DN2 mk2 mod", "DIGIDRUM: six digital drum voices after the Syntakt's, the voice p-lockable per trig; LIGATURE, a modular voice (22 blocks)"]
projects.notes: A second Digitone II firmware by the dn2mk2 author, separate from that mod: no Machinedrum or Monomachine machines, starting with one engine, FASCIA (two exciters into two coupled modal bodies, TZFM, ring and frequency shift, a spectral morph, a low-pass gate). Its first commit carries the dn2mk2 infrastructure (build framework, SHARC DSL, release gate); FASCIA's model, its float32 DSP-order contract and a bit-exact SHARC program come from dn2mk2 branches. Plan (docs/rift.md): stand FASCIA alone, measure its voice count, then integrate and release. The test bench is private. Found by find_new (new repo of a catalogued author) 2026-11-13. v0.1 (2026-11-13) removes the Machinedrum and Monomachine engines from the DSP image to fit the 2 MiB upgrade buffer. The roadmap (docs/rift-roadmap.md) plans per-track insert effects, an LPG filter type, a looping function-generator envelope and a granular machine. 2026-11-15 (releases/v0.3, ROADMAP): FASCIA fits about three voices of the heaviest patches and six to eight typical ones; sample voices get DSP time first. Planned next: an ORGAN engine, SILT, per-track insert effects, a granular sampler and stereo. 2026-11-17 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.4, docs/organ.md): v0.4 ORGAN ports the pipe organ of the author's Ravel firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 (GPL-3.0) bit-exact to a float32 reference, then to the SHARC within a stated tolerance; it runs inside FASCIA's DSP program under the same guard and costs much less than a FASCIA voice. Known issue: FASCIA with BEND up and DAMP near 0 decays unevenly and sometimes cuts a voice (keep BEND at 10 or less). Next: SILT (material synthesis), the BEND fix, the reworked FLEX, then a bead engine and a Three Sisters-style filter. 2026-11-18 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.5-v0.6, docs/organ.md, docs/silt-dsp.md): v0.5 adds two ORGAN pages that leave v0.4's organ bit for bit at 0; v0.6 adds SILT (type 20) with a DSP cost plan: per-voice DDR delay lines, a 4-voice cap with the oldest voice stolen, graceful degradation of ensemble size, cost and stress gate steps with a negative control. Known issues in v0.6: v0.5 ORGAN sounds with MIXT up change (old PHRM/VELO values read as MTUN/MCHR); FIBER plays about twice as loud as the other materials. Planned: SILT level matching, CPU guardrails for every engine, LIGATURE (a modular voice wired by the user), the reworked FLEX. 2026-11-19 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.8): v0.7 takes FLEX buffers, MUTE SRC and the NAME screen over from dn2mk2 v0.54-v0.57; v0.8 brings back RESONATOR as machine type 22 (24 two-pole modes a voice, a mallet blended with a noise burst; notes ring through retriggers, a rung-out voice costs nothing, the newest notes are kept when time runs short). Next: a new screen style, LIGATURE and the first FX machines. 2026-11-20 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.9-v0.11): v0.9 removes RESONATOR again at the owner's decision (a v0.8 RESONATOR track opens as FM Tone), lists LIGATURE in MACHINE SEL and draws every RIFT machine on LINE pages (two rows of four moving glyphs, values shown the Syntakt way, locked cells inverted while their trig is held); a manual sits behind the patcher's MANUAL button. v0.10 puts DIGIDRUM on machine type 22, RESONATOR's old number, so a v0.8 RESONATOR track never re-saved in v0.9 opens as DIGIDRUM with its old values read as DIGIDRUM's. v0.11: the frame guard rendered voices newest first, so a melody or a re-struck note took the time and a held chord was stolen (a user report); now voices whose note is off go after every held voice. More held notes than the DSP can run still lose the oldest. Planned: THOLET (a piano leaning toward a Rhodes), a granular phase-vocoded looper in WERP's place, FX machines that other tracks feed, an own stretch algorithm. 2026-11-21 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.13-v0.14, docs/microtuning.md): v0.13 PARITY ports the DN2 mk2 mod's v0.60-v0.63 sampler updates (live slice edits, zero-crossing snap, GRID's ALLOCATE SLICE fix, a FLEX save that does not normalise, +24 dB on single-track FLEX takes, which the mod itself cut to +12 in its v0.65 after a tester's measurement: I185). v0.14 MONTUNE adds recorder MON, microtuning (every RIFT machine retunes; SLICE and GRID never; the same +Drive record region as the mod, not cleared by ERASE MOD DATA yet) and +12 dB playback for FLEX takes of MAIN and IN. Planned: THOLET, the granular looper, more LIGATURE blocks, and the mod's keyboard HOLD. 2026-11-22 (FIRMWARE.md, README, releases v0.15-v0.17, docs/smear.md, docs/tholet.md): v0.15 adds THOLET and the DN2 mk2 mod's KEYBOARD HOLD; the DSP upload then had 1.3 KB left of its 1 MiB. v0.16 SMEAR takes WERP's place (a saved WERP track opens as SMEAR with odd settings) with three readers of one loop: a phase vocoder, a tape-like read and eight grains. To make room the ColdFire sends ORGAN's, THOLET's and SMEAR's tables to the DSP at power-on, and those machines stay silent until the tables arrive. v0.16 also adds eight LIGATURE blocks and machine logos in MACHINE SEL. v0.17 PLATEAU is RIFT's first FX machine: a track fed by the sum of chosen tracks (the BUS page); only one plays at a time. THOLET is removed (its tracks open as FM Tone). All gated in the emulators, no unit result. The README now says "in development, released in small steps". 2026-11-23 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.18-v0.19, notices/2026-11-22-smear-plateau.md): a notice told users not to play SMEAR or PLATEAU on v0.16/v0.17: on the owner's and a tester's units a SMEAR note silenced every machine until a power cycle (I190). v0.18 turns SMEAR's vocoder off, makes the frame guard expect a voice's peak cost, replaces any non-finite or runaway block with silence, and prices every machine's worst block on a cost model of the unit (memory waits included) in the gate. It also adds GLASS, a filter type that a sound saved with it loads as Multi-Mode on stock or the DN2 mk2 mod. v0.19 adds CONTOUR, a wave-terrain synth whose idea comes from TERRAIN for the Digitone II (terrain-dn2); none of its code is used. The DSP image is 1,042,588 of 1,048,575 bytes. Power-cycle once after flashing: the first start can leave ORGAN silent. 2026-11-24 (v0.20, v0.21): a slide trig with no SLEN lock now lasts until the next trig, not one step (lock SLEN 1 for the old timing); a high CONTOUR note with feedback costs the DSP up to about four times more. v0.21's plate replaces the call of the stock reverb core and keeps sends, routing and LFO destinations; PLATEAU's 9 KB of DSP upload went to the plate. Takes a track recorded on earlier versions stay 18 dB hot (GAIN -18). Known: GLASS on several busy tracks can run the DSP past its frame and SMEAR's TUNE does nothing at BLND 0, both fixed in a gated v0.22 not yet released.

projects.features: ["flash once, then add and remove mods without new firmware", "mods sent over USB from a command-line tool (Digitone) or copied to the CF card (Octatrack), each checked by CRC-32", "MODS page: switch mods on or off with a check for clashes, apply and restart", "crash guard: a boot that crashes right after linking is followed by one safe boot (Octatrack, Rytm MKII, A4 MKII: holding NO at power-on also skips the mods)", "projects remember their mods and offer to switch to them on load (Digitone, Octatrack)", "Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII: elekloader's Drive Loader under TELOS's name; mods uploaded to /mods with Elektron Transfer or Elektroid", "Octatrack: card mods may patch the OS and send DSP code (via dspload-ot)"]
projects.notes: An elekloader build that is flashed once and then links more mods at every boot from a store on the unit, so new mods need no new firmware: .elemod files go over USB (SysEx with the non-commercial id 0x7D, each file read back and checked by CRC-32), and a MODS (TELOS) page at the end of SETTINGS switches them on or off for the next boot. A boot that crashes within 10 s of linking makes the next boot link nothing (one safe boot). Only +Drive-style mods (code and .bss, no patch sites). On the Digitone mk1 the store is 2 MB of raw +Drive sectors outside every area stock uses, so it never shows in Transfer; up to 63 files. Planned for the other devices elekloader supports. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-17: the Octatrack port is in the repo (octatrack/, 0.4, emulator only): .elemod files on the CF card in /ELEKLOADER/MODS (copied by USB DISK MODE or a card reader) are linked at the card's first mount, before the project load; unlike the Digitone's, these mods may patch the OS (sites), checked against stock bytes, written with interrupts masked when no task is stopped inside a site, and refused when the OS already ran them before the mount (code 23). 14 of the shop's 15 non-USB octabam conversions link together (about 61 KB); USB mods stay flash-only. DSP code from the card goes through elekloader's dspload-ot. On both devices each saved project now keeps the list of mods that ran, and loading one whose mods differ offers to switch them (LOAD PROJECT MODS?). A poc branch adds site-writing and memory-region mods for the Digitone (POC.md). 2026-11-22 (README, ar2/ and a4mk2/ README and mod.json, vendor/drive-loader-*): ports for the Analog Rytm MKII (ar2/, 0.1, OS 1.74, core-ar2 0.18) and the Analog Four MKII (a4mk2/, 0.3, OS 1.56, core-a4mk2 0.10). Both are elekloader's Drive Loaders copied unchanged into vendor/ and shipped under TELOS's name; only the SETTINGS row is TELOS's own. The module id stays drive-loader, so a build holds TELOS or the Drive Loader, never both, and +Drive mods for the Drive Loader load unchanged. Mods go to /mods through the unit's own data transfer (Elektron Transfer, Elektroid). The A4 keeps them in raw +Drive sectors that FORMAT +DRIVE empties. Projects do not yet keep their mods on either device. Neither port has run in an emulator or on a unit.

projects.features: ["one recipe per track: a trig source (the track's own, random, Euclid, a Grids-style drum map or another track) shaped by pages", "random rhythms with density, strong-step bias and roles, weighted by Barlow's indispensability in six meters", "placement: rotate, anticipation, mask against another track, skip", "velocity shapes, accents, humanize; notes and two lock lanes from ranges, lists or noise", "trig conditions, retrigs, Ableton grooves and micro-timing drift (retrigs and accents on the Rytm only)", "takes: seed, VARY, phrases of takes, best of N; a preview before YES; a take is heard, then applied with FUNC + YES or undone with NO", "ROTATE ALL for the whole pattern, and YOLO: a random but musical recipe rolled for the track"]
projects.notes: Offline pattern algorithms as an elekloader mod, opened as a third TRIG page after EUCLIDEAN: generate rhythms, notes, accents, trig conditions, retrigs and sample locks for a track, audition takes with undo, apply groove timing and velocity, and rotate a track or the whole pattern. Everything it writes is ordinary pattern data that plays and saves on a stock OS. Analog Four MKII and Syntakt are planned. Groove tables can be made from the user's own Ableton Live grooves; none are shipped. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README and firmware notes read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-16 (v0.4.0/v0.4.1, README 0.5): navigation is LEFT/RIGHT, PAGE and the TRIG keys stay stock's while the page is open. 0.4.1 is the build to flash: 0.4.0 wrote new trigs without the stock SYN/SMP/ENV flag bits, and a compiler optimisation (store merging in m68k-elf-gcc 16.2) broke a step move in the emulator (I112). Recipes live in RAM only and are lost at power-off or a pattern change. The MAP source copies Grids' drum map (GPL-3.0, Mutable Instruments, not catalogued). 2026-11-17 (v0.5.0-v0.7.0, README, release notes, flashing, testing, firmware notes): first hardware passes on a Rytm MKII (0.5.1, 0.6.0). Since 0.5.1 YES writes a take only with grid recording on and a take stays only after FUNC + YES; changing track or pattern, closing or turning RECORD off restores the original. Fuzzing found that two lock lanes on one parameter lost locks (the Rytm keeps one lock per parameter and step); refused since 0.6.0. The mod is 62 KB of code and 107 KB of RAM. Planned after 1.0: a TURING page that rewrites the track at each loop end. 2026-11-18 (v0.7.1, README, manual, flashing, testing, status M2.6): 0.7 is declared a beta for users; feedback decides what changes before 1.0. 0.7.1 fixes YOLO: take() fell off its end without a return value, so whether a roll stayed depended on a leftover register; the emulator passed by chance (I142). The mod now builds with -Werror=return-type. Boot screen shows T071 (a patch release shows Txyz, a minor one TSxy). 2026-11-20 (README, docs/firmware-notes-st142.md, flashing-st.md, plan-syntakt.md, status S0.2-U3, mods/*-st, manual): a Syntakt OS 1.42 port is in development, tested in analog-emu only (102 emulator checks), with no file offered to flash; the beta stays Rytm-only, so `devices` stays analog-rytm. The mod's code is split into a device-neutral frame/ and one part per device. On the Syntakt it uses a minimal hook-bus core of its own (456 bytes, from Synfact's GPL sources) because Synfact's core-st 2.0.3 does not link with gcc 16.2, so it does not run beside Synfact's mods. Code and data sit at 0x47a00000-0x47b00000, a range the emulator never saw the OS use; a canary mod is to check that on a unit with all 64 sample slots loaded. Differences from the Rytm: no retrigs, accent or slide; NOTE only (chord notes kept); LOCK lists the track's machine's controls; no lock-row limit. The unit file is stock 1.42 rebuilt by elektron-firmware-tool with only MAIN changed. A device header (st_params.h) is generated from the user's own stock file and never committed. Unit steps planned: practise the startup-menu recovery, flash a round-tripped stock file, the canary, then the mod. Rytm manual: YES + SCENE does not save a pattern while the mod is open (the mod takes YES, SCENE closes it). 2026-11-21 (v0.8.0, README, release-0.8, flashing-st, testing, requirements, adding-a-device, site device pages): 0.8.0 makes the Syntakt (OS 1.42) a second device, "ready for testing" (beta), so `devices` now lists it. Its first hardware pass (2026-11-19, one unit, on the 0.7.1-labelled build of the same code) went in steps: the startup-menu way back on stock, a stock file round-tripped by elektron-firmware-tool, a memory canary over 0x478b0000-0x47bf0000 with all 64 sample slots loaded (OK), then the 15 first checks, including a take kept across a power off (I184). The Rytm build of 0.8.0 is the same instrument on reorganised code and has no unit pass yet. Analog Four MKII and Digitone II are named as the next devices (docs/adding-a-device.md).

projects.notes: Mods for the Digitone mk1 on elekloader. Drum Mode turns a MIDI track into an 8-lane drum sequencer on the track's own MIDI channel. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-16. 2026-11-17: Drum Mode 0.8 (build shows OS version DRM8) adds grid editing per lane in GRID RECORDING, per-lane trig LEDs and two DRUM pages behind the MIDI LFO page (mod pages 27/28); a user manual (docs/MANUAL.md) covers install, recovery via the startup menu's OS UPGRADE, and limits (the corner strip hides the tempo; no p-locks by holding a trig key in GRID RECORDING). The DigiArp build recipe and notes were removed; the README now points to DigiArp MIDI in the elekloader Mod Shop. Planned, after unit tests: drum kit presets, synth tracks as extra drum or MIDI tracks. 2026-11-18: a new digiarp-core5 folder rebuilds DigiArp MIDI 0.9-dev11 for core 5.3 (two exported names changed, since core 5.3 now exports fw_note_on/fw_note_off for other routines) and builds one firmware with Drum Mode (OS DMA1): DigiArp's 8 tests and Drum Mode's 119 checks pass on it in digiemu, plus 13 side-by-side checks; not yet on a unit and not reviewed by DigiArp's author. Known bugs listed: step 1 after PLAY follows the previous setting; a UI hang with the Mod Menu open in one emulator sequence; the lane strip vanishing on page switches (unit); a mod page slot clash with DigiTables (slot 27). The repo offers no ready-made .syx; users build their own. 2026-11-18 (README, docs/debugging.md): status beta, working on the unit. On a Digitone at OS 1.44, beats recorded by 0.8 never played: three on-screen debug builds and the emulator showed that the project keeps one set of track edit objects per pattern, and 0.8 always wrote through A01's (0.8.1 also tried A02's); every emulator test had run on A01. 0.8.2 uses the active pattern's set (I153). New known bug from the emulator: on a Drum Mode track the trig keys after PTN or BANK play pads instead of choosing a pattern. Planned: select a lane by its pad alone, and Drum Mode settings per pattern and track. 2026-11-20 (README, drum-mode README/MANUAL/design/ui, mod.json): the repo was renamed Digitone-mods -> Digitone-Drum-Mode (same history; the old URL redirects) and now holds Drum Mode only. The digiarp-core5 folder was removed on 2026-11-19: the DigiArp MIDI core 5.3 rebuild and the build of one firmware with both mods moved to the author's fork morriess/Digitone-MIDI-Arpeggiator (branch core-5.3), still emulator only; a unit test and a pull request to DigiArp's author are to do. 0.8.3 to 0.10 (2026-11-19): 0.8.3 fixes empty DRUM pages and the vanished lane strip after a pattern pick (seen on the unit on H02; a firmware view left on top of the view stack, probably I141's cause); a pad selects its lane (0.9); keys 9-16 are a running light (0.9.1); PTN, BANK, chains and held grid steps reach the stock again (0.9.2); step 1 follows a change made while stopped (0.9.4, through seq-events' sq_rearm); settings per pattern and track with up to 10 kits per project (0.10, project block DRMK and core lane parameter 191). Saving on the stock OS drops the Drum Mode settings (the steps stay). Open: pattern copy with PTN, MUTE mode and STEP RECORDING are unchecked; the DigiTables page 27 clash stays. Ideas after v1: ratchets, note repeat, Euclidean fills, lengths and probability per lane; a separate generative melody mod. 2026-11-23 (README, drum-mode README, MANUAL, ui README, mod.json): 0.10 was tested on a Digitone (OS 1.44) on 2026-11-22; pads, recording, grid editing, running light, DRUM pages, mutes, per-pattern settings, copy/paste and save/load passed. Found there: the trig keys did not reach the stock SCALE menu and covered the PTN/BANK LEDs (fixed in 0.10.1/0.10.2, emulator only), and a MIDI track showed "Drum Mode off" and became unusable (open). 0.10.3: a new pattern starts with Drum Mode off. 0.10.4 needs one mod page (27), so it links with machines-dn1, Filter-FX and CTRL-PLUS; builds pin core-dn1 5.4. Planned: kit presets with a browser. 2026-11-24: the repo was restructured (the mod's README, docs and mod.json moved from drum-mode/ to the root; the README now carries the feature list, plans and known bugs). No new version or unit result.

projects.features: ["library of .afsnd, .dnsnd, .syx, audio and ZIP files with filters, favourites and a JSON inventory", "reads AFSND manifests and tags; splits SysEx dumps into whole messages with basic checks", "audition: browser playback, a rough proxy preview of native sounds, WAV export", "links a recording of the real unit to a sound; captures audio input", "Web MIDI note and SysEx queueing to the unit"]
projects.notes: A local sound library and audition app in one HTML page for the Analog Four MKI / Analog Keys and the Digitone MK1 (Web Audio and Web MIDI in Chrome or Edge; a Windows script starts a local server for MIDI and audio input). It lists .afsnd, .dnsnd and .syx files, audio and ZIP archives, reads the manifest and tags of AFSND containers, and splits SysEx files into complete messages with basic manufacturer and 7-bit checks. Native sound payloads are not decoded: the "proxy preview" is a generic sound seeded from the file bytes, not the instrument's sound, so the docs suggest recording the real unit and linking that take. Elektron Transfer's protocol is not implemented; native sounds are never sent as raw SysEx, and project, OS and firmware transfer are excluded. A Web MIDI send only queues data and is no proof the unit received it. Bilingual docs (English, French). Was a candidate (repo created 2026-11-17 with only a LICENSE); the app and docs were merged 2026-11-20 and read the same day.

projects.notes: Track 9 (the first MIDI track) becomes a key track: its note trigs transpose chosen audio and MIDI tracks by their distance from C5 until its next note, and a free 12-note remap table bends notes into a scale. Both are switched per track. FUNC + TRIG opens it and alternates with stock Quantize. Only sequenced trigs are changed, not live playing or MIDI in; the key resets to 0 on stop. Stores its slots in an eMMC name resource (mod.json). Repo created 2026-11-19, one commit; found by the keyword search 2026-11-20. 2026-11-21 (README, devs.md, 0.13-0.14): FUNC + TRIG now opens the mod's screen first and stock Quantize on a second press; the per-track switches are kept per pattern as T9's CC values, so they save with the project. projects.name: Syntakt custom firmware (DelayCtrl, DJ filter, Drive rectifier)
projects.author: bengleg
projects.base_os: Syntakt OS 1.41 only (the build refuses any other stock file)
projects.version: v2o (tested baseline, untagged, 2026-11-23); v2l the known-good fallback
projects.tested_note: PROJECT_STATUS: DelayCtrl's freeze, chop-lock, fades and delay silencing, the DJ filter and the Drive rectifier are confirmed on hardware; DelayCtrl's 9-step rate list and the FX SYN page have no hardware result; a four-feature build from the browser page is checked in headless Chrome only (read 2026-11-23)
projects.install: build from your own Syntakt_OS1.41.syx on the GitHub Pages builder or with tools/build/build.py, then send it with Elektron Transfer
projects.features: ["DelayCtrl: MOD B becomes an Octatrack-style freeze and beat repeat with chop-lock and fades", "DJ filter in the FX filter's TYPE list (in place of LP-Notch)", "a rectifier mixed into the FX Drive above 5", "a rearranged FX SYN page with reverb, filter and send controls", "browser builder that patches your own OS 1.41 file locally"]
projects.notes: Unofficial Syntakt OS 1.41 mods built on SyntHack OS: DelayCtrl turns MOD B into an Octatrack-style freeze and beat repeat that takes over the delay while it is selected; a DJ filter replaces LP-Notch in the FX filter's TYPE list; a rectifier is mixed into the FX Drive above 5 (digital tracks only); the FX SYN page holds reverb, filter and send controls. The repo keeps source and patch data only; a browser page or a Python build patches the user's own Syntakt_OS1.41.syx and publishes the expected SHA-256 of each build. It also carries a mod SDK (slot map, taken-spot list), a .sypatch.json patch format with a conflict checker, a Unicorn ColdFire harness and a pre-commit guard against firmware files; the browser build uses synfact-dev's engine (GPL-3.0-or-later) at a pinned commit, not vendored. RECOVERY.md: the bootstrap (section 2) is never touched, recovery is the DIN MIDI startup menu (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4). 12 commits, all by the author, created 2026-11-22; not a GitHub fork (it imports SyntHack's mods with their MIT licence). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23. 2026-11-24 (PROJECT_STATUS, STATE): the browser builder runs live on GitHub Pages and re-deploys itself from main; checked only in headless Chrome with the owner's stock file (a wrong .syx shows Ready until Build is pressed, then it is refused); the engine stays synfact-dev pinned at fcbc288, licence GPL-3.0-or-later for that code. Still open: the DelayCtrl 9-step rate list on a unit. Listed by altstrument 2026-11-23.

projects.name: SynPat (Syntakt pattern manager)
projects.author: nrdsrfr
projects.tested_note: README: tested against one Syntakt on OS 1.42: slot list and project reads (byte-identical to Transfer's backup), writes into an empty slot incl. a multi-chunk write with verified read-back, the queue end to end with the written project playing on the unit; 0x0C to 0x0A conversion not checked on a device (read 2026-11-24)
projects.features: ["copy a pattern and its kit from one Syntakt project into another, also across project versions", "queue copies from several projects into one destination", "back up and load projects over USB MIDI from a local web page"]
projects.notes: Unofficial tool that copies patterns (with their kits) between Syntakt projects, including across project format versions, and backs up and loads projects over USB MIDI. A Python codec for the .stprj project file (container, LZ4 blocks, layout) with a command line (info, verify round trip, copy) and a local web GUI that talks to the unit through WebMIDI and Elektron's RPC; runs in Docker. No README and no licence file; four commits on 2026-11-22 by the author, who also publishes the synfact release copy. Changes no firmware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23. 2026-11-24 (README and LICENSE added): copies patterns with their kits between Syntakt project backups (.stprj) or projects read from the unit over USB MIDI, queues many copies into one destination and writes the result as a new file or into an empty slot only (checked again before writing, confirmed, verified by read- back); never overwrites or deletes on the unit or on disk. Browser GUI from a small local Python server with Web MIDI (Chrome or Edge), plus a command line; project versions 0x0A, 0x0C and 0x0D (0x08 refused). Not affiliated with Elektron.

projects.name: Multitone (shared multi-boot kernel design for Digitone II firmwares)
projects.author: w0ts
projects.license: none yet (all rights reserved until the design picks one)
projects.notes: A design, not built: a small boot kernel that could start a Digitone II firmware kept on the +Drive instead of the one in flash and fall back to a safe one when that fails, plus one shared rule for the extra data each custom firmware keeps (+Drive sector ranges, RAM ranges, machine-type numbers), its identity (number, 4-letter id, brand, name, version) and how projects made with another firmware are recognised. A proposed registry gives stock DN2 machine types 0..17 and the +Drive slot store 0x000000..0x5D7FFF, and reserves +Drive 0x5FFE00..0x5FFFFF and RAM 0x476F8000..0x47700000 and 0x47800000..0x47FFFFFF for the kernel; address tables per stock version (1.12 first), switched off on others. Nothing has run on a unit or in an emulator; open questions Q1-Q8. One commit, 2026-11-22. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23.

projects.name: PLAY+ (Digitakt mk1)
projects.author: JohanStache
projects.base_os: Digitakt mk1 OS 1.54; elekloader core 4.1+ and machine-pages (render event)
projects.version: 0.4 (2026-11-22, untagged): DRNK added as PLAY value 12
projects.tested_note: README: checked in digiemu on the real build over a resumed OS 1.54 snapshot; not tested on a unit (read 2026-11-23)
projects.install: add elemods/play-dt-0.4-os1.54.elemod to an elekloader build with core 4.1+ and machine-pages, from your own Digitakt_OS1.54.syx
projects.features: ["nine new ONESHOT PLAY modes: PING, VARI, STUT, SCRB, HALF, SWEL, CRWL, SKIP, DRNK", "LOOP becomes each mode's control (turnaround point, drift rate, stutter note, scrub position...)", "tempo-synced stutter, tape-style half speed, reverse swell, grain crawl, tape skips and a drunk walk"]
projects.notes: Nine new values for the ONESHOT machine's PLAY knob after the stock four; in each, LOOP becomes that mode's control and is renamed on the SRC and LFO pages. Raises the ONESHOT descriptor's PLAY maximum (0x401ab6cc) from 3 to 12; stock plays values above 3 as FWD, and the mod replaces the block in machine-pages' render event, reading the voice record at 0x8000edc4 + 94 x track. It hooks the same PLAY text site as DIGISLICER (0x4005f91c), so the two do not combine. 0.2 removed STOP, so patterns saved with 0.1 on VARI or later play the next mode. No .syx in the repo; an .elemod for elekloader. Two commits, created 2026-11-22. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23.

projects.author: JohanStache

projects.install: add elemods/amp-dt-0.2-os1.54.elemod to an elekloader build (core 4.1+) from your own Digitakt_OS1.54.syx
projects.features: ["five AMP envelope curves per track: stock, linear, exponential, logarithmic and punch", "tempo-synced hold with 16 note values from 1/64 to one bar", "holding FUNC shows the real curve shape and the attack, hold and decay times"]
projects.notes: Five AMP envelope curves and a tempo-synced hold per track on the Digitakt mk1, after Modwerk's Improved AMP for the Analog Rytm. FUNC + A picks the curve (STK, LIN, EXP, LOG, PNCH), FUNC + B the hold (FREE or SYNC, 16 note values); times match the stock's, shaped decays end where stock is 40 dB down. Settings live in RAM (STK and FREE at power-on). Hooks 0x400716c0, the first routine in digihealth's FAST AUDIO block. Besides the .elemod, the repo holds built full OS images in build/ (they contain Elektron's OS). One commit, created 2026-11-22. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23.

projects.name: DN2 WISHES
projects.author: w0ts
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.12; the builder also reads the user's Digitakt II DSP section, Machinedrum UW OS 1.63 and Monomachine OS 1.32B files
projects.version: 0.69.2 (2026-11-22; upstream dn2mk2 v0.68/v0.69 merged, PERFORM); test builds v0.69.2-dualboot (SAFE MODE with the stock sound), -fdn8hw (FDN8 on the DSP's hardware loops) and -all (both, 2026-11-22, not installed); untagged own releases
projects.tested_note: CHANGELOG: test build v0.69.2-fdn8lite was installed on the author's unit on 2026-11-22 and its bus FDN8 cost measured on the system meter (about 17.8-18.4k cycles a block per playing FDN8, four at once); v0.69.2-fdn8lite2 passed only the brick-guard checks, not the full release check, and is not installed; every build must pass the ship gate (emulators of both processors) before a flash (read 2026-11-23)
projects.install: the project's web builder: give it your own Digitone II OS 1.12 file (and the other Elektron files it asks for); it builds and flashes over USB
projects.features: ["seven own machines: JUNO, ANALOG, DRONE, SOPHIE, TB-303, PLAITS and DRUM", "paraphonic mode on ANALOG and JUNO: a chord through one filter", "13 insert effects per track, among them a FDN8 reverb, tape, fold, ring and gater", "a modulation matrix and a voice budget against DSP overload", "all dn2mk2 machines (Monomachine, Machinedrum, Digitakt II ports) on OS 1.12", "browser builder that builds from your own files and flashes over USB"]
projects.notes: A Digitone II OS 1.12 firmware built on the dn2mk2 mod (a GitHub fork of De-Pattern's dn2mk2-firmware with about 300 commits of its own since it branched; the history also carries upstream's and dn2-firmware-explore's). Its own machines are types 50-56 in MACHINE SEL: JUNO (a Juno-106 voice), ANALOG (two oscillators, five filter models), DRONE, SOPHIE, TB-303 (Open303), PLAITS and DRUM; paraphonic mode on ANALOG and JUNO; insert effects (FUZZ, TAPE, FOLD, CHOR, WIDE, HARM, FDN8, XDLY, SUB, DIST, GATER, RING, JUNO); a modulation matrix; a voice budget that takes an old note's voice before the DSP runs out of time. The machines ported from the Monomachine, Machinedrum and Digitakt II come from dn2mk2. A browser builder makes the image from the user's own Elektron files and flashes it over USB; a build may be flashed only after the ship gate prints CLEARED TO FLASH (bootstrap and updater stock byte for byte, both processors emulated, stock audio compared bit for bit). Proposes the Multitone shared multi-boot rule (multitone). Found as a new repo of a catalogued author 2026-11-23. 2026-11-24 (CHANGELOG): three test builds, none installed on a unit: v0.69.2-dualboot keeps a copy of stock 1.12's DSP program on the +Drive (sent once over USB, checked sector by sector) so SAFE MODE can play with the stock sound; v0.69.2-fdn8hw runs FDN8's loops as the DSP's hardware loops (about 4 % less per bus FDN8 in the emulator, bit-identical sound); v0.69.2-all combines both, gives each DT2 sample machine its own icon and counts the notes, voices and inserts the guard left out. Offered as a hidden TEST entry on the builder.

rules.title: Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section.
rules.text: A1. Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. Patch the main OS only. Then the stock OS file can always restore the unit. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {elekloader-readme} {digikit} (ElekLabs README: patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8) {dn2mk2-safety} (dn2mk2 gate: sections 2, 4, 5 and 8 byte-identical to stock; mods change only 3 = MAIN OS and 7 = DSP) {digikit-old} (earlier README: 2 = bootstrap and 4 = updater never modified; sections 3 and 7 were the patch targets) {dn2-cfw} (brick checker refuses any bootstrap change).

rules.title: Know the recovery path before anything is flashed.
rules.text: A2. Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. Write it down in your output, with the exact button combination for the device (see [`common/recovery.md`](common/recovery.md)). Keep the stock OS file and, for Digitakt II / Digitone II, a physical DIN MIDI interface at hand. Note: digikit's README itself says recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware" - treat Digitakt II recovery as unproven, Digitone II recovery was exercised by dn2-cfw, Overtone and dn2mk2. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old} {synthack-os} {dn2-cfw} Incidents: [I45](INCIDENTS.md#i45-recovery-used-on-a-digitone-mk1-after-a-logo-hang).

rules.title: Back up first.
rules.text: A3. Back up first. Back up projects/sounds (+Drive) with Elektron Transfer before flashing. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw} Incidents: [I47](INCIDENTS.md#i47-stock-storage-resets-did-not-create-the-sample-filesystem).

rules.title: Never power off during an upgrade.
rules.text: A4. Never power off during an upgrade. `[doc]` {elekloader-readme}

rules.title: BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step
rules.text: A5. BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step (DT2 startup menu; runs only if the incoming bootstrap version is strictly higher). Never build or send an image with a higher bootstrap version. Elektron's own notes add that some official upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap right after the first restart - never cut the power then. `[doc]` {digikit-old} {elektron-dt2-notes}

rules.title: Verify every candidate image before it is written
rules.text: A6. Verify every candidate image before it is written - re-read it, check all checksums, check that only the intended section differs from stock, check it fits the flash budget, check the main OS unpacks to exactly the patched image. elekloader does this per build; dn2-cfw additionally runs a 12-check brick checker. `[doc]` {elekloader-readme} {dn2-cfw} Incidents: [I40](INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short). Check the name the unit will show too: a KYOTI composite build re-ran the base builder without a name, so the flashed Octatrack read another build's OS VERSION and the reported hashes were wrong; compare the version line and the hash with a fresh named build before you report them ([I124](INCIDENTS.md#i124-a-flashed-image-carried-another-builds-os-version-name)). `[hw]` {kyoti-1117} Also [I148](INCIDENTS.md#i148-os-upgrade-from-the-card-installed-an-older-base-bin-modwerk).

rules.title: First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down.
rules.text: A7. First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw} {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

rules.title: Gate what you ship.
rules.text: A8. Gate what you ship. Overtone and dn2mk2 only let the patcher save a file whose output hash matches a build that passed the project's own checks (Overtone: ~160 emulator checks per build; dn2mk2: `scripts/ship_gate.py` "CLEARED TO FLASH"). Do the same: no ungated output reaches a unit. `[doc]` {overtone} {dn2mk2} A gate checks only the cases it has: dn2mk2's FLEX MUTE SRC passed its emulator gate and still left tracks muted until a power cycle on a tester's Digitone II; v0.57 added gate scenarios for the case ([I133](INCIDENTS.md#i133-flexs-mute-src-left-tracks-muted-until-a-power-cycle-dn2mk2)). Also [I138](INCIDENTS.md#i138-a-new-keyboard-scale-crashed-the-unit-in-a-chord-mode-dn2mk2-v058). Also [I157](INCIDENTS.md#i157-fm-knobs-moved-the-wrong-parameters-dn2mk2-v059) (FM+ pages: no gate step checked which knob reaches which parameter).

rules.title: Respect transfer limits.
rules.text: A9. Respect transfer limits. Digitone II's USB upgrade receiver does not check the size limit of 2 MiB; oversized images stall at the end (nothing is written, a power cycle clears it). The withdrawn dn2mk2 builds v0.4-v0.7 hit this. Also keep the DSP image under 1,048,575 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-firmware-md} Incidents: [I3](INCIDENTS.md#i3-usb-upgrade-receiver-does-not-check-the-2-mib-limit).

rules.title: Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version.
rules.text: A10. Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. On Digitone II, Overtone needs stock OS 1.12 and dn2mk2 needs 1.11; getting from 1.12 to dn2mk2 means going back to a 1.11 base, and projects saved under the newer OS may not open. Always state the exact OS in the first line of a README. `[doc]` {overtone} {dn2mk2}

rules.title: Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash
rules.text: A11. Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash, and prove the transfer link with stock firmware first. Receivers have no error recovery (a dropped packet freezes the bar near 80 %), and recovery has so far been proven with stock images only. Full procedure in [`common/flash-procedure.md`](common/flash-procedure.md). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety} Incidents: [I43](INCIDENTS.md#i43-recovery-stalled-at-80--the-midi-link-not-the-image), [I44](INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing), [I46](INCIDENTS.md#i46-syntakt-startup-menu-recovery-tested-over-din). A first send can stall at 0-1 % and the second work: [I156](INCIDENTS.md#i156-the-first-usb-os-send-to-a-modelsamples-stalls-at-0-1--modded-cycles-protocol-flashers) (Model:Samples). A staged first flash that worked (way back on stock, a null repack, a memory canary, then the mod): [I184](INCIDENTS.md#i184-a-memory-canary-held-with-all-64-sample-slots-loaded-then-trig-seedr-passed-its-first-checks-syntakt) (Syntakt).

rules.title: One change per flash.
rules.text: A12. One change per flash. Never combine a new feature with a fix or a second patch in one image; keep the unmodified stock `.syx` untouched. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing}

rules.title: Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see.
rules.text: A13. Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. dn2mk2 runs `gate_hwrules.py` (complex-ping's `hwrules.py`) because DSP code that runs in the emulator can fail on silicon with DSP silence until power cycle. Use a comparable static check and keep to instruction encodings found in stock. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-safety}

rules.title: Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size.
rules.text: A14. Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. On the Digitone II the in-place loader of section 4 has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes and the default compressor setting turns that into -39,318, corrupting the image; the receive buffer is 2 MiB and the stock container is `0x1CC740` bytes. Use a packer that respects Elektron's stream limits (1 MiB window, 2,048-byte matches) and verify the margin of both stages. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-ele3} Incidents: [I39](INCIDENTS.md#i39-the-default-compression-level-corrupted-a-dn2-image), [I183](INCIDENTS.md#i183-a-full-digikit-image-hung-a-syntakt-at-the-logo-the-bootstraps-unpack-overran-its-stream) (the Syntakt bootstrap stages MAIN at `0x40200000`, the DT2/DN2 at `0x40400000`; read the stage from your own device's section 2, and an emulator that installs MAIN directly never tests this stage {digikit-1121}).

rules.title: Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock
rules.text: A15. Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock, together with the bootstrap and updater. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-ele3}

rules.title: Withdraw builds that lose sound.
rules.text: A16. Withdraw builds that lose sound. Digiwerk withdrew its six spring-reverb builds after finding that two of them stop the sound on a Digitone II; dn2mk2 withdrew v0.4-v0.7 for oversized images. Keep a visible list of withdrawn builds with the reason. When a build goes silent and the cause stays open, make the next test build audible about faults: Digiwerk sends the stock DSP's idle parks to a tone whose pitch names the fault ([I68](INCIDENTS.md#i68-spring-reverb-builds-lost-their-sound-on-a-digitone-ii-no-cause-found-offline); armio did not publish two filter builds that overloaded the DSP and broke USB audio, [I74](INCIDENTS.md#i74-filter-builds-overloaded-the-dsp-and-broke-usb-audio)). `[hw]` {alt-digitone-ii} {dn2mk2-firmware-md} {dn2-cfw-mr03} Also [I138](INCIDENTS.md#i138-a-new-keyboard-scale-crashed-the-unit-in-a-chord-mode-dn2mk2-v058).

rules.title: In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit
rules.text: A17. In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit (Syntakt: empty reset and factory reset erase data); only TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE) belongs to recovery. State this in every recovery instruction you generate. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery}

rules.title: "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file.
rules.text: A18. "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. digitakt-ii-research's All-in-One v0.3.0 states in its install guide that "this exact release image is not hardware-tested", that a Plaits trigger click remains and that earlier Plaits builds failed normal Transfer updates at 0%/PREPARING. Put such statements next to the download and in the build log, not only in a changelog. `[doc]` {dt2-install}

rules.title: Red-team your own safety gate.
rules.text: A19. Red-team your own safety gate. Build deliberately unsafe candidates (patched upgrade validator, changed DSP, computed flash addresses) and make sure the gate refuses them; "incomplete" is never "accept"; protected ranges need exact end addresses. Details in [`common/agent-workflow.md`](common/agent-workflow.md). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-redteam}

rules.title: The progress bar is not proof.
rules.text: A20. The progress bar is not proof. On the Digitone II the recovery bar counts received packets only; the write and the decompression (next boot) come later, and a single bad packet stops the transfer silently. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap} Incidents: [I23](INCIDENTS.md#i23-plaits-builds-failed-normal-transfer-updates-at-preparing), [I43](INCIDENTS.md#i43-recovery-stalled-at-80--the-midi-link-not-the-image).

rules.title: Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly.
rules.text: A21. Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. On the Digitone II the "upload complete" event can be lost on the first upload after boot (unit stuck on "Receiving"); send Start without auto-commit, all blocks, then End(1); keep USB silent ~90 s while flash is written; one upload, no blind retries - look at the screen first. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts} Incidents: [I4](INCIDENTS.md#i4-auto-commit-upload-loses-its-complete-event-on-the-first-upload-after-boot).

rules.title: Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path
rules.text: A22. Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path (Syntakt section 1 and bootstrap); a wrong configuration can harm analog circuitry. Do not emulate or reconfigure the FPGA; stub its status only. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

rules.title: "Success! Rebooting" is not proof.
rules.text: A23. "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. The DT2/DN2 in-OS flash writer ignores erase/program return codes. Verify after reboot. Prefer the RPC route with an explicit End; send End 0 on every abort. Details: [`common/os-update-protocol.md`](common/os-update-protocol.md). `[doc]` {digikit-f75} The same holds for a loader's own update: Modwerk's Octatrack base update said Done and the next boot ran the old base, [I76](INCIDENTS.md#i76-a-loader-base-update-over-usb-said-done-but-did-not-stick). Check the version after the reboot. `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz} Stock Analog Four MKII 1.56 can even hang on SUCCESS! REBOOTING after writing the new OS; power-cycle by hand, do not reflash (I103). `[hw]` {elkflash-stall} Also [I152](INCIDENTS.md#i152-a-transfer-install-stalled-at-waiting-for-sysex-on-a-rytm-mkii).

rules.title: Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`;
rules.text: A24. Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; never write the factory sample area (DT2 `0x458000-0x5D7FFF`). Lower areas can be overwritten by firmware, FORMAT or a crafted Data-API request. `[doc]` {digikit-f59}

rules.title: Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC).
rules.text: A25. Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). The stock engine fills a block to the edge without missing one. Code you add inside the Audio task must stop on a deadline measured from the block start, with margin, because one overrun drops a whole block. Put background work in a FreeRTOS task at priority 2-4, which cannot delay Audio. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

rules.title: On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only.
rules.text: A26. On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. Words 1-6 and 677+ are rewritten by the firmware. Word k is at DM `base + 4k`, written to both copies. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

rules.title: Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`.
rules.text: A27. Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. Everything above is cleared at boot. Never touch the bootstrap (it holds the STARTUP menu and recovery), the FPGA bitstream, or the MAIN OS factory console (`#UPGRADE`, `#FACTORY_DUMP`, calibration blob). `[hw]` {own-heatfx-notes}

rules.title: Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs.
rules.text: A28. Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. Use a write-back invalidation of the DM and PM caches together (`SHL1C_CFG`), then an instruction-cache invalidation, and keep the 12 instructions after every cache-register write 48-bit. Never mix invalidation and write-back-invalidation in one write. The emulator has no cache model. `[hw]` {digikit-f91} Incidents: [I15](INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot), [I35](INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes).

rules.title: Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops.
rules.text: A29. Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. Write a breadcrumb word (step, voice, type) straight into both reply records before each risky step, and keep a heartbeat. A stopped core never reaches the block-tail copy. On a stall, write a hang record to RAM that survives a soft reset (digikit uses `0x47fe0000`), then boot into a safe mode. digikit also enters safe mode when REC is held at power-on, and this worked on a Digitakt II; read the stock key state, since a scan of the input queue missed the key. Code that runs in the stock intro task is not covered by a handler installed later and halts the unit on a fault. `[hw]` {digikit-f48} {digikit-f77} {digikit-f117} Incidents: [I54](INCIDENTS.md#i54-safe-mode-by-rec-at-power-on-tested-on-a-digitakt-ii). On ColdFire boxes with storage, the firmware's own file primitives can write a text log to the card or drive (OctaMax did this on an Octatrack); this is often the only way to see code the emulator can't run. {octamax} octabam's soak script appends each reading as it reads it, so a total freeze still leaves its record ([I57](INCIDENTS.md#i57-a-demand-loader-soak-froze-an-octatrack-mkii)). Also [I163](INCIDENTS.md#i163-an-octatrack-froze-while-playing-after-the-walk-proj-down-yes-yes-modwerk-base-079) and [I166](INCIDENTS.md#i166-the-sequencer-stayed-on-step-1-after-a-303-track-was-pasted-into-another-parts-pattern-kyoti-v18bc-seen-once) (open; the field record or the steps written down are all there is). Also [I191](INCIDENTS.md#i191-the-ui-stopped-during-playback-with-six-modules-installed-modwerk-base-0713) (a field record with the module set and transport state alone did not find the cause).

rules.title: Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock.
rules.text: A30. Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. The in-OS flash writer on DN2 1.12 has no length clamp and wraps addresses. A bumped section-2 version triggers the bootstrap self-upgrade on the next boot. Both are ways to lose recovery. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-t14} {dn2-cfw-t15} Incidents: [I3](INCIDENTS.md#i3-usb-upgrade-receiver-does-not-check-the-2-mib-limit).

rules.title: A negative is only as good as the search that produced it.
rules.text: A31. A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. Before you write "X is not there", run the same search on something you know is there. Say what the search covered (addresses, encodings, pages), and write "not found by <method>", not "not present". Every expensive wrong answer in dnfw's history was such a negative. Examples: - "no SHARC program in the update": it was a boot stream, not raw code; - "no upload path": it was on the DSPI next door; - "no references": the addresses live in another address space. `[doc]` {dn2-principles} The same holds for readers and writers a patch must cover: when a probe lists every routine that reads or writes a value, patch them all or say why not. A Syntakt step-order mod patched the sequencer's readers but not the trig LEDs' own accessor, and missed the kit mirrors a power cycle restores; Clyps redirected one of three Octatrack tab painters and drew half tabs. Incidents: [I116](INCIDENTS.md#i116-a-step-order-mod-missed-two-readers-of-its-state-syntakt), [I122](INCIDENTS.md#i122-redirecting-one-stock-painter-drew-half-track-tabs-and-a-stray-mark).

rules.title: Store each section the way the original stores it.
rules.text: A32. Store each section the way the original stores it. Some sections are aPLib streams and some are raw, and this differs between devices. Decide from the original (do its bytes depack?), never from an argument. A wrongly compressed or raw section passes every checksum and bricks the unit. Mirror the original's own integrity fields and re-verify the written file. `[doc]` {dn2-principles} Incidents: [I40](INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short).

rules.title: Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them.
rules.text: A33. Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. Both ran bit-exactly in the emulator and hung a real Digitakt II's DSP. Save I/M/L/B registers through an R register. Do SIMD compute on registers, and move data in SISD unless a one-variable probe image has proven the access mode on silicon. `[hw]` {dt2-plaits} Independently confirmed: digikit's unexplained "rung C" halt on a DT2 came from 17 such stores in a frame save. The SHARC manual excludes them (a store's source may not be a register of the DAG it addresses through), and the assembler and emulator accepted them. A build without them played on the unit. digikit's patchkit now refuses these encodings at build time. `[hw]` {digikit-f49} Incidents: [I14](INCIDENTS.md#i14-dag-registers-stored-through-their-own-dag-hung-the-dsp).

rules.title: On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget.
rules.text: A34. On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. The Syntakt's CPU #1 sits at ~89 % at rest, so a few thousand instructions per block make the UI lag. Measure cost per block in the emulator, keep a regression test, and make effects idle when silent. Never use RAM above the BSS for mod code on the Syntakt: sample loading overwrites it. `[hw]` {synthack-docs} {synthack-guide} On the Digitone mk1 an emulator cycle model even pointed the wrong way: it called a release faster while the unit's idle CPU rose from ~70 % to ~87 %. Only A/B builds on the unit decide. `[hw]` {tonefx-dev} Incidents: [I24](INCIDENTS.md#i24-a-granular-engine-froze-the-ui-at-low-pitch), [I49](INCIDENTS.md#i49-idle-paths-of-sixteen-mods-cost-two-percent-of-a-rytm-block). On the Octatrack, a 43 KB copy with interrupts masked held off the audio frame and clicked ([I60](INCIDENTS.md#i60-a-long-copy-with-interrupts-masked-clicked-on-every-reload)); on the Syntakt, code fetched from DDR cost far more than its instruction count and took MAIN to 100 % ([I64](INCIDENTS.md#i64-a-chorus-running-from-ddr-overloaded-the-syntakts-main-cpu)). Machines rendered on the Octatrack's ColdFire need a budget too: three FM Synth tracks beside a busy pattern froze an MKII until Modwerk counted them ([I79](INCIDENTS.md#i79-three-fm-synth-tracks-beside-a-busy-pattern-froze-an-octatrack)). On the Digitakt mk1, released voices that never switched off took the audio load from 86 % to 94 % and made the UI lag; end a voice by the real amp envelope (the value first used was the filter envelope, A59) ([I81](INCIDENTS.md#i81-released-notes-that-never-ended-raised-a-digitakts-audio-load-and-made-the-ui-lag)). Count divisions in per-sample code: a ColdFire `rems.l` costs 20-35 cycles but one instruction in an emulator profile (I91); a mode switch at 85-94 % load froze a Digitakt (I90); four software drum voices overran an Analog Rytm MKII block, which costs about three times the emulator count (I97). `[hw]` {digicmi-037} {modwerk-rytm-analogbd} Also [I145](INCIDENTS.md#i145-many-stock-samples-overwrote-synfacts-resident-core-and-crashed-it-at-boot-synfact). A gap can also be the start of the next tenant's buffer: octabam's "free" Octatrack window `0x33da3..0x37eff` held the next FX2 slot's reverb buffer, and stubs placed there stopped the DSP ([I188](INCIDENTS.md#i188-window-stubs-placed-inside-dark-revs-buffer-stopped-the-dsp-octabam-test-images)). {octabam-1122}

rules.title: Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts.
rules.text: A35. Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. Measured on a DT2 and a DN2: taken branches ~7 cycles, CALL+RTS ~14, a dependent float multiply chain 1.5 per instruction, hardware-loop start-up 12, and ~58 cycles for every L2 data miss. Buffers spaced at 16 KiB multiples fight over one cache set. Emulator counts underestimate all of these. `[hw]` {digikit-f103} Incidents: [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x). Budget by a voice's peak cost, not its last block: RIFT's frame guard let a heavy vocoder block through and the whole Digitone II went silent ([I190](INCIDENTS.md#i190-a-smear-note-silenced-the-whole-digitone-ii-until-a-reboot-rift-v016v017)). {dn2-rift-1123}

rules.title: The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here.
rules.text: A36. The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. USB updates are received by the running OS. Before flashing anything that replaces or deeply changes the OS, make sure the user has a working DIN (or 3.5 mm TRS on Model:Cycles) MIDI interface and has sent a stock file through it once. A custom OS without the in-OS USB update leaves DIN as the only way back. `[hw]` {rytm-fw-re} {modded-cycles} {octabam} Incidents: [I22](INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I23](INCIDENTS.md#i23-plaits-builds-failed-normal-transfer-updates-at-preparing), [I44](INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing), [I45](INCIDENTS.md#i45-recovery-used-on-a-digitone-mk1-after-a-logo-hang), [I46](INCIDENTS.md#i46-syntakt-startup-menu-recovery-tested-over-din).

rules.title: A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC).
rules.text: A37. A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). Stock's audio task waits inside its block, so "time outside the idle task" and stock's block-handler span both read ~80 % on an idle DN2 and *fall* to ~65 % with 64 notes held. To know whether added code fits, measure the deadline margin of the block itself (A25) under the heaviest stock load, not the busy percentage. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} Incident: [I74](INCIDENTS.md#i74-filter-builds-overloaded-the-dsp-and-broke-usb-audio) (a load model without interrupts, cache, DMA and USB).

rules.title: If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum).
rules.text: A38. If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). The OS re-flashes the boot code from its embedded copy when a version or magic check says so (A4 MK1: a newer embedded version; Machinedrum: magic `0x224B` missing at flash `0x3FFE`), so a stray byte there can become the recovery path. Locate the embedded image per OS version, keep every cave and pool outside it, and verify copy and check byte-identical to stock on the finished `.syx`. `[doc]` {a4mods} {rytm-mk1-mods} {mdkit-docs}

rules.title: Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver.
rules.text: A39. Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. On the Octatrack this froze a unit (a stale zero-length packet) and stalled OUT stages (stock leaves ZLT on). Size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when you prime the stage. Send DMA'd replies from an uncached copy. Probably the same on every ColdFire box with the stock USB stack: the DT2 uses the same EHCI-style controller (queue heads in on-chip SRAM, EP0 max packet 64) and serves its own vendor requests on EP0 (digikit finding 42). Not yet measured there. On the DT2/DN2 the controller's transmit buffer is 64 bytes per endpoint: program every IN queue head you add for 64-byte packets, as stock does even where its descriptor says bulk 512; two 512-byte IN packets wedged a Digitone II's USB until a power cycle ([I70](INCIDENTS.md#i70-a-1024-byte-bulk-in-transfer-wedged-the-digitone-iis-usb-controller)). `[hw]` {octabam-traps} {modwerk-ot-traps} {digikit-f42} {digikit-usbfast} Incidents: [I5](INCIDENTS.md#i5-ep0-data-stages-of-a-multiple-of-64-bytes-stall-or-freeze-stock-usb-driver), [I6](INCIDENTS.md#i6-about-one-ep0-out-stage-in-50-100-goes-unanswered), [I70](INCIDENTS.md#i70-a-1024-byte-bulk-in-transfer-wedged-the-digitone-iis-usb-controller).

rules.title: Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator.
rules.text: A40. Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. An Octatrack change booted in the emulator and in quick power cycles, then stalled at the logo after minutes off. Emulators model neither reset settling nor RAM retention. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} Incidents: [I110](INCIDENTS.md#i110-a-remote-commanded-remix-switch-boot-stopped-on-the-boot-screen), [I7](INCIDENTS.md#i7-a-soft-reset-leaves-the-usb-controller-running), [I78](INCIDENTS.md#i78-the-first-play-after-power-on-started-a-tracks-recorder) (the first PLAY after power-on started a recorder), [I34](INCIDENTS.md#i34-a-startup-change-stalled-at-the-logo-after-a-long-power-off). Also [I150](INCIDENTS.md#i150-powering-off-on-a-mod-page-broke-the-stock-euclidean-page-at-the-next-boot-euclidean-scale). A RAM boot skips the clock and converter set-up of a cold start, so it does not count as one ([I159](INCIDENTS.md#i159-headphones-silent-after-flashing-though-every-ram-boot-bench-test-passed-aeria-os)); a power-up may restore state from battery RAM and never read the saved file, so a setting kept only in DRAM is lost though it was saved ([I168](INCIDENTS.md#i168-per-track-trig-modes-were-saved-but-gone-after-a-power-cycle-track-trig-mode)).

rules.title: Disassemble what you assemble.
rules.text: A41. Disassemble what you assemble. Every community assembler for these chips has silently mis-encoded something: - octabam's `dsp_asm`: `tfr` as `rnd`, unknown `mpy` orders as `mpysu`, `cmp` as `max`; - selas: negative shift immediates; - the DSP56300 reference assembler: overlapping `ORG`s accepted silently. Incidents: [I15](INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot), [I27](INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip). Round-trip new code through a disassembler and compare, and make the build refuse a mismatch. `[hw]` {octabam-traps} {elekloader-adapting} {mdkit-docs} Mis-encoding can also produce wrong facts, not only crashes: digikit's finding 103 published silicon "measurements" that came from probe instructions the old assembler had encoded as other registers (MMASK read as IMASKP, TPERIOD/TCOUNT as I0/I1), withdrawn on 2026-11-16. `[doc]` {digikit-1116} The compiler can be wrong too: m68k-elf-gcc 16.2's store merging at -O2 moved a 4-byte store 6 bytes early after a struct copy; build ColdFire code with `-fno-store-merging` and keep a test that checks a struct copy with field stores byte for byte. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116} Incident: [I112](INCIDENTS.md#i112-the-compiler-merged-two-stores-and-broke-a-step-move-trig-seedr-emulator). Also [I158](INCIDENTS.md#i158-a-mis-encoded-dsp-multiply-put-garbage-on-the-octatracks-headphones-aeria-os) (an `mpysu`-encoded multiply put garbage on an Octatrack's headphones).

rules.title: ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator.
rules.text: A42. ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. The forms below were excluded by ColdFire, ran in the emulator, and failed on a unit: Jump targets must be even: a jsr/jmp to an odd address raises an address error on the unit while the emulator runs on; elekloader's linker now refuses odd targets ([I61](INCIDENTS.md#i61-odd-jump-targets-froze-a-digitakt-ii-at-boot-the-emulator-kept-running)). Check that every routine lands in an executable section: code placed in `.bss` is zero-filled on the unit and stopped a Digitakt II with an illegal instruction, while the emulator ran the zeros as no-ops ([I67](INCIDENTS.md#i67-code-built-into-bss-crashed-a-digitakt-ii-at-boot-the-emulator-ran-the-zeros)). The same holds for storage the OS clears after boot: a Synfact core that moved a routine into the storage appended after the Syntakt's MAIN image crashed every boot, because startup wipes that storage after the resident copy ([I104](INCIDENTS.md#i104-a-development-core-put-its-module-binder-in-boot-storage-that-startup-wipes)). {digi2core} - `move.l #imm,d16(An)` (immediate to displacement) crashed a Digitakt II at startup with exception vector 4. digikit's machine builder wrote the same form (`2f7c imm 0008`, `move.l #imm,(8,A7)`) independently: it is 8 bytes long, and ColdFire instructions are at most 6 (the programmer's reference: "1 to 3 words", "limited to 3 sizes: 16, 32, or 48 bits" {nxp-cfprm}), so every image with that shim faults on a real ColdFire while the old generic m68k emulator ran it {digikit-f02}; - `move.l #imm,abs.L` (immediate to absolute) appeared five times in an early copier of a Digitone mk1 build, which then hung on the logo. It was the most likely cause, though the fault address was never captured. In the second case, a local ISA checker also accepted the form, because it decoded the instruction without checking the source/destination pair. Assemble with the right `-mcpu`, check hand-encoded bytes against the manual's mode tables (CFPRM pp. 4-47/4-48), and round-trip (A41). `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} {dn1-arpmod-e04} The compiler and the emulator can also read one form two ways: for `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` and a byte push to `-(sp)` GCC and octabam's ot_emu disagree, and the unit is not checked. Keep such forms out of the build (TELOS: `dl_memcpy` out of line, `-fno-ipa-sra`). `[emu]` {telos-ot-1117} Incident: [I117](INCIDENTS.md#i117-two-coldfire-instruction-forms-where-gcc-and-ot_emu-disagree-octatrack-emulator).

rules.title: A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit.
rules.text: A43. A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. Zero bytes in the image can be `.bss` that the engine writes only while it plays. A mod placed in such a region worked with the sequencer stopped and failed during playback (octatrack-mods, reported by rytm-mods-src). Before shipping into a new cave: fill it with a known pattern, flash, exercise playback, sampling, Overbridge and storage, and read it back. Combine this with static proof (no references) and emulator coverage (A4 MK1 practice), not instead of it. The same failure was seen on the Octatrack: tables lost to a heap tail (octamax), and a scratch word at `0x80006a60` overwritten under live recording on an MKI (KYOTI). This applies to data scratch as well as code. `[hw]` {rytm-mods-src} {a4mods} {kyoti-caves} Incidents: [I18](INCIDENTS.md#i18-the-flash-cave-reportedly-froze-a-unit-at-the-logo), [I19](INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit), [I48](INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit). Further cases: OCTAMAX state inside the stock audio-analysis buffer of the Octatrack silenced tracks ([I59](INCIDENTS.md#i59-patch-state-inside-a-stock-tasks-buffer-silenced-tracks)); a Synfact window in the zero tail of a Syntakt filter table was read as filter poles ([I63](INCIDENTS.md#i63-a-mods-memory-window-broke-the-basewdth-filter)). Also [I146](INCIDENTS.md#i146-pattern-mute-stored-its-layer-in-the-one-shot-trig-mask-octabam). A canary that passed this test on a unit, with all sample slots loaded: [I184](INCIDENTS.md#i184-a-memory-canary-held-with-all-64-sample-slots-loaded-then-trig-seedr-passed-its-first-checks-syntakt) (Syntakt `0x478b0000-0x47bf0000`, one unit).

rules.title: A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over.
rules.text: A44. A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. When a mod sheds voices to stay inside the audio budget: - Trigger on a peak that lasts several blocks or on a slow average. Isolated heavy blocks (a step with many trigs, caches flushed by the UI) are over before you see them, and cutting a voice then only adds an audible gap. - Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units. An integer `avg += (x - avg) >> 8` never moves, and the rule silently never fires. - Choose the victim by audibility after the mixer, and prefer muted tracks. On a Model:Cycles this turned "the last track always cuts out" into clean playback at 89 % peak. `[hw]` {supermodel-notes} A voice the governor drops must stay off until its next note: dn2mk2's guard retried a dropped sample voice every block, and an ONESHOT kick flickered and sounded crunchy beside heavy synth voices ([I71](INCIDENTS.md#i71-a-dsp-load-guard-dropped-a-sample-voice-block-after-block)). Render the cheap voices first, so time runs out on the expensive ones. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v048} Shed released tails before held notes: a guard that ordered voices newest first stole a held chord under a melody ([I161](INCIDENTS.md#i161-held-chord-notes-were-cut-when-a-melody-played-over-them-rift-v010-and-earlier-digitone-ii)).

rules.title: Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A45. Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). The last 11 instructions of a hardware loop, and all of a loop shorter than that, must be legacy 48-bit instructions; the rest of the code may be compressed. Three projects reached this independently: - digikit: a selas defect left the end of a nested loop compressed, and `fx/freqshift` froze a real Digitakt II at boot while the emulator ran it ([digitakt-2.md](devices/digitakt-2.md)) {digikit-f91}; - the digitone-2-modding-skill checks it with `hwrules.py`, and stock DN2 1.11 obeys it in all 286 loops; its full list (loop end, `LCE`, CALL and branch spacing, same-DAG) is in [digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md](devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md) {dn2-skill-scripts}; - the DT2 Plaits port compresses everything else and keeps loop ends in ISA ([digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md](devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md)). Incidents: [I15](INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot). Wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS`, and check the rule on the disassembly (A41), since the emulator does not enforce it. `[hw]`

rules.title: Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A46. Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). The ColdFire depacks section 7 into a 1 MiB buffer and checks the size only afterwards, so a larger stream overruns the buffer before it is refused. One build with a 1,314,460-byte stream raised an exception on a unit. Run the stock depacker (or an exact copy) in the build and fail above the limit; zero regions can be fill blocks instead of stored bytes. Details: [firmware-container.md](common/firmware-container.md). `[hw]` {dt2-lab-capicola} {digikit-f06} Incidents: [I16](INCIDENTS.md#i16-a-decoded-section-7-over-1-mib-crashed-the-unit).

rules.title: Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2).
rules.text: A47. Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). The DN2's eMMC TRIM can report TRIM ERROR on a busy card: the stock busy wait arms its DAT0 interrupt before testing DAT0 and leaves a stale semaphore post, and the driver has no timeout. Read the eSDHC present state (`PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024`) before every TRIM and verify read and call only when DAT0 is high and no inhibit is set; retry an idempotent command a few times; let a long erase pause and resume instead of failing. Incidents: [I1](INCIDENTS.md#i1-stock-emmc-trim-fails-with-trim-error-on-a-busy-card). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v040}

rules.title: Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized.
rules.text: A48. Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. On the DN2 the bootstrap leaves the data cache off, but the main OS turns it on for `0x40000000-0x47ffffff` only; the SSI DMA buffers stay uncached. Packing the SSI slots with byte-wise uncached reads stalled the sequencer; reading each of the 14 slots once as a 32-bit word did not. On the A4 MK1 only `0x40000000-0x43ffffff` is cached and ~1,000 uncached accesses per block per voice slowed the UI and could crash the unit. The reverse also bites: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache, so a reply the CPU wrote may go out stale. Copy hot state into cached memory (or the stack) once per block, work there, write it back; send DMA data through the uncached alias. Incidents: [I10](INCIDENTS.md#i10-byte-wise-reads-of-uncached-dma-buffers-stalled-the-sequencer), [I11](INCIDENTS.md#i11-uncached-state-in-a-chord-oscillator-slowed-the-ui-and-could-crash-the-unit), [I35](INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-cfw-usb} {a4mods} {modwerk-ot-traps}

rules.title: Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit.
rules.text: A49. Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. A development unit carries state the users' units lack: armio's R012 mounted a sample filesystem it never created, and only new users' units (0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads) showed it. Before a release, flash stock, reset, then install the build as a new user would, and check every storage path it relies on. Incidents: [I12](INCIDENTS.md#i12-a-sample-machine-mod-could-not-create-the-storage-it-needed), [I47](INCIDENTS.md#i47-stock-storage-resets-did-not-create-the-sample-filesystem). `[hw]` {armio-samples}

rules.title: Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads.
rules.text: A50. Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. On the Octatrack, key events posted straight into stock's queues crashed the unit minutes later, and restoring DSP-read data every frame corrupted the audio. Feed the panel parser its own bytes; restore only CPU-side bookkeeping. (E2 is the same rule for stored sound data.) Incidents: [I30](INCIDENTS.md#i30-key-events-posted-into-stocks-queues-crashed-the-unit-minutes-later), [I31](INCIDENTS.md#i31-restoring-dsp-read-state-every-frame-corrupted-the-audio). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} {octamax} Use stock's own state bits as stock does: on the Octatrack hide a window by its visible bit, never by unlinking it, or stock builds its next window into your slot ([I121](INCIDENTS.md#i121-hiding-a-window-by-unlinking-it-let-stock-build-setup-inside-it)). Stock's queues may have no full check: the Analog Rytm MKII's UI queue (1024 entries) overwrites unread messages under load, so a mod that posts into it keeps its own bounded pool and counts its own waiting events ([I131](INCIDENTS.md#i131-an-overloaded-rytm-overwrote-its-own-ui-messages-and-lost-live-recorded-hits), SB27). `[hw]` {kyoti-1117} {modwerk-rytm-1116} Read stock's own state rather than counting keys yourself: a missed release left Arr Rows' own CUE count stuck ([I155](INCIDENTS.md#i155-arr-rows-drew-its-selection-wrong-and-pasted-as-an-insert-modwerk-draft-octatrack-mki)). When you suppress a stock handler, still do its bookkeeping: a hook that kept the Octatrack's hold popup closed skipped the clear of the hold bit, and the release then deleted the trig ([I167](INCIDENTS.md#i167-holding-a-step-again-deleted-its-trig-octabam-lock-edit)).

rules.title: Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width.
rules.text: A51. Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. An Octatrack DSP frame engine stopped after 50.7 minutes because its counter saturated past `$7fffff`. Short tests do not reach such limits; let a build play for at least an hour with the busiest project you have. Incidents: [I32](INCIDENTS.md#i32-a-dsp-frame-counter-saturated-after-507-minutes). `[hw]` {octabam-traps} octabam's 118-switch demand-loader soak found a freeze no short test showed ([I57](INCIDENTS.md#i57-a-demand-loader-soak-froze-an-octatrack-mkii)). Also [I151](INCIDENTS.md#i151-a-rytm-mkii-mod-read-a-32-bit-kit-index-as-16-bits-and-played-the-old-sound-midi-engine). Also [I169](INCIDENTS.md#i169-a-project-reload-after-a-demand-loader-phase-left-the-dsp-frame-count-stopped-octabam-build-05), [I170](INCIDENTS.md#i170-dark-rev-picked-on-all-eight-tracks-while-modulation-was-loaded-stopped-the-dsp-octabam-build-05). A release check is itself a soak: octabam v0.5 tagged with 3 of 32 program changes unapplied and the long mixed soak unfinished ([I189](INCIDENTS.md#i189-v05-release-check-3-of-32-program-changes-were-not-applied-octabam)). {octabam-1123}

rules.title: Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A52. Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). Per-sample stores to the Digitakt II's DDR output buffer crashed the unit while the emulator was bit-identical, and a per-voice DDR path can cost ~10x its instruction count on the DN2. Render into L2 and copy once per block; read int16 samples two at a time. Incidents: [I17](INCIDENTS.md#i17-per-sample-stores-to-the-ddr-output-buffer-crashed-the-unit), [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-sharc}

rules.title: Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map.
rules.text: A53. Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. Emulators often map more than the hardware: Gearmulator maps the Machinedrum's flash at `0x0` and at `0x10000000`, but after the OS remaps CS0 nothing decodes the low window, so images with low-window pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit. Link through the address the running OS uses and scan images for the other one. Incidents: [I38](INCIDENTS.md#i38-low-window-flash-pointers-boot-in-the-emulator-and-hang-on-the-unit). `[hw]` {mdkit-docs} The DN2 emulator path reads low memory as zeros, which hid a wild read that froze units; dn2mk2 now traps every non-stock read below `0x40000000` in the emulator ([I65](INCIDENTS.md#i65-a-machine-kind-past-the-end-of-a-label-table-froze-digitone-ii-units)).

rules.title: Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state.
rules.text: A54. Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. On the Octatrack, undoing a synth module's install while tracks used it left Modwerk's loader in `needs-recovery`; its `recover` was refused even after the tracks were set back, and only a power cycle helped. A loader should refuse to remove a module that a track, kit or Part still references, and its recovery command must work from every state it can reach. `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz} Incident: [I75](INCIDENTS.md#i75-removing-a-synth-module-that-tracks-still-used-left-the-loader-stuck-in-recovery). A module's open window counts as use: Modwerk's base 0.7.5 refuses to undo a module whose window or key layer stock still holds, so a timed trial's automatic rollback failed until the window was closed; close every window and key layer a module opens on every path out, and give the rollback a path for an open one. `[hw]` {modwerk-1117} Incident: [I130](INCIDENTS.md#i130-a-timed-module-trial-could-not-roll-back-while-the-modules-window-was-open). Also [I149](INCIDENTS.md#i149-a-trial-rollback-timed-out-halfway-and-left-the-unit-in-recovery-modwerk).
