A loader's refusal can name the wrong resource: Modwerk's base reported a DSP claim meeting a delay buffer as "module memory" ([I129](INCIDENTS.md#i129-an-octatrack-restore-left-out-the-same-module-at-nearly-every-start), Later); find which check refused before you act on it. `[hw]` {modwerk-1120} Keeping a removed module's engine until the trial ends, and judging a page or menu as it will read once the module is out, are part of the same rule: a rollback that freed Analog BD's DSP engine left it silent until a power cycle, and a VECTOR Undo that saw the machine's own menu patch as a use stuck in recovery. `[hw]` {modwerk-1121} Incidents: [I178](INCIDENTS.md#i178-analog-bd-stayed-silent-after-a-rolled-back-trial-until-a-power-cycle-modwerk-base-079), [I179](INCIDENTS.md#i179-a-vector-trials-undo-left-the-loader-in-recovery-until-a-power-cycle-modwerk-0711-development-image).

rules.title: Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu.
rules.text: A55. Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. On the Digitakt II the stock mode switch stops the USB controller without a lock; a mod that used it to move from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI and back lost the unit from USB in cycle 5 of 20, and in cycle 11 even after holding the restart and parking the PHY. A cable replug did not help, only a power cycle. Reply to the host before you switch, space switches by seconds, keep the switch off by default, and run at least 50 cycles on a unit before you rely on it. `[hw]` {digikit-f123-hw} Incident: [I80](INCIDENTS.md#i80-a-usb-mode-take-over-left-a-digitakt-ii-off-the-bus-until-a-power-cycle). Later runs (2026-11-14): failures also came on release, and parking or rewriting the PHY around the switch made the loss about ten times more frequent; the base rate was 1 in 76 to 1 in 200. Stopping the controller is the risk itself, so prefer a design with no stop: digikit now adds an endpoint at boot (an unused EP2 OUT in USB AUDIO/MIDI). `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk} The Octatrack confirms it: a run-time descriptor change by Modwerk's base lost the unit from USB twice before its reconnect was hardened (A88, [I176](INCIDENTS.md#i176-a-usb-audio-undo-froze-the-panel-and-left-the-octatrack-off-usb-modwerk-0711-candidates)). `[hw]` {modwerk-1121}

rules.title: On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module.
rules.text: A56. On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. A frame interrupt entering about 150 µs late stopped the DSP's frame exchange at START; a USB capture (25-30 µs more) put it there, and 60 µs more in every frame interrupt moved it out again. Before you blame or clear a module, log the entry lateness of the frame interrupts before the stop, and guard the window (octabam's FRAME GUARD). `[hw]` {octabam-frameguard} Incident: [I82](INCIDENTS.md#i82-a-frame-interrupt-entering-about-150-µs-late-stopped-an-octatracks-dsp-frame-exchange). Also [I170](INCIDENTS.md#i170-dark-rev-picked-on-all-eight-tracks-while-modulation-was-loaded-stopped-the-dsp-octabam-build-05).

rules.title: On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook.
rules.text: A57. On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. A video player that read the CF card from a module's UI tick stopped the DSP frame exchange and froze the unit until a power cycle. `[hw]` {aeria-log} Incident: I83.

rules.title: A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording.
rules.text: A58. A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. On the Octatrack a delay effect left the output silent while the DSP still answered, and an own engine sent 3 of every 16 samples 32 samples late on main, cue and phones, which USB recordings (tapped earlier) never showed. `[hw]` {aeria-log} Incidents: I85, I86. Bit-exact is not the same as good: model27's first MAXSAW Sub matched its host model within 0.6 dB on a Model:Cycles and still sounded as buzz and crackle, because the design was wrong; listen on the unit before you call a sound done ([I125](INCIDENTS.md#i125-a-bit-exact-sub-oscillator-sounded-as-buzz-and-crackle-on-the-unit-model27-maxsaw-modelcycles)). An audible fault needs a cause shown with real audio: KYOTI's first fix for a pattern-jump pop, inferred in an emulator that streams no samples, changed nothing on the unit ([I119](INCIDENTS.md#i119-a-direct-jump-jump-popped-with-silence-tracks-on-the-emulators-inferred-fix-did-not-help)). `[hw]` {model27-maxsaw} {kyoti-1117}

rules.title: Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays.
rules.text: A59. Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. On the Digitakt mk1 the core export named `fw_amp_env` is the filter envelope; a voice switch-off keyed to it cut sounding notes on the unit. A SUS fix passed every check in FWD.L, which looked only at the playhead, and still stopped notes dead in ping-pong. Log a level, flag or envelope beside the output for a held note and a release, and check gain or audio in tests, not only position. `[hw]` {digicmi-037} Incidents: I89, I92. A mod that takes stock keys must list every stock mode and menu that uses them (SCALE menu, PTN/BANK LEDs) and test each ([I193](INCIDENTS.md#i193-drum-mode-kept-the-trig-keys-from-the-stock-scale-menu-and-covered-the-ptnbank-leds-digitone-mk1)). {drum-mode-1123}

rules.title: Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent.
rules.text: A60. Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. Stock validates at power-on before any loader restores its modules, on units without the mod, and after the user switches the track away, so a wrapper around the check does not help. On the Octatrack one byte outside its range dropped a whole bank at restart. Stay inside the stock range of the slot you reuse, or use a slot stock does not check. `[hw]` {modwerk-vector} Incident: I95. Also [I175](INCIDENTS.md#i175-quan-read-54-instead-of-11-on-entering-vari-varispeed-and-the-303-shared-spare-bytes-kyoti-varispeed) (the Octatrack's Part validator zeroes any `---` machine slot value from 128 up on every load, so a flag in bit 7 is lost).

rules.title: Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A61. Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). The init `0x40006c52` runs at boot and again from the USB tick, in interrupt context, after every controller reset, the firmware's own PHY watchdog reset included. Make no allocator or runtime calls there, check the stock descriptor (length, header, interface count) and leave USB stock when the check fails. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

rules.title: When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments.
rules.text: A62. When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. A hook may read registers the C ABI does not pass: on the Digitakt mk1 CC Names' hook reads d2, and a mod that called the site as plain C made labels read ERR. `[hw]` {modwerk-digiperform} Incident: I101.

rules.title: When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it.
rules.text: A63. When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. Windows writes an interface's registry values only at its first setup or for a new device revision; a replug does not. `[hw]` {modwerk-win-usb} Incident: I100.

rules.title: When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads.
rules.text: A64. When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. On the Model:Cycles the OS copies a previewed sound into one of two alternating preview buffers, so edits to the original never reached the preview notes. `[hw]` {model27-sample017} Incident: I88.

rules.title: Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost.
rules.text: A65. Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. A stopped unit reads far below a playing one (Octatrack MKII stock: about 45 % stopped, 60-75 % playing), so a check made while stopped lets through picks that overload the unit at PLAY. Use the last playing load and add the price of what is being added. `[hw]` {modwerk-1114} Incident: [I105](INCIDENTS.md#i105-module-picks-accepted-while-stopped-stalled-the-dsp-once-the-unit-played). Also [I140](INCIDENTS.md#i140-a-70--cpu-budget-greyed-out-every-heavier-machine-on-old-projects-modded-cycles-techno-edition). Count the UI too: one redraw request recomposes the whole screen, so rate-limit meters and remote screens ([I196](INCIDENTS.md#i196-a-compressors-gr-meter-raised-main-cpu-through-screen-repaints-synfact-comp-st-020-syntakt); Sidecar 0.4.3 capped its Rytm redraws for the same reason). {synfact-1123} On the Octatrack judge the longest frame, not the mean: renders drop past about 125-130 % of a frame, and a late frame entry stops the DSP for good ([I198](INCIDENTS.md#i198-tape-echo-froze-an-octatrack-mkii-after-the-frame-budget-was-exceeded-modwerk-0714-development-base), [I199](INCIDENTS.md#i199-a-pattern-change-made-a-late-frame-entry-and-the-octatrack-dsp-stopped-modwerk-08-development-twins)); on the Syntakt new machines reached 99 % AUDIO beside busy stock tracks ([I200](INCIDENTS.md#i200-new-machines-ran-the-syntakt-audio-cpu-to-99--synfact-sy-mnm-and-md-machinedrum)). {modwerk-1124} {synfact-1124}

rules.title: On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head.
rules.text: A66. On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. On the Octatrack MKII core B has no idle: its frame head is a word-by-word handshake with core A. octabam's demand-load copy at the frame head stalled the DSP in about two runs of three during play; the same copy at the frame end ran clean 12 of 12 times. `[hw]` {octabam-1115} Incident: [I108](INCIDENTS.md#i108-a-demand-load-during-play-stalled-an-octatracks-dsp-until-the-copy-moved-to-the-frames-end).

rules.title: Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block.
rules.text: A67. Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. On the Model:Cycles the OS chains a note and an immediate note-off into one batch, and the amp envelope ignores an end that arrives in the trig's own block, so with GATE on the note stays held. Raise the end in a later block, and check a "fixed" claim on the unit before writing it down (A31). `[hw]` {model27-chips} Incident: [I113](INCIDENTS.md#i113-a-previewed-sample-played-to-its-end-however-short-the-key-press-modelcycles).

rules.title: Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache.
rules.text: A68. Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. On the Analog Rytm MKII a mailbox written through the copyback data cache and pushed with `cpushl` alone was missing after the reset; evict the lines, turn the data cache off, then write. Gate a reset-only path on the reset cause (software reset), and remember that a short power flick can read as one. Extends A48. `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-link}

rules.title: Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM.
rules.text: A69. Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. A loader that fills a mod's displaced stock instructions from the running image reads what the flashed core or a companion already patched there, and the OS itself changes some image data before a card load (1,238 bytes on a Digitone mk1 1.44; Octatrack data in `0x400b9000..0x400e2324`). TELOS's card-loaded mods crashed the emulated Digitone until the build descriptor carried a stock shadow of every range the flashed build writes and the core kept its own copy of the image from boot. `[emu]` {telos-ot-1117} Incident: [I118](INCIDENTS.md#i118-card-loaded-mods-copied-stock-bytes-the-flashed-build-had-already-patched-digitone-mk1-octatrack).

rules.title: Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock.
rules.text: A70. Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. On the Octatrack the sample clock runs in audio frames, so a comparison at the boundary can flip by a frame on the unit while the emulator's exact clock never flips: Clyps' sequence loads came in a step off now and then. Land a whole tick early and cancel the old event with a margin, and do not take a tick-exact emulator pass as proof of timing (C10). `[hw]` {kyoti-1117} Incident: [I120](INCIDENTS.md#i120-a-landing-on-the-boundary-tick-was-exact-in-the-emulator-and-sometimes-a-step-off-on-the-unit).

rules.title: Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change.
rules.text: A71. Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. The Analog Rytm MKII keeps one lock per parameter and step and keeps the later write without an error, so two lanes or layers aimed at the same parameter lose one of them. Refuse such a setting before anything is written, as trig-seedr 0.6.0 does. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1117} Incident: [I126](INCIDENTS.md#i126-two-lock-lanes-on-one-parameter-lost-one-lanes-locks-trig-seedr-emulator).

rules.title: When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time.
rules.text: A72. When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. dn2mk2 v0.58 gave the Digitone II's five scale tables two more rows and raised the SCALE clamps; the chord MODEs keep a sixth per-scale table built at run time, which stayed short, and a chord MODE on a new scale stopped the unit with an exception. Find every reader of the index (static and in an emulator trace) and gate each one. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v058} Incident: [I138](INCIDENTS.md#i138-a-new-keyboard-scale-crashed-the-unit-in-a-chord-mode-dn2mk2-v058).

rules.title: A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response.
rules.text: A73. A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. On the Syntakt, a DJ filter at THRU that still sent the whole mix through the analog FX block made it sound harder and crackly on the author's unit; analog paths colour the sound even when the digital side is transparent. Bypass by restoring stock's routing, and listen on a unit. `[hw]` {stpm-1118} Incident: [I139](INCIDENTS.md#i139-a-neutral-filter-setting-still-coloured-the-mix-through-the-analog-fx-block-syntakt-performance-mods).

rules.title: Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`.
rules.text: A74. Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. trig-seedr's `take()` fell off its end without a return value; whether a roll was kept depended on a leftover register, and every emulator test passed by chance. A passing emulator run proves nothing about undefined behaviour. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1118} Incident: [I142](INCIDENTS.md#i142-a-function-without-a-return-value-passed-the-emulator-by-chance-trig-seedr-070).

rules.title: On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig.
rules.text: A75. On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. The VCA (`0x400a9430`) cuts the level in a trig's block and jumps at the attack; model27's TERRA clicked at trigs until 0.2 hid the trig and attack flags for the VCA call only and put them back before PUNCH. Test retrigs at short DECAY on a unit. `[hw]` {model27-1118} Incident: [I144](INCIDENTS.md#i144-an-added-machine-clicked-at-trigs-through-the-stock-vca-model27-terra-modelcycles).

rules.title: Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB.
rules.text: A76. Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. The analog calibration record ("RBOZ", `0x22d40` bytes) sits at NOR `0x300000` with its backup at `0x340000`; the OS is written from `0x80000`, so a container longer than `0x280000` bytes would reach the record, and an invalid record asks for a warm-up calibration at boot. `[doc]` {digikit-st-1118} Conflict: [O34](CONFLICTS.md).

rules.title: Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record.
rules.text: A77. Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. A byte that is zero in a test project may be a feature the project does not use: octabam's PATTERN MUTE kept its layer in byte 40 of the Octatrack's audio track record, the low byte of the one-shot trig mask, and an unmute deleted one-shot trigs on a unit. Prefer a side file or RAM the stock code never names. `[hw]` {octabam-pmute-1118} Incident: [I146](INCIDENTS.md#i146-pattern-mute-stored-its-layer-in-the-one-shot-trig-mask-octabam). Also [I165](INCIDENTS.md#i165-a-flex-src-page-pasted-onto-a-303-track-left-a-303-with-flexs-numbers-kyoti-v18bc) (a page paste writes the machine byte but not a mod's signature beside it), [I175](INCIDENTS.md#i175-quan-read-54-instead-of-11-on-entering-vari-varispeed-and-the-303-shared-spare-bytes-kyoti-varispeed) (two features of one project parked data in the same spare NEIGHBOR bytes; keep the meaning of a parked value in the bytes, not only in RAM that a Part apply forgets).

rules.title: When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time.
rules.text: A78. When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. On the Digitakt II, core 1.1's 191 bytes of kit data ran into the last 48 bytes of the kit record that Modwerk's project archive uses; saving a kit-data module zeroed the archive, and a setting came back off after a power cycle. `[hw]` {modwerk-1118} Incident: [I147](INCIDENTS.md#i147-kit-data-overlapped-the-project-archive-a-module-setting-came-back-off-after-a-power-cycle-modwerk).

rules.title: Test every edit path on a pattern, bank and project far from the defaults, not only on A01.
rules.text: A79. Test every edit path on a pattern, bank and project far from the defaults, not only on A01. The Digitone keeps one set of track edit objects per pattern; Drum Mode wrote through A01's set, so its recordings went to A01 on any other pattern, and all 119 emulator checks passed because every one ran on A01. Run each recording or editing test on at least one pattern of another bank (H02, say) and check on the unit that the data lands where it plays. When a bug shows only on the unit, a debug build that prints the mod's view of the data on screen finds it quickly. `[hw]` {drum-mode-1119} Incident: [I153](INCIDENTS.md#i153-live-recorded-beats-went-into-pattern-a01-every-emulator-test-had-run-on-a01-drum-mode-08081). Also [I164](INCIDENTS.md#i164-a-303-voice-lost-its-last-step-popped-and-played-a-blip-at-part-and-pattern-changes-kyoti-blackpyramids_303), [I141](INCIDENTS.md#i141-drum-modes-lane-strip-disappeared-on-page-switches-digitone-mk1) (Later: found on H02).

rules.title: A parameter a mod sets right before it plays a note may be smoothed by the OS: set the smoothing state too, or set the value a few blocks earlier, and listen on a unit.
rules.text: A80. A parameter a mod sets right before it plays a note may be smoothed by the OS: set the smoothing state too, or set the value a few blocks earlier, and listen on a unit. On the Model:Cycles the audio side smooths every parameter target per block and snaps the state only when a note brings another sound, so a chord shape set just before a live note slid in from the old chord. An emulator check of the parameter word does not hear the slide. `[hw]` {model27-1120} Incident: [I160](INCIDENTS.md#i160-a-chord-set-just-before-a-live-note-slid-in-from-the-old-chord-model27-chord-joy-modelcycles).

rules.title: A sound a mod starts without a trig must obey the track's mute itself.
rules.text: A81. A sound a mod starts without a trig must obey the track's mute itself. Stock mutes may only hold back the sequencer's trigs: on the Model:Cycles a drone started without a trig kept sounding on a muted track, even across a pattern change. Stop or fade such a voice on mute and start it again on unmute. `[?]` {mcte-1120} Incident: [I162](INCIDENTS.md#i162-a-drone-kept-sounding-on-a-muted-track-modded-cycles-techno-edition-atmos-before-v19).

rules.title: On the Octatrack, read the Part a track is playing from stock's per-track pair (`0x8000182a` / `0x80001832` + t), not from the UI or engine Part.
rules.text: A82. On the Octatrack, read the Part a track is playing from stock's per-track pair (`0x8000182a` / `0x80001832` + t), not from the UI or engine Part. The UI Part and the engine Part move about 7 ticks before a switch applies, while a carried track keeps the old Part until its own first trig. A voice that asked the UI Part lost its last step, popped and played early notes on an MKI. Read settings that stock re-stages only at a trig (SETUP) from the scheduled pattern's Part too. `[hw]` {kyoti-1120} Incident: [I164](INCIDENTS.md#i164-a-303-voice-lost-its-last-step-popped-and-played-a-blip-at-part-and-pattern-changes-kyoti-blackpyramids_303).

rules.title: Test the smallest legal build as well as the full one.
rules.text: A83. Test the smallest legal build as well as the full one. When a platform loads optional parts (machines, modules, banks), also build and run a composition with zero machines, one module or no optional part. An early return for an empty list can skip the set-up the other parts depend on: a Syntakt bank with one module and no machine showed ERR labels on a unit. `[hw]` {synfact-1120} Incident: [I171](INCIDENTS.md#i171-a-third-lfo-page-showed-err-labels-when-the-bank-held-only-modules-synfact-core-211-syntakt).

rules.title: When you patch a stock routine for audio tracks, find its MIDI-track twin and patch and test that too.
rules.text: A84. When you patch a stock routine for audio tracks, find its MIDI-track twin and patch and test that too. The Octatrack's LIVE erase calls one worker for audio tracks and a separate one for MIDI tracks with the same arguments; KYOTI's fix for erased trigless locks hooked only the audio worker, and on an MKI MIDI steps stayed lit. Add a MIDI case to every check of a sequencer or lock fix. `[hw]` {octatrack-kyoti-fw-1121} Incident: [I173](INCIDENTS.md#i173-a-fix-for-erased-trigless-locks-covered-audio-tracks-only-kyoti-erase_empty_trigless_locks).

rules.title: A mod machine that stock sees as another machine must handle both edges of a machine switch itself.
rules.text: A85. A mod machine that stock sees as another machine must handle both edges of a machine switch itself. On the Octatrack a machine stored as FLEX is FLEX to FLEX for stock, which then re-stages nothing until the next trig: the new machine played FLEX's numbers (silent) on an MKI. Leaving it, the old renderer still ran until the next trig and played the hidden FLEX voice. Re-stage the track's live bytes when your machine is chosen, render silence until the next trig when it is left, and test every switch from the machine chooser with the sequencer running and no trig in between. `[hw]` {octatrack-kyoti-fw-1121} Incidents: [I172](INCIDENTS.md#i172-a-303-chosen-on-a-flex-track-was-silent-until-switched-away-and-back-kyoti-v18bc-rc1), [I174](INCIDENTS.md#i174-a-track-that-stopped-being-a-303-played-a-burst-of-its-flex-sample-kyoti-v18bc-rc2). Also [I195](INCIDENTS.md#i195-stock-rytm-samples-played-under-sidecar-machines-rytm-firmware-044050) (stock's sample layer kept playing under Sidecar machines on the Rytm). {sidecar-mods-1123}

rules.title: Take key ids from the target device's own decoder table, never from another model.
rules.text: A86. Take key ids from the target device's own decoder table, never from another model. The id in a key event is the firmware's key index; on the Digitakt II and Digitone II it equals the panel code, on the Syntakt it does not (YES 12, NO 13, RIGHT 17 against 10, 12, 15). A list page that compared events with the Digitakt II ids swallowed NO on a Syntakt and froze the unit until a power cycle. Keep key ids in per-device data, and let an unknown key fall through to the stock handler so NO always leaves your page. `[hw]` (symptom) / `[emu]` (cause) {digikit-1121} Incident: [I181](INCIDENTS.md#i181-the-digikit-modules-page-froze-a-syntakt-it-used-the-digitakt-ii-key-ids).

rules.title: Place card data by the smallest capacity the firmware accepts, and check the capacity the driver reports before you touch the card.
rules.text: A87. Place card data by the smallest capacity the firmware accepts, and check the capacity the driver reports before you touch the card. The emulators model the 32 GB eMMC (`0x2e1a000` sectors), but a Syntakt carried a 1.82 GiB part (`0x3a4000` sectors, the smallest row of the firmware's part table), so a store placed for the larger card lay beyond its end. Read the driver's capacity word at run time (the getter returns `0xFFFFFFFF` until the driver is ready: decide nothing then), refuse the area when the card is too small, and keep a fixed area rather than one computed from the capacity. `[hw]` {digikit-1121} Incident: [I182](INCIDENTS.md#i182-the-first-digikit-store-on-a-syntakt-lay-beyond-the-units-card).

rules.title: When a mod changes the USB descriptors at run time, bring the controller back from a context that keeps running, check that it attached, and keep every other host client off the device while it reconnects.
rules.text: A88. When a mod changes the USB descriptors at run time, bring the controller back from a context that keeps running, check that it attached, and keep every other host client off the device while it reconnects. On the Octatrack, Modwerk's USB Audio package makes the base leave the bus and come back with new descriptors. When only the UI tick could switch the controller back on, an Undo froze the panel and left the unit off USB until a cold start; a later build lost the unit when the controller ran but never attached, and only a check after three seconds with one retry fixed it. A paired browser tab that opened the vendor interface first rolled trials back. Re-enable the controller from the frame interrupt or a timer as a fallback, read the attach status before you start the host deadline, close every other client (browser pages, other tools) before a test, and run every layout and Undo on a unit with the host you ship for. `[hw]` {modwerk-1121} Incidents: [I176](INCIDENTS.md#i176-a-usb-audio-undo-froze-the-panel-and-left-the-octatrack-off-usb-modwerk-0711-candidates), [I177](INCIDENTS.md#i177-a-paired-browser-tab-rolled-back-usb-audio-trials-at-the-reconnect-modwerk). Also [I192](INCIDENTS.md#i192-a-small-usb-staging-transfer-went-unconfirmed-and-a-usb-audio-trial-rolled-back-at-the-reconnect-modwerk-windows) (the first claim of the returning interface can fail; retry it under the trial's lock).

rules.title: On the Octatrack, do not change which effects the DSP holds while a project loads; plan only from the complete effect map.
rules.text: A89. On the Octatrack, do not change which effects the DSP holds while a project loads; plan only from the complete effect map. Modwerk's DSP manager began binding while the bank and Parts were still loading and stalled the DSP on the first load after modules were restored from the card; a gate that starts no new plan until the load has published its effect map fixed it. Test the first project load after a power-on restore, not only loads after a USB install. `[hw]` {modwerk-1121} Incident: [I180](INCIDENTS.md#i180-a-project-load-after-a-card-restore-stalled-the-dsp-modwerk-079-development-base).

rules.title: Load from the card only when a sound needs it, never on every knob or modulation step.
rules.text: A90. Load from the card only when a sound needs it, never on every knob or modulation step. A Sidecar user machine that asked for its sample on every knob change loaded several samples a second when an LFO moved the knob, and a Pi 5 reset again and again; 1.0.1 loads only on a trig. Keep large files short for the same reason. `[hw]` {sidecar-machines-1122} Incidents: [I186](INCIDENTS.md#i186-a-user-machine-that-loaded-samples-between-hits-reset-a-sidecar-pi-5-wavesurfer-100).

rules.title: Never include, commit or publish Elektron firmware
rules.text: B1. Never include, commit or publish Elektron firmware (original or modified), dumps or decompressed code. Ship patches that carry only the author's bytes plus hashes of the expected stock bytes. The user supplies the stock OS file. `[doc]` {elekloader-readme} {elektron-firmware-tool} {digitakt-ii-research} {dn2-cfw}

rules.title: Identify the stock file by hash (SHA-256) and refuse anything else
rules.text: B2. Identify the stock file by hash (SHA-256) and refuse anything else - modified files and other OS versions are rejected, not "adapted". `[doc]` {digitakt-ii-research} {synthack-os} {syntakt-workbench}

rules.title: Say what you are.
rules.text: B3. Say what you are. Mods are unofficial, unsupported, not affiliated with Elektron, and used at the user's own risk (may brick; Elektron's wording: modifications "may affect warranty coverage" and may prevent future updates - it does not explicitly say the warranty is void, so do not claim more than that). Put that in every README. `[doc]` all mod READMEs {elektronauts-policy}

rules.title: Respect the manufacturer's forum policy.
rules.text: B4. Respect the manufacturer's forum policy. Elektron's post of 2026-09-16 (updated 09-17) forbids, on Elektronauts and Elektron's official social platforms, sharing, requesting or linking to files, tools, repositories or instructions for modifying firmware, and developing or distributing firmware/hardware that makes unauthorized use of Elektron's IP; such posts are removed. General discussion stays allowed. It applies to legacy machines as well. Do not post mod links there. This aggregator lives on GitHub and links only to metadata. `[doc]` {elektronauts-policy}

rules.title: Never assume an old stock OS can be fetched later.
rules.text: B6. Never assume an old stock OS can be fetched later. Elektron no longer lists old firmware (downgrades can cause errors; older versions only by email) and community archives are incomplete - ask the user to keep their own stock files for every OS they flash, and record their SHA-256. `[doc]` {em-firmware-list}

rules.title: Respect each project's contribution policy - for AI agents too.
rules.text: B5. Respect each project's contribution policy - for AI agents too. elk-herd's README says issues, comments and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected. Before opening an issue or PR in someone else's repo, read the README/CONTRIBUTING and disclose AI help where the project expects it. `[doc]` {elk-herd}

rules.title: Prove that what you ship contains none of the manufacturer's bytes.
rules.text: B7. Prove that what you ship contains none of the manufacturer's bytes. Overtone's patcher carries copy instructions over the user's own file plus its own bytes, and checks that no 16-byte run of its own bytes occurs in the stock OS. That turns B1 from a promise into a test. `[doc]` {overtone}

rules.title: One mod = one OS version.
rules.text: C1. One mod = one OS version. Addresses and stock bytes are version-specific (hash-pinned). A mod for Digitakt mk1 1.53 is refused on 1.54; Digitakt II 1.17 addresses do not carry to 1.18+. Porting = find every address again. Keep a separate build per OS version. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {digitakt2-perform}

rules.title: Test ladder, in order:
rules.text: C2. Test ladder, in order: build -> lint -> emulator cold boot compared against stock -> a unit you can recover. A verifying build is well-formed, not proven to work. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.title: Record the test state of every build
rules.text: C3. Record the test state of every build as `hw` / `emu` / `untested` in the project metadata. Several projects ship builds that are lint-clean but "not yet run on a unit". `[doc]` {digislicer} {digichroma} {digitakt2-perform}

rules.title: Emulators do not prove real-time DSP behaviour.
rules.text: C4. Emulators do not prove real-time DSP behaviour. The earlier digikit README said "no audio"; the current ElekLabs Features that cross the ColdFire-SHARC boundary need both processors emulated together, or a unit: dn2mk2's BOUNCE passed a ColdFire-only gate and failed on units. On the Octatrack the DSP AMP envelope restart only showed as clicks on a unit. Incidents: [I58](INCIDENTS.md#i58-a-wavetable-machine-clicked-on-every-note), [I66](INCIDENTS.md#i66-a-feature-that-crosses-coldfire-and-dsp-passed-the-gate-and-failed-on-units). An emulator that plays no samples cannot find the cause of an audible fault: KYOTI's first fix for an Octatrack jump pop, inferred there, changed nothing on the unit, and a render with real audio then showed the hard voice kill ([I119](INCIDENTS.md#i119-a-direct-jump-jump-popped-with-silence-tracks-on-the-emulators-inferred-fix-did-not-help)). README has ColdFire + SHARC+ running together with audio, but the DSP "does not run in real time yet", and dn2mk2 reports the emulators do not model the two chips' timing. DSP overruns show up only on a unit. `[doc]` {digikit-old} Incidents: [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x). Also [I143](INCIDENTS.md#i143-gearmulators-dsp56300-jit-misexecuted-cmpm-and-xy-half-writes-gearmulator-md-mm).

rules.title: Windows:
rules.text: C5. Windows: the DN2 tooling needs an m68k objdump; use WSL. `[doc]` {dn2-firmware-explore}

rules.title: Report honestly.
rules.text: C6. Report honestly. "Nothing counts as working until it has run on my unit" is the standard the more careful authors apply. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

rules.title: Porting to a new OS version = re-locating, not re-applying.
rules.text: C7. Porting to a new OS version = re-locating, not re-applying. Diff decoded content, check bootstrap and updater separately, re-find every patch by masked pattern (`find`/`expect`) and pin the build by hash; inspect unfamiliar sections first. (Digitone II 1.11 vs 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes.) `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions} {dn2-cfw-release-history}

rules.title: Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken.
rules.text: C8. Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines). Run view opening and closing through the native push, compose, tick and cleanup, not through doubles: on the Syntakt a view a mod pushes is composed and ticked before the push returns, and stock's deferred cleanup can drop a close raised then, so Synfact's ARP pages stayed blank on the unit while stubbed tests passed. Publish a view's state before you push it. `[hw]` {synfact-1117} Incident: [I115](INCIDENTS.md#i115-arp-pages-stayed-blank-or-lost-their-keys-after-permanent-mute-syntakt).

rules.title: After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route.
rules.text: C9. After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route. Old data meets new code only on the unit: a DN2 project with a stored row count out of range crashed stock and modded builds, Octatrack projects stalled when an effect layout changed, dn2mk2's MD/MM tracks went silent after an install, armio's USB audio repeated after a project change, and Overtone 1.0 broke the next USB update. A release test opens an old project and a stock project, changes project once, and installs the following build with Transfer. Incidents: [I2](INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I13](INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change), [I21](INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install), [I22](INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I28](INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). [I73](INCIDENTS.md#i73-an-old-project-stopped-all-sound-on-a-sample-machine-mod) (an old project silenced every track), [I77](INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (mod data lost at a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT). `[hw]` Also [I154](INCIDENTS.md#i154-a-project-load-dropped-installed-effects-from-the-next-starts-list-modwerk-octatrack-base-up-to-078) (Octatrack: a project load replaced Modwerk's effect map, and installed effects were refused at the next start).

rules.title: Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers.
rules.text: C10. Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers. Call stock routines in the emulator and compare with what they must return (complex-ping's check found that its SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply); measure one timing per project on the unit and carry the ratio (2x on the DT2 for DDR-reading code, 7-12x in one digimod case, a hard stop that overshot 3x as far). An emulator that agrees with itself proves nothing about silicon. The display is part of this: digikit's emulator showed intro frames upright that the panel showed upside down. Check one asymmetric picture on the unit before trusting the emulator's orientation. Pointers too: a Digitakt II UI pointer that digikit's emulator filled stayed 0 on the unit; find screens from what the OS drew, not from UI object pointers ([I106](INCIDENTS.md#i106-a-ui-pointer-the-emulator-filled-stayed-0-on-a-digitakt-ii)). Incidents: [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x), [I37](INCIDENTS.md#i37-a-sharc-emulator-shifted-every-fractional-multiply), [I53](INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {digimod} {dn2-skill-md} The same holds for event fields: Modwerk read a knob's own push-button byte as FUNC, and an emulator reference screen lacked markers the unit draws. Incidents: [I55](INCIDENTS.md#i55-a-knobs-own-push-button-byte-was-read-as-func), [I56](INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). State an emulator's cost per emulated second (instruction budget divided by instructions per second), not per run: trig-seedr read 5 emulated seconds as one and overstated an idle cost five times ([I128](INCIDENTS.md#i128-idle-cpu-cost-overstated-five-times-an-instruction-budget-read-as-one-second-trig-seedr-analog-emu)).

rules.title: Every failure or test on a unit becomes an incident, and every incident that teaches something general becomes a rule.
rules.text: C11. Every failure or test on a unit becomes an incident, and every incident that teaches something general becomes a rule. Record it in [INCIDENTS.md](INCIDENTS.md) with the next free I-number: unit and OS, what was seen, the cause and how it was found (measured, read from code, emulator, unknown), the fix, the status and the evidence level. Then either add a rule here or add the incident to the rule it confirms, and mark the fact in the device page with `(I<n>)`. Rules grow from tests, not from opinion.

rules.title: Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list.
rules.text: C12. Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes} A test failure right after a restart can be stock's boot too: in digikit's emulator the Digitakt II dropped stock MidiRpc requests while its boot intro ran, which failed a storage test (not yet checked on a unit); wait for the firmware's own ready state before the first request ([I114](INCIDENTS.md#i114-stock-midirpc-requests-were-lost-while-the-boot-intro-still-ran)).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Prefer events over raw patch sites.
rules.text: D1. Prefer events over raw patch sites. The core mod owns the shared hook sites; subscribe via its event bus, do not patch core-owned sites. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Patch whole instructions only.
rules.text: D2. Patch whole instructions only. A site that ends mid-instruction is refused. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: No overlapping claims.
rules.text: D3. No overlapping claims. No two mods may patch or claim overlapping bytes, memory or named resources. Declare resources (`sysex:`, `settings:`, `drive:`, `ui:`, `machine:` names; other memory as regions). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Prefix every global symbol with the mod id, make internals `static`.
rules.text: D4. Prefix every global symbol with the mod id, make internals `static`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} Incidents: [I41](INCIDENTS.md#i41-a-label-defined-twice-resolved-to-the-wrong-file).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Let the linker place code and data, never hard-code addresses.
rules.text: D5. Let the linker place code and data, never hard-code addresses. Sections allowed: `.run`, `.fast`, `.bss`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them.
rules.text: D6. Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them. Range 4-127. Claim `machine:<id>`. Known claims (Digitakt mk1, core 2.1): 4 = NEIGHBOR, 5 = DIGISLICER. Pick a free ID, then register it in [`devices/digitakt.md`](devices/digitakt.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} D6b. Digitone II machine IDs: synths 5-31 and filters 6-31 are separate namespaces, permanent, and there is no allocator - agree IDs with other authors before shipping; saved sounds of an absent mod keep their ID and show as MISSING. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2} D6c. Analog Rytm MKII mod machines take the hidden slots 34-43 (from elekloader core-ar2 0.13 also the TEST slots 44-52), claimed as `machine:<slot>`. Kits store the slot; on a build without the mod the kit loads it as DISABLE. elekloader refuses two mods with the same slot, and Modwerk also records claims on its agent board. Each slot has fixed knob positions, so give meaning to a sound index, not to a knob letter. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Do not mix format 1 (whole build) with format 2 (linkable) mods
rules.text: D7. Do not mix format 1 (whole build) with format 2 (linkable) mods - whole builds cannot be combined. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Keep the audio interrupt handlers (`ev_render_in/out`) short.
rules.text: D8. Keep the audio interrupt handlers (`ev_render_in/out`) short. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Licence everything with an SPDX identifier and matching file headers.
rules.text: D9. Licence everything with an SPDX identifier and matching file headers. The ecosystem is mostly GPL-2.0-or-later (elekloader family); MIT and AGPL-3.0 also occur. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Disclose AI-generated code
rules.text: D10. Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: An address that exists or maps onto another is not thereby free.
rules.text: D11. An address that exists or maps onto another is not thereby free. Prove an area unused (stock data pointers, caches, DMA buffers, boot ROM sharing) before placing code or data there; an unreferenced-looking L2 block once stopped a unit from starting. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {dn2-skill-firmware} Incidents: [I19](INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit), [I20](INCIDENTS.md#i20-mod-code-at-a-free-address-crashed-projects-with-certain-samples), [I29](INCIDENTS.md#i29-dsp-scratch-at-84-and-up-hung-the-unit), [I33](INCIDENTS.md#i33-module-state-on-a-load-meter-counter-gave-a-jittery-pitch), [I48](INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit). Also [I145](INCIDENTS.md#i145-many-stock-samples-overwrote-synfacts-resident-core-and-crashed-it-at-boot-synfact).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Budget voices, not tracks.
rules.text: D12. Budget voices, not tracks. Dynamic voice allocation can need far more voices than tracks; guard the DSP frame time and expose a CPU indicator. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports} Incidents: [I24](INCIDENTS.md#i24-a-granular-engine-froze-the-ui-at-low-pitch).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Keep a trap register in your agent file.
rules.text: D13. Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`); on the Octatrack `0x80000012` (MIDI tracks shown) is a long, so a byte read always gives 0 ([I123](INCIDENTS.md#i123-a-byte-read-of-a-long-flag-hid-the-midi-tracks)). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire} A software-started ColdFire eDMA channel runs one minor loop unless it is linked to itself (ELINK), as stock's channel 47 is ([I197](INCIDENTS.md#i197-an-edma-block-without-a-self-link-moved-only-its-first-16-bytes-synfact-stereo-tracks-syntakt)). {synfact-1123}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Fail closed.
rules.text: D14. Fail closed. If any anchor (stock hash, symbol, instruction pattern) does not match, build nothing or boot stock - never patch "close enough". `[?]` {dubspot} {elekloader-format}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Disclose AI assistance
rules.text: D15. Disclose AI assistance where the community expects it (several projects require it; elk-herd rejects AI-generated issues/PRs). `[doc]` {dubspot} {elk-herd}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: A hook on a hot path must cost nothing while its mod is idle: test first, then call.
rules.text: D16. A hook on a hot path must cost nothing while its mod is idle: test first, then call. dnfw's LFO4 hooked `memcpy`, `memset` and the per-frame LFO evaluators, and paid a call on every copy and frame even with no fourth LFO in use. Playing alone it was inaudible, but SAVE PROJECT while a pattern played stuttered until the save ended (whole-project serialise +6.3 %). The fix was an early exit in the stub (empty table or a block smaller than a sound: straight back) and skipping an idle LFO; stock then saved clean. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Projects store values by slot, not by table row.
rules.text: E1. Projects store values by slot, not by table row. Details and the P-lock trap in [`devices/digitone-2.md`](devices/digitone-2.md). Moving the OS parameter table does not by itself change the saved format. New rows are only safe if they follow the author's growth rules (`docs/parameter-table-growth.md` in dn2-cfw - not yet read by us). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Persist a mod's own sound parameters through the stock edit event, not a writer of your own.
rules.text: E2. Persist a mod's own sound parameters through the stock edit event, not a writer of your own. On the Digitone II (1.11) an edit is written into the stored sound record at once, so unsaved edits survive a power cycle; the writer is `Sound::updateMirror` (`0x4004ca80`). dnfw's LFO4 values did not survive until its setter sent the stock whole-sound event (`SoundConfigChangedInfo`) through the sound's holder; `updateMirror` then re-serialised the sound with LFO4's lane. Confirmed on the unit: unsaved LFO4 edits survive a power cycle, and SAVE PROJECT stores them. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change.
rules.text: E3. Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change. Stock trusts what it loads: the DN2's song LOAD copies a stored row count without a check (21,503 rows instead of at most 99 crashed stock and modded builds alike), and an Octatrack select value outside its count stalled the sequencer on first play after an effect's layout changed. Clamp every count and enum a mod writes; when a build changes a stored layout, rewrite old projects' values on load. Incidents: [I2](INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I28](INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Store a mod's data only where it differs from the defaults.
rules.text: E4. Store a mod's data only where it differs from the defaults. Every record a mod adds is written and checked on each save and load: Synfact's ARP mod sealed a carrier for every kit even with default settings, and a user saw project load and save slow down; leaving default carriers absent cut the serialization by 81 % in the emulator. Let "absent" mean "default", remove a record when it returns to default, and keep old projects readable. Incidents: [I50](INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save). `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT.
rules.text: E5. Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT. A mod's companion can pass explicit save/reload while remaining stale in the unsaved working backup. On DN2 1.11, native settings updates bypass the whole-project serializer; armio's sample extension missed that path. Exercise load, change and unload through real notifications, serialize the working backup, then restore into a fresh emulator without retaining its heap. Keep current-project ownership/UID checks and the same lock as pool mutations; do not replace a saved checkpoint or add storage work to the shutdown interrupt. A passing replay does not prove physical power-loss recovery or that a frozen task completed its queue. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incidents: [I77](INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (Digitakt mk1: a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT drops kit spare bytes that LOAD PROJECT keeps), [I52](INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot), [I116](INCIDENTS.md#i116-a-step-order-mod-missed-two-readers-of-its-state-syntakt) (Syntakt: a power cycle without a save restores kits from mirror slots that only `KitActive::kitChanged` re-encodes).

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F1. Back up first, via Elektron Transfer and by re-reading the destination pattern; abort if the backup fails. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F2. Allowlist the exact OS builds you have tested; refuse others. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F3. Change only the bytes that must change, then read back and byte-compare. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio} Incident: [I201](INCIDENTS.md#i201-a-pattern-write-to-a-blank-analog-four-pattern-failed-its-readback-on-the-kit-byte-digi-roll-studio) (the unit rewrote a blank pattern's kit byte; the compare caught it). {digi-roll-1124}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F4. Work on throwaway projects while a format is still being decoded; trust only mappings with a hardware-confirmed level (SYXGRID level A). `[doc]` {syxgrid}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F5. Never run parsers across device generations (Digitone mk1 device ID 0x0D vs Digitone II, Analog Four gen-1 vs gen-2). `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F6. Treat file-write / delete commands of the +Drive API as dangerous: only single-chunk writes were hardware-verified; move/copy/delete are not implemented anywhere we know. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F7. Close every other application on the port (Transfer, Overbridge, DNX) before a client run, and check every reply's length. With Overbridge holding the port replies were cut at exactly 885 bytes; with Transfer open a preset list showed 35 of 256. Incidents: [I9](INCIDENTS.md#i9-a-second-application-on-the-port-corrupts-sysex-replies). `[hw]`

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F8. A mod that sends its own SysEx from the device must never send between the parts of a stock multi-message dump: wait on the OS's own SysEx-in-progress state, not only on the MIDI lock, and bound the wait. On the receiving side, a report missing during a long stock transfer is not a lost link. `[emu]` {sidecar-mods-1116} Incident: [I111](INCIDENTS.md#i111-a-mods-own-sysex-report-cut-a-stock-pattern-dump-on-an-analog-rytm). Full loop, spec questions and triage in [`common/agent-workflow.md`](common/agent-workflow.md). Short form:

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G1. Ask the spec questions in one round before building. G2. Reproduce every bug as a failing test with a stock control before fixing it.

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G3. Test what the hardware consumes, never by reading back what your own patch wrote. G4. Run emulator and static checks before every flash; the unit should only judge sound and feel. G5. Flash one clearly named image with its SHA-256 and a list of what to try; never overwrite older images.

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G6. After two failed flashes on the same problem stop and restate goal, proven facts, unknowns and options. G7. Ask the user before cloning or installing anything.

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G8. Keep levels honest: measure worst cases, add no unrequested gain compensation, clamp audio output, never read memory you did not write. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-md} {dn2-skill-workflow} Incidents (G8): [I8](INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan), [I72](INCIDENTS.md#i72-a-drum-machine-mod-played-silent-hits-after-power-up-and-misread-stocks-voice-start) (a stock flag found set at power-up; a wrapper that passed two of three arguments), [I78](INCIDENTS.md#i78-the-first-play-after-power-on-started-a-tracks-recorder) (a staged record start read after power-on), [I185](INCIDENTS.md#i185-a-flex-take-level-built-in-by-ear-was-12-db-too-loud-dn2mk2-v063-v064) (a gain judged by ear on another build shipped 12 dB too high; measure the level on the build you ship, with fixed levels and a recorded comparison).

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.title: Repo conventions to adopt from elekloader's AGENTS.md:
rules.text: G10. Repo conventions to adopt from elekloader's AGENTS.md: never weaken a check to make a test pass; a skipped test is not a pass - report which tests ran; keep device facts in profile files; check whether a core event already exists before adding a code site; keep byte-exact writer tests. `[doc]` {elekloader-agents}

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.title: DSP rules the emulators cannot check
rules.text: G9. DSP rules the emulators cannot check (Digitone II, each reportedly silenced or crashed a real unit): whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock instruction encodings only (incl. sign bits of negative shift immediates), PRM loop/DAG/branch rules, no L2 above `0x200B0000`, never read unwritten DDR (power-on NaN), preserve registers at hooks (clobbered R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio), count memory accesses not instructions. Details and addresses in [`devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md). `[hw]` {dn2-skill-sharc} Incidents: [I8](INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan), [I25](INCIDENTS.md#i25-clobbering-r8-at-the-fx-bus-mixer-hook-lost-all-audio), [I26](INCIDENTS.md#i26-a-boot-block-of-8n4-bytes-left-the-unit-silent), [I27](INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip).

goals.goal: Every device has a recovery path somebody has actually used
goals.status: ✅ DN2, DT mk1, Octatrack, A4/Rytm MK1; 🟢 DT2 (one report, OS 1.16); documented for Syntakt (SyntHack) and Heat +FX (official). 🟢 Digitone mk1 (one report, OS 1.44). Every phase-1 device now has a used or official recovery path.

goals.goal: An honest load/headroom measure per device (rules A25, A34, A37)
goals.status: ✅ DT2 (idle-task measure on a unit), DN2 (elekloader busy meter, with the "busy is not headroom" caveat). 🟢 DT mk1: Digi CMI's render meter (PIT0 timer) read about 85 % right after boot on OS 1.54, nearly all stock render (2026-11-12). ❓ Syntakt (two readings conflict, O3). ⬜ Heat +FX, Digitone mk1 voice CPU.
goals.moved_by: T4, T9, T10; tests H15, H17

goals.status: At least six phase-1 boxes use MCF5441x-family ColdFires (DT, DN, DT2, DN2, Syntakt, Heat +FX); DT2 and DN2 share the SHARC and 85 % of its functions. Many rules were found on one box and are only assumed for the others (e.g. A39 USB, A28 cache write-back).
goals.moved_by: T3, T12, T19; tests H7, H12-H15, H17

goals.goal: Emulators you can trust for more than "it boots"
goals.status: ✅ known gaps: no memory stalls (device cycles ~2x emulator), no pipeline model, EMAC fractional-mode bugs in stock Unicorn. 🟢 CPU readings: analog-emu's unit timing comes within about 3.6 points of the Rytm MKII for 9 of 11 builds when the Overbridge stream is emulated too (elkbench, 2026-11-12). ❓ digikit: real-time DSP audio.

Every mod pins one OS version; address translation between versions was done ad hoc; since 2026-11-11 `scripts/anchor_translate.py` does it from two user-supplied images (T6, T8). Good news for DSP work: the SHARC sections are **byte-identical** between DT2 1.16 and 1.17 and between DN2 1.11 and 1.12 (digikit finding 53), so only the ColdFire side moves.

goals.goal: Official numbers instead of guesses (MIDI CC/NRPN tables, startup menus)

goals.goal: Talk to every unit the same way (SysEx dumps, the RPC, device ids, project files)

goals.moved_by: T18, T22; tests H1, H2, H3, H18

goals.goal: Mods that coexist (with each other, with Overbridge, with stock projects)

hypotheses.inference: Each unit has three different ids: SysEx device byte, product id, Overbridge USB id. Expected: DT2 `0x14` / `0x2A` / USB `0x0B2B`; DT1 `0x0A` / `0x0C` / `0x0B2C`; DN2 `0x15` / `0x2B` / `0x0B34`; Heat +FX `0x13` / `0x20` / `0x0B53`. The USB id's low byte changes with the USB mode (`0x012B` MIDI, `0x102B` audio/MIDI on the DT2).
hypotheses.test: Read the USB ids in each USB mode (`lsusb` on Linux, System Information on a Mac, Device Manager on Windows). Read the product id with Elektroid's device info.

hypotheses.inference: Unsaved edits survive a power cycle on the DT2 and the DT1 as on the DN2, because the stock edit writer stores each edit in the sound record at once.
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, turn a filter knob, do not save, power-cycle. Is the value still there? Also try a parameter lock.

hypotheses.inference: A received pattern dump lands in the slot armed on the unit, not in the slot its index byte names (shown on the DN2 by syxgrid).
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, send a pattern dump with index A05 while A02 is armed, using Elektroid or digi-roll. Where does it land?

hypotheses.inference: The DT1 recorder holds at most 33.0 s (1,584,000 frames at 48 kHz, mono).
hypotheses.test: Record with free length until it stops; time it.

hypotheses.inference: Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01).
hypotheses.test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?

hypotheses.inference: The Heat +FX answers the screen request (RPC framing `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`), as the Heat MKII does, so its screen can be mirrored and read without a mod.
hypotheses.test: Open Elek View (bluesgl.github.io/Elek_View) with nothing else on the MIDI port, select the unit, Start.

hypotheses.inference: The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20).
hypotheses.derived_from: digikit f117 (timer model) vs digikit f07 (derived)
hypotheses.test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).

hypotheses.inference: The ~4 KB cut in long MidiRpc LIST replies is in the stock reply router, not in a mod: an unpaged listing of a 256-entry table store on a modded DN2 came back as 3,997 bytes, correct up to entry 125 and garbage after; pages of 64 were clean.
hypotheses.test: On stock, list a +Drive folder with more than 130 entries in one unpaged request (DNX or Elektroid) and compare the reply length and the tail with a paged listing. Until settled, page listings at 64 entries or fewer.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too.
hypotheses.derived_from: elekloader Drive Loader (Rytm) {elekloader-drive}, digikit f120 (DT2 file layout)
hypotheses.test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitakt II on OS 1.17 answers midi.guide's NRPN numbers (track mute 1:108, track level 1:110, pattern mute 1:109, master overdrive 2:50), not the manual's (1:101, 1:100, 1:104, 2:37) (O24).
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, send each NRPN pair from a DAW or a MIDI tool on the auto channel with value 0 and then 127, and watch which parameter moves on the screen.

hypotheses.inference: On a stock Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.74) the first note right after a boot can be silent.
hypotheses.test: Power the stock unit on, wait for the main screen, play one pad or trig once and note whether it sounds; repeat over ten boots.

hypotheses.inference: A Digitakt II or Digitone II drops stock MidiRpc / Transfer requests while its boot intro still plays, and answers them once the main screen is up (digikit's emulator, 2026-11-16; I114).
hypotheses.test: Power on with Elektron Transfer (or another MidiRpc tool) connected and start a file listing as soon as USB appears; note whether the request fails or hangs during the intro and works after it.

hypotheses.inference: Stock TRACK COPY / PASTE on the Octatrack does not carry the LFO designer (SB26).
hypotheses.test: On T1 set an LFO WAVE to the designer, draw an obvious shape, aim it at volume with high depth; give T2 a different designer; GRID REC copy T1, paste onto T2: does T2 follow T1's shape?

hypotheses.inference: With SILENCE TRACKS on, stock also pops at a Part-changing pattern change when a ringing track has no trig on the new pattern's step 0 (the hard kill `0x40006820`; I119).
hypotheses.test: OT DEMO, SILENCE TRACKS on: let a sample ring on T4, T5 or T7, change A05 -> A03 with CHAIN AFTER 2; listen for a pop; repeat with SILENCE TRACKS off.

hypotheses.inference: The brief "new settings on the old sound" heard at a FULL load (Clyps) is stock's single sound path per track, not the mod: a retriggered voice fades through a path that already carries the new Part.
hypotheses.test: Stock [PTN] + trig between two patterns on different Parts with clearly different settings on one track and a sample ringing up to the change; the same blip on stock settles it.

hypotheses.inference: On Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74 the OS version field of a flashed build shows only on the boot screen; no GLOBAL menu shows it (trig-seedr's corrected check 1).
hypotheses.test: Boot a stock 1.74 unit, look through GLOBAL > SYSTEM for an OS INFO entry; note what the boot screen shows.

hypotheses.inference: The Rytm MKI boot-flash writers lie at `0x40096A6C-0x40096B3E` and BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE ends at `0x4011AA7A` in OS 1.74; the upgrade buffer is `0x40366570` (2 MiB; SB21).
hypotheses.test: Static: disassemble the stock MKI 1.74 image at those addresses and check the callers of the erase and program routines. No flashing needed.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitakt II's stock USB MIDI transmit path (OS 1.17) waits indefinitely for buffer space when the host stops reading.
hypotheses.test: Send a SysEx request whose reply is large, keep the port open but stop reading, and watch whether the UI and sequencer keep running.

hypotheses.inference: Octatrack stock LFO-design Invert maps v to -1 - v and Clear sets all steps to 0 and stepped.
hypotheses.test: Invert and clear a custom LFO on the unit, save, and read the Part's 16 values and interpolation mask.

hypotheses.inference: On stock DN2 OS 1.11 the chord MODEs' per-scale chord table is built in RAM at start-up from the five stock scale tables, with one row per SCALE value 0-34.
hypotheses.test: Dump the RAM table after boot in the emulator and on a unit (read-only), compare row count and content per scale.

hypotheses.inference: On a Model:Cycles with stock OS 1.13, a project track holding an out-of-range machine number plays CHORD with wrong settings, shows *Error* on MACHINES, and is repaired by turning LEVEL/DATA, without any crash.
hypotheses.test: Save a project with an added machine on a mod, flash stock, open it and play; then turn LEVEL/DATA on MACHINES.

hypotheses.inference: A Monomachine (OS 1.32B) sometimes reads a pattern status request sent right after a kit dump and never answers it; the same request sent again is answered.
hypotheses.test: Send a kit dump, then a pattern status request at once, 50 times; count requests with no reply within 3 s.

hypotheses.inference: A Model:Samples running a Cycles OS that checks with the Cycles key refuses a Samples-signed OS file at the last block, after all packets were sent (the check covers the whole file).
hypotheses.test: Only with a recovery path ready (MIDI startup menu): on a Samples with such an OS, send a Samples-signed OS by USB with a tool that logs each reply; note which block gets an error, and what the screen says.

hypotheses.inference: A Model:Cycles OS `.syx` with more than 16,270 packets (packet numbers past 16,383) is refused or fails during the update.
hypotheses.test: Do not flash such a file. Instead count the packets of your build and check that each packet number's two bytes are below 0x80.

hypotheses.inference: On a Rytm MKII (OS 1.74), Transfer's progress bar goes wrong while reading a file over 4,294,967 bytes from the unit (SB28).
hypotheses.test: Read a sample larger than 4.3 MB back from the unit with Transfer and watch the progress.

hypotheses.inference: A `.wav` saved by a stock Octatrack holds the file size, not size - 8, in its RIFF header (bytes 4-7).
hypotheses.test: Save any sample or recorder buffer on a unit; read bytes 4-7 as little endian and compare with the file size.

hypotheses.inference: With several .bin files at the CF card's top level, Octatrack OS UPGRADE picks one by a fixed rule (name order or file date), not the newest.
hypotheses.test: Put two copies of the stock 1.40C .bin with different names and dates on the card (both stock, so nothing changes), run OS UPGRADE and note which file it names or reads; swap names and repeat.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Rytm MKII 1.74, TRK SEND MIDI sends only a step's first message on time; later notes of the same step leave 5-30 ms late, more on p-locked steps.
hypotheses.test: Stock OS: TRK SEND MIDI on BD and SD, trigs on the same steps, one p-lock on BD; record DIN out on a computer MIDI monitor and compare each note's time to the step grid.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Digitone II 1.12, after NEW project the LFOs of a MIDI track send nothing until a note trig plays on that track; lock-only trigs do not start them.
hypotheses.test: Stock OS 1.12: NEW project, a MIDI track with LFO1 in FRE mode on a CC, no trigs; PLAY and watch a MIDI monitor. Then add a lock-only trig, then a note trig. Which one starts the CCs?

hypotheses.inference: On Syntakt OS 1.42 the top 4 MiB of DDR (`0x47c00000-0x48000000`) is rewritten every frame while delay and reverb are in use, so Modwerk's freed `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` is not free then.
hypotheses.test: Fill `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` and `0x478c0000-0x47bf0000` with a pattern after boot, play a pattern with heavy delay and reverb sends, load a sample-heavy project, then read back. Settles O35. The lower range is done for one unit: trig-seedr's canary over `0x478b0000-0x47bf0000` held with all 64 sample slots loaded (2026-11-19, I184) {trig-seedr-1121}; the top 4 MiB is still open.

hypotheses.inference: Holding TRIG 16 at power-on on a Syntakt with stock OS 1.42 does nothing else than (at most) toggle step 16 of the first pattern; MAIN has no boot-time key reader.
hypotheses.test: Hold TRIG 16 while powering on a stock unit; check the boot and step 16.

hypotheses.inference: On a stock Digitakt II (OS 1.17), changing a track's filter type sends the same MIDI parameter as a machine change (`0xea`, the "Machine Type" row, or (`0xf`, type) in the other send mode), because the stock filter setter `0x40051886` is a copy of the machine setter `0x40051712` (O39). What a receiving unit does with it is unknown.
hypotheses.test: Stock OS, MIDI out (CC/NRPN) to a computer MIDI monitor: change the filter type on the FLTR page, then the machine; compare the messages. Optionally send the captured message into a second unit and see what changes.

hypotheses.inference: A stock project rename on a Digitakt II or Digitone II keeps the save stamp (32-bit word at slot record +`0x18`), so a tool keyed on the stamp follows a renamed project. The rename callback (DT2 `0x400a1246`, DN2 `0x4009b3bc`) does not call the stamp builder directly; what its change notice triggers is not traced. Partly answered 2026-11-21: in the DN2 1.12 emulator a menu rename of the *current* project gave it a new live stamp, written at the next save; a non-current slot keeps its stamp by static reading. `[emu]`
hypotheses.test: Read the slot listing (with a tool that reads it) before and after a rename in PROJECT MANAGER; compare the stamp.

hypotheses.inference: Stock Model:Cycles OS 1.13 plays an LFO WAVE value past RND (a sound saved by the Techno Edition with its T3-T16 waves) as RND and does not crash.
hypotheses.test: Load such a sound on the official OS (back up first); check the LFO page and listen.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Model:Cycles OS 1.13, muting a track does not stop a note already sounding; only later trigs are held back (I162).
hypotheses.test: Play a long-decay note (CHORD or TONE), mute the track mid-note, listen.

hypotheses.inference: Stock Octatrack OS 1.40C reads a trig condition above 64 (octabam's TRIG MUTE stores condition + 65) as no condition: it plays the trig, shows ERR, and the bank still loads (no BANK UNAVAILABLE, cf. A60).
hypotheses.test: Load a project saved with a TRIG MUTE build on stock 1.40C (back up first): does the muted trig play, does its condition read ERR, does the bank load?

hypotheses.inference: A stock Octatrack power-up never parses `project.work`; it restores the project from battery RAM (I168).
hypotheses.test: With the unit off, edit the tempo in `project.work` on the card (keep a copy), power on: the old tempo should stay until LOAD PROJECT.

hypotheses.inference: A stock Syntakt (OS 1.42) keeps an unsaved trig edit across a power-off once its supercap is charged: the power-off handler writes the working state only when byte `0x43be3154` is set, which happens when PPDSDR_G bit 3 (supercap charged) reads high.
hypotheses.test: Leave the unit on for a few minutes, add a trig without saving, switch off and on: is the trig there? Repeat right after a cold start. Partly seen 2026-11-19: on one unit running trig-seedr (stock save path) an applied and a pending take survived a power off {trig-seedr-1121}; a plain stock unit and a power off right after a cold start are still open.

hypotheses.inference: Syntakt OS 1.42 has no parameter-lock row limit (unlike the Rytm's 72 rows a pattern): each track's lock store is a full 64-step x 71-id matrix and the set routine counts no rows.
hypotheses.test: Lock several SYN, FLTR and AMP parameters on every step of several tracks; look for any refusal.
