incidents.title: Window stubs placed inside DARK REV's buffer stopped the DSP (octabam test images)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, octabam diagnostic images (P1, D4), 2026-11-21/22
incidents.seen: image P1 booted with the DSP frame count at 0 for 90 s, twice; D4 stalled 6.6 s into its run with no DARK REV picked.
incidents.cause: SIDECHAIN_COMPRESSOR's hook stubs had grown past `0x33fff` into the FX2 slot at `0x34000`, which DARK REV fills up to slot + `0x3da2`. The window believed free, `0x33da3..0x37eff`, is really two gaps: `0x33da3..0x33fff` and `0x37da3..0x37eff`. The results of those diagnostic builds for I170 were discarded.
incidents.fix: octabam's build refuses a window record inside the extent of a guarded reverb's slot.

incidents.title: v0.5 release check: 3 of 32 program changes were not applied (octabam)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, octabam v0.5 images `octabam`, `octabam-verbs` and `octabam-bus` built from `main` at `382a478b` plus the release commit, booted by REMIX SWITCH from the flashed image (none flashed), 2026-11-22
incidents.seen: the 32-program-change soak left 3 of 32 changes unapplied on `octabam`, 0 on `octabam-bus`, and 0 on `octabam-verbs`, which still logged 32 bad DSP records (one per transition, when the dearest layouts loaded). The meter, transport, USB and DSP-watch checks passed on all three. The long mixed soak did not complete on any image.
incidents.cause: not given. v0.4 had applied 32 of 32 in the same soak (2026-11-08).
incidents.fix: none. v0.5 was tagged with this result, with the DARK REV stall (I170) as a known fault, and with module changes made after the tested commit that never ran on a unit.

incidents.title: A SMEAR note silenced the whole Digitone II until a reboot (RIFT v0.16/v0.17)
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11, RIFT v0.16 and v0.17 (gated in the emulators), the owner's and a tester's units, 2026-11-22
incidents.seen: a SMEAR note gave a short burst, then the whole output went silent, every other machine with it, until a power cycle; projects were unharmed. PLATEAU (v0.17) also did nothing while other tracks played. Separately, the first start after a flash could leave ORGAN silent until one more power cycle.
incidents.cause: SMEAR's vocoder (VOC) jobs cost 200,000-260,000 cycles a block on a cost model of the unit (instructions plus memory waits, fitted to the idle frame's measured 416k of 667k cycles), which runs the DSP past its frame. The frame guard expected each voice to cost what its last block cost, and VOC's light blocks kept that figure low, so a heavy block was let through. PLATEAU was dropped for the rest of a note whenever the guard was short of time.
incidents.fix: v0.18 (2026-11-22) turns VOC off, makes the guard expect a voice's peak cost, adds an output guard that replaces any block that is not finite or runs away with silence and restarts that voice, and skips PLATEAU only for a block with no room. The release gate now prices every machine's worst block on the unit's cost model (`rcost`) and checks non-finite blocks (`sanitize`). The fix itself is gated in the emulators only.
incidents.status: fixed in v0.18 (not yet confirmed on a unit)

incidents.title: The UI stopped during playback with six modules installed (Modwerk base 0.7.13)
incidents.unit: Octatrack (model not stated), OS 1.40C, released Modwerk base 0.7.13, six modules including Tape Echo and E-Verb, a tester's field diagnostics, 2026-11-22
incidents.seen: the UI tick stopped during playback while the audio frame interrupt kept running long enough to record the freeze; the CPU meter read about 78 %. The incident and its installed set belong to the same boot. At the next start all six modules were restored. An earlier boot on base 0.7.12 with only Tape Echo and E-Verb installed showed the same symptom.
incidents.cause: unknown. The record gives the set and the transport state but not the last action or where the UI stopped making progress; the overlap in installed modules does not show that either effect is responsible.
incidents.fix: none yet; Modwerk needs the action and the point where the UI stopped in the next record.

incidents.title: A small USB staging transfer went unconfirmed, and a USB Audio trial rolled back at the reconnect (Modwerk, Windows)
incidents.unit: Octatrack (model not stated), OS 1.40C, Modwerk bases 0.7.12 and 0.7.13, a tester's unit on a Windows host with the Modwerk site open in a browser, reported 2026-11-22
incidents.seen: (1) a USB staging transfer went unconfirmed on both bases; on 0.7.13 the offer held only two removal headers, small enough for one chunk. All three failed attempts recorded one more primed USB receive than completed receives, and zero bus resets. (2) Other attempts with the same removals reached the trial, disconnected during the USB Audio configuration change and came back with the previous active set. Removing MIDI Scenes alone was then kept.
incidents.cause: (1) open; the released diagnostics do not say which command failed. (2) not proven on the unit: in Modwerk's host link test the first claim of the returning interface fails, and the installer then entered its ordinary busy state, ended the page's wait and released its lock on the open trial.
incidents.fix: (2) the installer retries the claim under the trial's existing lock and deadline (host tests cover Keep once the interface is free and expiry while it stays busy); diagnostic summaries now name USB Audio, and an opted-in report shows a failed claim during the trial. (1) none yet; the next record needs the upload command and the remaining receive length.
incidents.status: open (1); fix not yet tried on a physical Windows reconnect (2)

incidents.title: Drum Mode kept the trig keys from the stock SCALE menu and covered the PTN/BANK LEDs (Digitone mk1)
incidents.unit: Digitone mk1, OS 1.44, Drum Mode 0.10 on elekloader core-dn1 5.3, the author's unit, 2026-11-22
incidents.seen: in the SCALE menu (FUNC + PAGE) the trig keys played pads instead of setting the number of steps; only PAGE and the knob worked. While PTN or BANK was held the trig keys showed the pads, not the stock's pattern and bank LEDs. The emulator test sets had passed.
incidents.cause: Drum Mode handed the trig keys back to the stock only while PTN or BANK was held, the pattern/bank select was open or a chain's key was held; the SCALE menu was not on that list, and its LED painting ignored all of these states. The emulator tests did not cover either case.
incidents.fix: 0.10.1 leaves the trig key LEDs to the stock in those states; 0.10.2 leaves the trig keys and their LEDs to the stock while the SCALE menu is open. `test_stock_keys.py` grew from 25 to 33 checks.
incidents.status: fixed in the emulator; waits for the unit (0.10.4)

incidents.title: A MIDI track showed "Drum Mode off" and then could not be used (Drum Mode 0.10)
incidents.unit: Digitone mk1, OS 1.44, Drum Mode 0.10 on elekloader core-dn1 5.3, the author's unit, 2026-11-22
incidents.seen: on some MIDI tracks the screen showed Drum Mode turned off, and the track could not be used after that.
incidents.cause: unknown. Which tracks, what was pressed before and what "unusable" means (no sound, dead keys, stuck UI) are still to be recorded. The author thinks it may be linked to the UI hang with the Mod Menu open seen once in digiemu (digitone.md, 2026-11-17 section).
incidents.fix: none yet.

incidents.title: Stock Rytm samples played under Sidecar machines (Rytm firmware 0.4.4/0.5.0)
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII with Sidecar, Rytm firmware 0.4.4 (a user's unit; reported before 2026-11-22)
incidents.seen: the Rytm's own samples sounded under PLAITS and SOPHIE.
incidents.cause: page 2 of every Sidecar machine is the sound's sample words 17-24, and the stock sample player renders them for every voice. The mod zeroed the voice's sample gain (`0x80007000 + 8 x voice`), which scales buffer B only. The layer's output S (`0x800067f8 + 128 x voice`) is written by `sample_render` after the machine renders, so the machine cannot clear it.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from the code and shown in the emulator
incidents.fix: Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1: a detour at the mixer call zeroes S of voices under a Sidecar machine, and the stock sample player skips its resampler and filter for those voices (also some Rytm CPU back). A stock track's sample-only trig on a shared voice still plays. The mirror case (a stock-latched engine and a sample-only trig from the Sidecar track) still plays the Rytm sample.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.5.1.1 (emulator; no unit run stated).

incidents.title: A compressor's GR meter raised MAIN CPU through screen repaints (Synfact comp-st 0.2.0, Syntakt)
incidents.unit: Syntakt, OS 1.42, Synfact core 2.4.0 with comp-st 0.2.0 (the owner's unit), 2026-11-20/21
incidents.seen: MAIN's CPU reading rose a lot while the COMP page was open.
incidents.cause: not the DSP. Every meter change asked for a repaint, and each repaint recomposes every visible view of the double-buffered screen (about 30,000 instructions for the COMP page). With drums the meter asked on 24-26 of the 30 UI ticks a second.
incidents.fix: comp-st 0.3: the meter repaints at most every third tick (10 Hz) and ignores 1-pixel moves except to zero; 8-10 repaints a second with drums, none with a steady signal.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.3 / 1.0.0 (emulator count); the CPU drop is not measured on the unit.

incidents.title: An eDMA block without a self-link moved only its first 16 bytes (Synfact stereo tracks, Syntakt)
incidents.unit: Syntakt (the owner's unit), Synfact stereo engine development build, 2026-11 (before samplers-st 1.6)
incidents.seen: a block sent by AUDIO eDMA channel 46 to the shared window never arrived whole: only the first 16 bytes (sequence, mask, shifts) reached it, never the tag; the profile written by the CPU did arrive. Synfact went back to copying word by word (about 6 % of the block against 5.1 % with DMA).
incidents.cause: the TCD set CITER 35 without the channel link; a software start runs one minor loop of 16 bytes. Stock's channel 47 links the channel to itself.
incidents.cause_found_by: as the docs state it; how it was found is not said, the fix copies stock's channel 47 TCD
incidents.fix: samplers-st 1.6 sets CITER/BITER `0xdc23` (ELINK to channel 46, 35 loops of 16 bytes).
incidents.status: fixed in 1.6 (emulated TCD check); not stated on a unit.

incidents.title: Tape Echo froze an Octatrack MKII after the frame budget was exceeded (Modwerk 0.7.14 development base)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII (the owner's unit), OS 1.40C, Modwerk 0.7.14 development twin with an 11-module set, 2026-11-21
incidents.seen: the meter admitted Tape Echo; the longest frame reached 134 % and 165 renders were skipped. About 3 s into the next PLAY MAIN froze: USB audio looped 250 ms for 9 s, then the unit and a second interface on the same hub left USB.
incidents.cause: Tape Echo's work runs at interrupt level 5 and cannot be shed; the admission check looked at the mean load, while dropped renders depend on the longest frame.
incidents.fix: base 0.8 admits modules by frame time (renders capped at 122 %) and adds a frame-deadline event; Tape Echo 0.1.9 took an overload scene from 139 % to 130 %.
incidents.status: mitigated in base 0.8 (unit runs on development twins).

incidents.title: A pattern change made a late frame entry and the Octatrack DSP stopped (Modwerk 0.8 development twins)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII (the owner's unit), OS 1.40C, Modwerk 0.8 development twins, 2026-11-22 (stalls 49, 50, 55 and 56)
incidents.seen: after a pattern change a 477-498 µs frame was followed by an entry 147-162 µs late, and the DSP stopped; a power cycle was needed.
incidents.cause: an entry that comes too late breaks the DSP frame exchange for good.
incidents.fix: base 0.8 holds an entry 80-190 µs late until it is 190 µs late, so the DSP skips one frame (a click) instead of stopping; with the 122 % render ceiling 20 switches ran on. Entries later than 190 µs cannot be held. A tester's MKI on 0.7.12 froze its UI after a 513 µs frame and an entry 172 µs late; not reproduced on an MKII, open.
incidents.status: fixed in base 0.8 (unit runs); the MKI case is open.

incidents.title: New machines ran the Syntakt AUDIO CPU to 99 % (Synfact SY MnM and MD MACHINEDRUM)
incidents.unit: Syntakt (the owner's unit), OS 1.42, Synfact banks 0.37-0.42 and SY MnM 0.6.1, 2026-11-21/23
incidents.seen: SY MnM's FM+ STAT, PAR and DYN on three tracks plus five ONE SHOT read 99 % AUDIO; DENS's in-machine stereo chorus beside seven stock tracks read 99 %; MD's PI-RC or PI-RS voices with two or three SWARM, CY ALLOY, ONE SHOT, SY TOY, SY CHORD and SY TONE tracks read 99 % and the audio broke up.
incidents.cause: the machines' per-sample cost, measured against the unit's own readings (see the cost model on the device page).
incidents.fix: SY MnM 0.7.0's lighter FM+ backend (-25 % instructions, emulator), DENS's chorus removed (the stock Chorus FX instead), PI voices at 22.05 kHz from bank 0.40 (the same projects then read 95 % with no break-up). md-st also strikes through voices that do not fit its CPU budget.
incidents.status: fixed on the unit for MD; FM+ re-check on a unit not stated.

incidents.title: A pattern write to a blank Analog Four pattern failed its readback on the kit byte (digi-roll-studio)
incidents.unit: Analog Four MKI, OS 1.56 (build 0204), 2026-11-23
incidents.seen: a track write to A16 of a blank pattern read back different in one byte; the tool restored the original byte for byte.
incidents.cause: a blank pattern holds 0xFF as its kit reference; after a note write the unit stored 0 there.
incidents.fix: track writes now refuse a pattern with an unset kit reference before anything is sent (v0.6.0/v0.6.1).

incidents.title: COPY PROJECT copied a stale saved state into a new Octatrack project (octabam)
incidents.unit: an Octatrack (model not stated), OS 1.40C, octabam COPY PROJECT first version, 2026-11-24
incidents.seen: the new folder made by SAVE TO NEW held the old project's `bank02.strd`, older than the take that had changed `bank02.work`, so reloading the saved state brought back the old bank.
incidents.cause: the module copied every sidecar file, `.strd` included, after stock had written only `.work` files.
incidents.fix: `.strd` files are no longer copied; SAVE PROJECT writes the new project's own.
incidents.status: fixed in source; the fix has not run on a unit.

stock_bugs.title: eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card
stock_bugs.symptom: TRIM ERROR at a sector number; after a restart at another one.
stock_bugs.trigger: many TRIMs in a row while the card is busy (seen while a mod erased its own data).
stock_bugs.cause: the busy wait after CMD38 arms the DAT0 edge interrupt before it tests DAT0, leaving a stale semaphore post; the next TRIM on a busy card returns at once and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout.
stock_bugs.workaround: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry (TRIM is idempotent); fixed in dn2mk2 v0.40.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a mod that erases or rewrites many blocks must be tested on a card that is busy, not only on an idle one.
stock_bugs.found_by: dn2mk2 (error seen on a unit; cause read from stock code)

stock_bugs.title: Song LOAD trusts a stored row count and halts the unit
stock_bugs.symptom: a project halts the instrument when opened, on stock and modded builds alike.
stock_bugs.trigger: a song whose stored row count is out of range (one project held 21,503 rows, at most 99 are valid).
stock_bugs.cause: song LOAD `0x400dea6a` reads the count as a signed word at stored `+2891` and copies that many 29-byte rows into 37-byte live rows without a check.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by the `songguard` mod (dn2_firmware_explore, also in dn2mk2): a damaged song loads empty; confirmed on hardware. Users: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`).
stock_bugs.test_tip: a project that crashes your build may crash stock too: open it on stock before you debug your mod.
stock_bugs.found_by: dn2_firmware_explore (seen on a unit, cause read from stock code)
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: The USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit
stock_bugs.symptom: an oversized image stalls at the end of the transfer; nothing is written; a power cycle clears it.
stock_bugs.trigger: a container larger than `0x200000` bytes.
stock_bugs.cause: a 2 MiB receive buffer without a size check.
stock_bugs.workaround: keep the container under 2 MiB; check the size in the build.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a build that "hangs while updating" may just be too big.

stock_bugs.title: Auto-commit upload loses its "upload complete" event
stock_bugs.symptom: the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving".
stock_bugs.trigger: the first auto-commit upload after boot, sent before the upgrade view is open.
stock_bugs.cause: the OS posts "upload complete" while the view is not open; the event is lost.
stock_bugs.workaround: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a flashing script that hangs once and works the second time may be meeting this.
stock_bugs.found_by: complex-ping's Digitone II modding skill (seen on a unit, read from stock code)

stock_bugs.title: LFO TRIG MODE ONE and HALF do not run one (half) cycle and hold
stock_bugs.symptom: with TRIG MODE ONE or HALF the LFO does not run exactly one cycle (half a cycle) from its start phase and then hold the value it reached; two separate stock bugs, on audio and MIDI tracks.
stock_bugs.trigger: set an LFO's TRIG MODE to ONE or HALF and trigger it.
stock_bugs.cause: not described in the source.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by the `lfolength` mod (dn2_firmware_explore; supersedes `lfohold`); confirmed on hardware on an audio track (2026-10-09), MIDI tracks in the emulator.
stock_bugs.test_tip: do not judge an LFO mod by ONE/HALF behaviour without comparing stock.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: Each USB controller reset leaks a timer slot (DT2/DN2, static reading)
stock_bugs.device_os: Digitakt II OS 1.17, Digitone II OS 1.12
stock_bugs.symptom: none reported on a unit. Each run of the stock controller-reset path (`0x40006ada` -> `0x40007104`) takes one of 16 shared timer slots and does not give it back; the reset also spins on USBCMD.RST with no bound.
stock_bugs.trigger: the firmware's PHY viewport watchdog firing, or a mod calling the reset path.
stock_bugs.cause: read in the image by digikit, not cross-checked.
stock_bugs.workaround: do not call the reset path repeatedly from a mod.
stock_bugs.test_tip: count free timer slots before and after forced resets on a unit.

stock_bugs.title: MIDI-track LFOs freeze after a new project until a note trig plays
stock_bugs.symptom: after creating a new project, the LFOs on a MIDI track send nothing until a note trig plays on that track (or its trig key is tapped); lock-only trigs do not start them, so a MIDI track used only for LFO modulation stays frozen.
stock_bugs.trigger: NEW project, MIDI track with an LFO in FRE or TRG mode and no note trigs.
stock_bugs.cause: not described; the fix patches the lane update `0x40137770` and the LFO send loop's destination check `0x4012a340`.
stock_bugs.workaround: tap the track's trig key, or place a note trig; fixed by vitel2's MIDI LFO run mod (which also stops the CCs while the transport is stopped).
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; unconfirmed by us (H53)

stock_bugs.title: The stock restart does not wait for the +Drive or drain the panel link
stock_bugs.symptom: a restart triggered by code can cut off a +Drive write or a panel message in flight.
stock_bugs.trigger: calling stock's own restart from a mod while the card or the panel link is busy.
stock_bugs.cause: stock's restart does not wait for the +Drive and does not let the panel link drain with interrupts on.
stock_bugs.workaround: elekloader core-dn1 exports `core_restart`, which does both; use it instead of stock's.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a mod that restarts the unit should be tested right after a save and while keys are pressed.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; worked around by a core

stock_bugs.title: EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze
stock_bugs.symptom: the request after a 64/128/192/256-byte reply returns 0 bytes; once the unit froze; 128/192-byte OUT stages never complete.
stock_bugs.trigger: a control transfer whose data stage is a multiple of 64 bytes.
stock_bugs.cause: stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head.
stock_bugs.workaround: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming.
stock_bugs.test_tip: test USB replies of exactly 64 and 128 bytes on purpose.

stock_bugs.title: About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered
stock_bugs.symptom: host requests time out now and then.
stock_bugs.trigger: many EP0 OUT stages in a row.
stock_bugs.cause: the stage completes inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stops part-way.
stock_bugs.workaround: finish a completed stage from a 60 Hz tick, or stall EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits.
stock_bugs.test_tip: count timeouts over a thousand requests, not ten.

stock_bugs.title: A Plays-Free MIDI track stalls after its first step
stock_bugs.symptom: the track stops after its first step on a manual trig.
stock_bugs.trigger: a Plays-Free MIDI track with trig quantize Direct and pattern scale Per Track, triggered manually.
stock_bugs.cause: read from stock code at `0x4009b6f2` (an 18-byte splice fixes it).
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's BATCH_BUGFIXES (`MIDI_PLAYS_FREE_FIX`); hardware-confirmed 2026-08-28.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a sequencer mod that uses scales Per Track can run into this on stock paths.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: A pattern that holds only parameter locks shows as empty
stock_bugs.symptom: the pattern's grid LED stays unlit under [PTN], as for an unused slot.
stock_bugs.trigger: a pattern whose only content is parameter locks (on a MIDI track, or trigless locks on an audio track), with no trig.
stock_bugs.cause: stock's "used" test looks at trigs only.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`EMPTY_PATTERN_LED_FIX`) under [PTN]; under [BANK] a full scan of 256 patterns' locks on every LED refresh starved the CPU. Since 2026-11-20 (318 B version) [BANK] also lights a bank whose pattern holds a trigless lock with a locked value, by reading only the trigless-lock masks and at most 16 lock rows per pattern; confirmed responsive with [BANK] held on an MKI. Other lock-only content still reads empty under [BANK]. {octatrack-kyoti-fw-1121}
stock_bugs.test_tip: do not overwrite a "free" pattern slot in a test project without checking for locks.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: A pattern-triggered Part change carries the old Part's state over
stock_bugs.symptom: a track leaving PICKUP for FLEX keeps playing the old Part's pickup loop; the recorder's SRC/RLEN cache goes stale; a pattern switch into a PICKUP track marks the Part edited when nothing changed. Also reported on Elektronauts.
stock_bugs.trigger: a pattern change that changes Part, with a track going from PICKUP to another machine.
stock_bugs.cause: the "select Part" handler `0x400621a6` calls `FUN_400972fc` per track, whose PICKUP-to-other branch does nothing; PICKUP and FLEX share one sample arena, so the stale pointer still looks valid; nothing republishes the recorder cache.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`PART_CHANGE_CARRYOVER_FIX`): republish the recorder records, set the voice-kill bit, re-seed the slot.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a mod that changes Parts (DIRECT JUMP and others) reaches the same stock path and shows the same symptom; compare a stock pattern change.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: A trigless lock stays lit after its last lock is erased
stock_bugs.symptom: the step stays lit on the trig row forever, although it is now inert.
stock_bugs.trigger: erase the last remaining lock of a trigless lock (LIVE REC: [NO] + knob), on an audio or a MIDI track.
stock_bugs.cause: the LIVE erase worker (audio `0x40038874`, MIDI twin `0x40038668`) clears the step from the lock bitmap when its row empties, but never the trigless-lock flag at track `+0x10`, which keeps the LED lit. The MIDI clear-trigs path also leaves `+0x10` set where audio clears it. {octatrack-kyoti-fw-1121}
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS (a deliberately empty trigless lock placed with FUNC + TRIG is left alone); since 2026-11-20 on MIDI tracks too, confirmed on an MKI (I173).
stock_bugs.test_tip: lit steps after a lock edit are not necessarily your mod.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: LO-FI's AMF ring-mod pitch falls at eleven values instead of rising
stock_bugs.device_os: Octatrack MKI and MKII, OS 1.40C (LO-FI on FX1 and FX2)
stock_bugs.symptom: turning AMF up lowers the ring-mod pitch at AMF 8, 17, 23, 28, 32, 35, 37, 40, 42, 45 and 48 (worst at 7 to 8, about 63 % lower); monotonic again above 48.
stock_bugs.trigger: LO-FI with AMF in those ranges (also reached by LFOs, scenes and fine values).
stock_bugs.cause: the coefficient's extended-precision multiply starts with `mpysu x0,y0,a` (signed x unsigned) on two magnitudes; when the low word's top bit is set the partial product's sign flips. Reported to Elektron, not fixed upstream.
stock_bugs.workaround: `mpyuu` instead (octa-bt-pt's LOFI AMF FIX; also a Modwerk draft module). Saved projects at affected values will sound different with the fix.
stock_bugs.test_tip: an effect mod that compares against LO-FI by ear may be comparing against this bug.
stock_bugs.found_by: octa-bt-pt (AMF 0-127 x fine 0-127 swept in the DSP emulator with the fix: monotonic)
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod (not yet run on hardware per the Modwerk draft)

stock_bugs.title: Probable: SPATIALIZER's ring misaligns when selected mid-play
stock_bugs.symptom: a misaligned delay ring when SPATIALIZER is selected while playing with a non-zero held offset; later calls can read across the ring end (wet path only); re-selecting at offset 0 realigns.
stock_bugs.trigger: select SPATIALIZER mid-play.
stock_bugs.cause: the dispatcher splits a frame's FX call at `x:$20c`, and SPATIALIZER's init zeroes its ring write offset between the two calls, misaligning the ring by 32 - 2 x offset.
stock_bugs.workaround: none yet; the source plans a hardware test on stock.
stock_bugs.test_tip: odd SPATIALIZER artefacts after switching effects live may be stock.

stock_bugs.title: The AUDIO EDITOR key opens the sample the track had before
stock_bugs.symptom: after a track copy/paste or a Part reload, the [AUDIO EDITOR] key shows the old sample's name, waveform and slices.
stock_bugs.trigger: change a track's sample by copy/paste or Part reload, then press [AUDIO EDITOR] without reselecting the track.
stock_bugs.cause: stock reuses the sample the track had when it was last selected.
stock_bugs.workaround: reselect the track first; fixed by OCTAMAX 2f.
stock_bugs.test_tip: when a mod changes a track's sample, reselect the track before you judge the editor.
stock_bugs.found_by: OCTAMAX (seen on a unit; fixes confirmed on an MKII 2026-11-07 (2f) and 2026-11-11 (2i))
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: One Part byte outside its stock range drops the whole bank at power-on
stock_bugs.symptom: after a restart all eight tracks of the bank read STATIC with no trigs and default FX; the next restart restores the bank with the byte reset to 0.
stock_bugs.trigger: a byte in a Part record outside the range stock's Part check accepts (a mod's packed value of 0x80 or more).
stock_bugs.cause: the boot's battery restore runs stock's Part check and drops the bank when it repairs a byte.
stock_bugs.workaround: store only values stock accepts in stock records (rule A60).
stock_bugs.test_tip: after any mod that stores bytes in Parts, save, restart twice and check the bank.

stock_bugs.title: Probable: TRACK COPY / PASTE leaves the LFO designer behind
stock_bugs.symptom: a pasted track whose LFO WAVE is the designer plays the destination track's designer shape, not the copied one; seen only when pasting to another track or into a pattern on another Part.
stock_bugs.trigger: GRID REC copy of a track with a designer LFO, paste onto another track.
stock_bugs.cause: TRACK COPY `0x40029754` copies the record plus six Part blocks into clipboard `+0x91f..+0x9a1`; the designer (`+0x1702+16t`, slope `+0x1782+2t`) is not among them (read from stock code).
stock_bugs.workaround: none yet; KYOTI names a fix (TRACK_PASTE_DESIGNER_FIX, about 60-100 bytes) if it is confirmed.
stock_bugs.test_tip: stock test H31 in [HYPOTHESES.md](HYPOTHESES.md).
stock_bugs.found_by: octatrack-kyoti-fw ("candidate stock bug", read from the code, not yet seen on a unit)

stock_bugs.title: WAV files saved by the Octatrack carry a RIFF size 8 bytes too large
stock_bugs.symptom: bytes 4-7 of a saved `.wav` hold the whole file size instead of file size minus 8. Most decoders ignore it because they trust the `data` chunk size; strict tools may warn or read past the end.
stock_bugs.trigger: any stock sample save (seen with a recorder buffer saved through the stock routine).
stock_bugs.cause: the header writer stores the file length, not length - 8 (read from the code; measured under the port: 176,444 B file, 176,444 in the field).
stock_bugs.workaround: tools that read Octatrack WAVs should trust the `data` chunk size.
stock_bugs.status: confirmed in emulator, not checked on a unit-saved file

stock_bugs.title: FX1 SETUP knob F on EQUALIZER changes a hidden Part byte
stock_bugs.symptom: turning knob F on FX1's SETUP page with EQUALIZER loaded changes a Part byte while no screen shows a parameter there.
stock_bugs.trigger: EQUALIZER in FX1, SETUP page, turn F.
stock_bugs.cause: none of the page-2 editors tests an enable bit for the slot.
stock_bugs.workaround: leave knob F alone on that page.
stock_bugs.status: unconfirmed on a unit; audible effect unknown

stock_bugs.title: A timestretched voice retriggered within about 300 samples stays silent
stock_bugs.symptom: a voice with TSTR AUTO, NORM or BEAT that is retriggered within its first ~300 samples stalls silent (200 and 250 samples failed, 308 held); slices made by stock's CREATE SLICE GRID show it too.
stock_bugs.trigger: very short slices or fast retriggers with timestretch on.
stock_bugs.cause: timestretch needs about 300 samples of run-up (octabam's reading).
stock_bugs.workaround: keep slices and retrigger gaps above ~300 samples, or turn timestretch off for them; octabam's LAZY CHOP guards against it.
stock_bugs.status: stock behaviour (a limit more than a bug)

stock_bugs.title: Deleting an arrangement row above a JUMP that targets it turns the JUMP into a HALT
stock_bugs.symptom: FUNC + UP (delete) on row D, with a JUMP on row D+1 that targets D, moves the JUMP into D, where it points at itself and plays as a HALT; no message.
stock_bugs.trigger: delete the row a JUMP below targets.
stock_bugs.cause: the delete routine `0x4009b168` shifts rows without fixing jump targets (matches the image reading).
stock_bugs.workaround: check JUMP targets after deleting rows.
stock_bugs.found_by: Modwerk (Arr Rows research; reported to the Modwerk owner)
stock_bugs.status: stock behaviour, reproduced on the developer's MKI with no module

stock_bugs.title: Inserting on a HALT row leaves an endless LOOP below it
stock_bugs.symptom: FUNC + DOWN (insert) on a HALT row keeps the HALT and leaves a `LOOP: n/∞` below it.
stock_bugs.trigger: insert on a HALT row.
stock_bugs.cause: not described.
stock_bugs.workaround: check the rows after an insert near a HALT.

stock_bugs.title: SAVE TO NEW reports FILE NOT FOUND for a project with no `.strd` files (Octatrack)
stock_bugs.symptom: SAVE TO NEW shows FILE NOT FOUND, yet the new project folder is written.
stock_bugs.trigger: SAVE TO NEW on a project that has never been saved as a state (no `.strd` files).
stock_bugs.cause: not read; stock first saves the open project, then copies only `.work` files to the new folder.
stock_bugs.workaround: none needed; the new folder is complete. octabam's COPY PROJECT adds the sidecar files to SAVE TO NEW.
stock_bugs.test_tip: check the new folder on the card before you trust or distrust the message.

stock_bugs.title: Edits to hidden FX words overwrite the delay's saved TIME (latent)
stock_bugs.symptom: after an edit of live FX words 38-41 and a power cycle, the delay TIME comes back wrong (2 instead of 23 in the test).
stock_bugs.trigger: a parameter setter writes FX words 38-41. The stock UI never edits them, so only mods reach this.
stock_bugs.cause: the FX edit save maps words 38-41 to stored slot 0, which holds the delay's TIME.
stock_bugs.workaround: keep mod values for those words in your own storage (Modwerk's base redirects them to its kit storage).
stock_bugs.test_tip: after any mod that touches FX words, save, power-cycle and check the delay TIME.

stock_bugs.title: A non-sample file on the +Drive hangs LOAD TO PROJECT and later stalls the OS upgrade
stock_bugs.symptom: loading a file that is not a sample (a raw `.elemod` in this case) into the project hangs the unit; a project that holds such a file then stalls the next OS upgrade at PREPARING until CREATE NEW.
stock_bugs.trigger: any file on the +Drive's sample filesystem is listed by SAMPLES, in every folder; LOAD TO PROJECT reads its first 16 bytes as the sample header without a check.
stock_bugs.cause: per elekloader, LOAD TO PROJECT trusts the 16-byte header at the start of the file.
stock_bugs.workaround: a tool that stores other files on the +Drive starts each with 16 zero bytes, which stock loads as an empty sample (elekloader's Drive Loader does this).
stock_bugs.test_tip: keep test files off the +Drive, or give them the zero header; if an OS upgrade stalls at PREPARING after +Drive experiments, try CREATE NEW before blaming the image.

stock_bugs.title: The Rytm MKI's in-OS upgrade decodes into a 2 MiB buffer without a bound check
stock_bugs.symptom: not seen; an image that decodes past 2 MiB would overrun the buffer.
stock_bugs.trigger: an update image larger than the fixed decode buffer.
stock_bugs.cause: a fixed buffer with no size check (elekloader's profile, static reading). Modwerk's MKI research names the buffer `0x40366570` (2 MiB; reported, still to be checked on a 1.74 image, H36) and notes that the startup menu's MIDI DIN recovery survives an overrun. {modwerk-1117}
stock_bugs.workaround: keep an image at or below `0x1F0000` bytes (elekloader's limit).
stock_bugs.test_tip: check the size in the build, as for SB3 on the Digitone II.

stock_bugs.title: FX-track lock indexes 38-41 read past their table and share rows with 18-21
stock_bugs.area: parameter locks on the FX track
stock_bugs.symptom: the FX track's sound-index-to-row-type table has 38 entries (`0x401c5b4c`), but indexes 38..41 are looked up anyway; they read on into the next table (`0x401c5be4[0..3]`) and get row types 9..12, the same rows as indexes 18..21.
stock_bugs.trigger: a lock on one of the FX track's parameters 38-41.
stock_bugs.cause: the selector (`0x400075c8`/`0x40007602`) picks the table by "track == 12" alone and does not check the index against the FX table's length.
stock_bugs.workaround: a mod that writes FX-track locks should treat 38-41 and 18-21 as one row each.
stock_bugs.status: open; seen in the emulator only.

stock_bugs.title: The UI queue overwrites unread messages when more than 1024 wait
stock_bugs.symptom: under heavy load the panel lags and key, pad pressure and other UI messages are lost.
stock_bugs.trigger: more than 1024 messages waiting in the UI queue (seen with 13 mods and BD ANALOG voices playing, plus pad pressure at 200-290 messages a second during a held pad).
stock_bugs.cause: the queue is a ring of 1024 pointers; its send updates the write index and count with interrupts masked but never checks for a full ring (read in the OS 1.74 disassembly).
stock_bugs.workaround: keep audio-block load low enough that the UI task keeps up; a mod that posts to the queue keeps its own bounded pool and counts only its own waiting events.
stock_bugs.test_tip: read the queue's read index and count (Modwerk's test counters) while holding a pad with RTRG under load.
stock_bugs.found_by: Modwerk (Live Rec Retrig Fix 0.2.2 testing; overflow counted on a unit, I131)

stock_bugs.title: Data transfer progress wraps for files over 4,294,967 bytes
stock_bugs.area: Data router (USB transfers of files, as Transfer uses)
stock_bugs.symptom: the per-mille progress of a read goes wrong past 4,294,967 bytes.
stock_bugs.trigger: a read of a file larger than 4,294,967 bytes.
stock_bugs.cause: the progress (`0x4008c9d6..0x4008c9e8`) wraps there; 4,294,967 is 2^32 / 1,000, so a 32-bit multiply by 1,000 is the likely cause `[?]` (the source gives only the range and the limit).
stock_bugs.workaround: a client counts the bytes it gets; elekloader's tools do.
stock_bugs.test_tip: download a sample over 4.3 MB with Transfer and watch the progress bar.

stock_bugs.title: Pad pressure goes to the wrong note in CHROMATIC mode and is dropped during RTRG rolls (Rytm MKII)
stock_bugs.symptom: in CHROMATIC mode a held pad's poly pressure goes out 24 semitones above the note it played (note on 36, pressure for 60, note off 36), so a synth that follows the note sees no aftertouch. During a retrig roll held with RTRG and VEL.CUR set, the RETRIG menu takes the pressure and throws it away: no AFTERTOUCH movement and no MIDI poly pressure (ALWAYS ON pads with VEL.CUR set keep it).
stock_bugs.trigger: hold a pad in CHROMATIC mode and press it harder; or hold RTRG with VEL.CUR set and squeeze a pad.
stock_bugs.cause: not read; the module README describes the behaviour only.
stock_bugs.workaround: Modwerk's Pad Pressure Fix module (0.2.0-experimental) sends pressure on the played note and routes roll pressure to aftertouch and MIDI out; its fixes are moving into the Modwerk Rytm base.
stock_bugs.test_tip: watch MIDI out for the poly pressure note number while you hold a CHROMATIC pad.

stock_bugs.title: A random exception while browsing (filesystem block cache)
stock_bugs.symptom: a random exception while browsing.
stock_bugs.trigger: browsing (the source gives no exact steps).
stock_bugs.cause: the filesystem block cache, per Model-TG.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by Model-TG ("a long-standing stock bug"), and in builds that include it (Modded-Cycles lists it).
stock_bugs.test_tip: an exception while browsing on a modded build is not necessarily the mod.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: Eleven sequencer and UI bugs fixed by ems-monomachine-firmware
stock_bugs.symptom: as listed in the project's changelog: clearing a track in EDIT KIT sets GND>SIN's TUNE to -64 instead of 0; leaving the snapshot manager through the KIT shortcut can make later COPY/PASTE/CLEAR act on snapshots; switching POLY mode on or off during playback can mute tracks when MULTI ENV > SUS is 0; MULTI ENV changes do not persist while POLY mode is active; notes in POLY mode get stuck after various actions (changing track, pattern); CLEAR > UNDO SONG ROW does not work; CLEAR SONG ROW does not clear per-track transpose data; PASTE > UNDO TRANSPOSE does not work; muting a track that another track triggers and unmuting it later leaves the trigs that fell into the muted time muted; muting such a track does not mute its active ARP sequence; the playhead is not shown for the first step triggered by SPP.
stock_bugs.trigger: see each item.
stock_bugs.cause: not described in the source.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed in ems-monomachine-firmware (beta).
stock_bugs.test_tip: POLY-mode and mute behaviour on a modded Monomachine should be compared with stock 1.32B.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a custom firmware

stock_bugs.title: The MKII can hang on its own restart after writing a new OS
stock_bugs.device_os: Analog Four MKII, OS 1.56 (the running OS does the update)
stock_bugs.symptom: the unit sits on SUCCESS! REBOOTING, stays on USB, and every MIDI call to it blocks until it leaves USB.
stock_bugs.trigger: a flash that stock 1.56 runs; seen twice in about 30 flashes.
stock_bugs.cause: the restart masks every interrupt and then waits for a serial queue that only those interrupts drain (elkflash's reading). elekloader's reading: 1.56 masks interrupts at `0x4007db24` and then waits in `0x40002766` while bytes are pending behind the panel link's DMA (`0x4133cfc0`) or in the UART queue (`0x4133cfd0`), which only those interrupts drain; core-a4mk2 (0.4+) masks only once nothing is pending, not yet checked on the A4. {elekloader-core-a4}
stock_bugs.workaround: power-cycle by hand; the new OS is already written. Do not reflash, and do not take a screenshot over MIDI.
stock_bugs.test_tip: watch the USB node: units leave USB 16-32 s after the commit; one still there after 45 s has stalled.

stock_bugs.title: Live recording records nothing after a sample arrives by SDS
stock_bugs.symptom: after any sample is received over SDS, live recording records no TRIG key and no knob lock until the machine restarts.
stock_bugs.trigger: one SDS sample transfer, then live recording.
stock_bugs.cause: the RECEIVING SAMPLE screen takes the main screen's objects out of a linked list and puts them back without restoring the list head (head cell at RAM `0x28092c`; unlink `0x213450`, append `0x2134ac`), found by bisecting RAM in the emulator.
stock_bugs.workaround: restart the machine after sending samples, before live recording.
stock_bugs.status: open; seen on the unmodified OS in the emulator, a real unit "very likely" the same but not tried.

stock_bugs.title: A Data API card write takes its length from the host and is bounded only by the card's end
stock_bugs.device_os: Syntakt, OS 1.42 (the same eMMC write and erase code is in Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.11/1.12; whether their Data API sizes a write the same way is not read)
stock_bugs.symptom: none with Elektron Transfer, which sends the slot size. A host that declares a larger size writes upward from the slot through the next slots, the project pool, the COKi state copies (`0x7a000`) and the working project (`0x7e000`) up to the card's end.
stock_bugs.trigger: a Data API write (samples, projects, sounds) whose import header declares more bytes than the slot holds (the u32 at +`0x19`, copied without a compare in `0x4010b4de`).
stock_bugs.cause: the start comes from the path, the size from the host; the block write `0x4010f7f8` checks only the card capacity, and the block erase `0x4010f52a` checks nothing (a count of 0 makes the end sector `sector - 1`).
stock_bugs.workaround: a host client must bound the size to the slot; digikit's card guard hooks both entries and refuses a request outside the stock area `[0, 0x180000)` (emulator-tested).
stock_bugs.test_tip: back up the +Drive card before you test any tool that writes samples or sounds into the stock slots.
stock_bugs.found_by: digikit (read from the code; not reproduced on a unit)
